question: Fed decreases interest rates by 50+ bps after January 2026 meeting?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's January 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for January 27 - 28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their January meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

subquestions.question: Will the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) cut the federal funds target range by at least 25 basis points between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-18?
subquestions.background_information:
The FOMC has been considering rate cuts due to concerns about the labor market and inflation. In the past, a rate cut has been indicated by a decrease in the federal funds target range. The current target range is 4.25%–4.5% (FOMC's statement after its meeting scheduled for July 30, 2025: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomcminutes.htm). A rate cut by at least 25 basis points would be a significant decrease, indicating a potential shift in monetary policy.

Sources:
Federal Reserve. (2025-07-30). FOMC Meeting Minutes. Retrieved from https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomcminutes.htm
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the FOMC's statement after its meeting scheduled for October 29, 2025 (https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm) indicates that the federal funds target range has been cut by at least 25 basis points between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-18.
subquestions.rationale: If the FOMC cuts the federal funds target range by at least 25 basis points, it would indicate a potential shift in monetary policy, which could be an indicator of a future rate cut by 50 basis points or more.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: The FOMC must have cut the federal funds target range by at least 25 basis points between 2025-09-18T00:00:00Z and 2025-10-18T23:59:59Z. Observable evidence: An FOMC statement issued within or directly after a meeting in that window showing a rate reduction ≥25 bps. Key entities: FOMC, federal funds rate. The resolution criteria specifically references the October 29, 2025 FOMC statement as the resolution document, asking whether it indicates a cut occurred between Sep 18 - Oct 18.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'FOMC Federal Reserve interest rate decision September October 2025' (to find rate decisions in the window). Query 2: 'FOMC meeting schedule 2025 federal funds rate cut' (to confirm no meeting in window). Query 3: 'FOMC September 17 2025 rate cut 25 basis points' (to verify the Sep 17 cut date). Query 4: 'FOMC October 29 2025 meeting rate decision' (to verify the next meeting date).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event 1: September 17, 2025 — FOMC cut rates by 25 bps from 4.25%-4.50% to 4.00%-4.25%. REJECTED: This occurred on September 17, 2025, which is one day BEFORE the window start date of September 18, 2025. Candidate event 2: October 29, 2025 — FOMC cut rates by another 25 bps from 4.00%-4.25% to 3.75%-4.00%. REJECTED: This occurred on October 29, 2025, which is after the window end date of October 18, 2025. No FOMC meeting or rate action occurred within the September 18 - October 18, 2025 window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Multiple sources confirm the September 17, 2025 rate cut: [News18](https://www.news18.com/business/economy/us-fed-rate-cut-jerome-powell-fomc-reduces-interest-rates-by-25-bps-first-in-9-months-9579537.html), [Coingape](https://coingape.com/fomc-meeting-fed-makes-first-rate-cut-of-the-year-lowers-rates-by-25-bps/), [ValueWalk](https://www.valuewalk.com/news/fomc-lowers-rates-by-25-basis-points-first-cut-this-year/). The cut was announced on September 17, 2025 — one day before the question's window begins. The October 29, 2025 cut is confirmed by [Yahoo Finance](https://uk.finance.yahoo.com/video/fed-cuts-rates-25-basis-180705296.html) and [Livemint](https://www.livemint.com/market/stock-market-news/us-fed-meeting-jerome-powell-led-fomc-cuts-key-interest-rates-to-3-75-4-00-5-key-highlights-11761770631432.html), but it falls outside the window. Neither cut satisfies the criteria of occurring between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-18.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: September 17, 2025: FOMC cut rates — confirmed exact date from multiple sources. This is OUTSIDE the window (before Sep 18). October 29, 2025: FOMC cut rates — confirmed exact date from multiple sources. This is OUTSIDE the window (after Oct 18). No rate cut with a timestamp within the Sep 18 - Oct 18 window exists.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: There is no qualifying occurrence within the window. The FOMC does not hold unscheduled emergency meetings between these dates based on all available evidence. The FOMC calendar shows scheduled meetings only in September (16-17) and October (28-29), with no meeting scheduled between Sep 18 and Oct 18.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: One article (time.news, Sep 17) suggests the Fed 'left the federal funds target range unchanged at 4.25%-4.5%' on September 17, but this appears to be a preview article published before the decision was announced. All confirmed post-decision articles agree the cut occurred on September 17. The resolution criteria becomes definitively impossible because there was no FOMC meeting within the September 18 - October 18 window, and the FOMC only adjusts the federal funds rate at scheduled meetings (or emergency meetings, none of which occurred here). The condition became definitively impossible once the September 17 meeting concluded without any scheduled meeting within the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. The FOMC cut rates on September 17, 2025 (outside the window — one day before it began) and again on October 29, 2025 (outside the window — 11 days after it closed). No FOMC meeting occurred between September 18 and October 18, 2025, making a rate cut within that window impossible. The condition became definitively impossible when the September 17, 2025 meeting concluded without any further meeting scheduled within the window. Resolution datetime is set to September 17, 2025 (end of day in UTC) when it became definitively impossible for a cut to occur within the window.

subquestions.question: Will the CME FedWatch tool report a probability of at least 70% of a rate cut by 25 basis points at the next FOMC meeting between 2025-09-18 and 2025-10-18?
subquestions.background_information:
The CME FedWatch tool is a widely followed indicator of market expectations for future FOMC meetings. A probability of at least 70% of a rate cut by 25 basis points would indicate a strong market expectation of a rate cut, which could be an indicator of a future rate cut by 50 basis points or more.

All explicitly from CME FedWatch for 25bp cut at October FOMC.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Earliest occurrence in window: September 18, 2025 - articles published on that date citing 87.7%-90% probability of 25bp cut at October FOMC meeting per CME FedWatch. evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The window begins 2025-09-18. Articles from September 18 already show probabilities well above 70% (87.7-90%). The FOMC cut on September 17 itself, and post-cut articles on September 18 show the October FOMC probability already at 87.7%+. This is the first day of the window. evidence.step7_verification: No contradictory evidence found. All sources consistently cite CME FedWatch probabilities well above 70% throughout the entire window. evidence.step8_final_decision: The CME FedWatch tool consistently reported probabilities well above 70% for a 25bp rate cut at the October 28-29 FOMC meeting throughout the entire window from September 18 to October 18, 2025. question: US recession in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes”, if either of the following conditions are met:

1.  The National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) publicly announces that a recession has occurred in the United States, at any point in 2025, with the announcement made by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

2.  The seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly U.S. real GDP from the previous quarter is less than 0.0 for two consecutive quarters between Q4 2024 and Q4 2025 (inclusive), as reported by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). 

Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No". 

Note that advance estimates will be considered. For example, if upon release, the advance estimate for Q2 2025 was negative, and the Q1 2025's most recent, up-to-date estimate was also negative, this market would resolve to "Yes". If on December 31, 2025 the latest estimate for quarterly GDP in Q3 2025 was negative, this market will stay open until the Advance estimate of Q4 2025 is published, at which point it will resolve to "Yes" if Q4 2025 was negative or if the NBER declares a recession by then.

The resolution source will be the official announcements from the NBER and the BEA’s estimate of seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly US real GDP from previous quarters as released by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product

subquestions.question: Will the seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly U.S. real GDP be negative for the third quarter of 2025?
subquestions.background_information: The recent trend of economic growth has been uncertain, with the GDP growth rate revised up to 3.3% in the second quarter and the Q2 upturn being largely due to a decline in imports and an acceleration in consumer spending. However, the possibility of a recession in 2025 remains uncertain. Some economists point to the fact that two quarters of negative GDP growth are commonly perceived as the start of a recession, but this definition is false. The National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) determines the start and end of recessions by month. [1] [2] [3] [4] [5] [6] [7] [8]
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly U.S. real GDP is negative for the third quarter of 2025, as reported by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30 (inclusive). The resolution will be based on the official data released by the BEA's technical note: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product. If the data is delayed or not released, the question will be considered unresolvable.
subquestions.rationale: A negative GDP growth rate in the third quarter of 2025 could be an indicator of a potential recession in 2025, making this question relevant to the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: The BEA must publish an official seasonally adjusted annualized percent change in quarterly U.S. real GDP for Q3 2025 (July-September 2025) that is negative, with that release occurring between September 1-30, 2025. Key structural issue: Q3 2025 ends on September 30, 2025, and the BEA's advance estimate is normally released ~30 days after quarter-end, i.e., in late October 2025, making a September release structurally impossible.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'BEA Bureau of Economic Analysis GDP Q3 2025 third quarter advance estimate release' (Sept 1-30, 2025) — intended to find any Q3 2025 BEA GDP data released in September. Query 2: 'US real GDP third quarter 2025 negative growth recession' (Sept 1-30, 2025) — intended to find evidence of negative Q3 GDP.
evidence.step3_event_detection: No Q3 2025 official BEA GDP release was found in the September 2025 window. The BEA released its THIRD ESTIMATE for Q2 2025 GDP (3.8% growth) on September 25, 2025. All Q3 2025 references are tracking estimates/forecasts (Atlanta Fed GDPNow at 3.9%, economists projecting 1.6%), NOT official BEA releases. One article (Newsweek, Sept 26) explicitly states the advance Q3 2025 GDP estimate is expected October 30, 2025.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event matches the resolution criteria. The BEA released no Q3 2025 GDP data in September 2025. The only BEA GDP release in September 2025 was the Q2 2025 third estimate (3.8%, positive). [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/map-shows-which-states-economies-are-growing-and-shrinking-this-year-10790529) explicitly states: 'The Commerce Department is expected to release its advance estimate for third-quarter GDP on October 30.' No Q3 2025 BEA official data exists within the resolution window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The BEA Q2 2025 third estimate was released September 25, 2025 — this covers Q2, not Q3. No timestamp for a Q3 2025 BEA GDP release exists within the September 1-30, 2025 window because no such release occurred.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: N/A — no qualifying event occurred. The advance estimate for Q3 2025 is scheduled for October 30, 2025, outside the resolution window.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple sources confirm the Q3 2025 advance estimate is expected October 30, 2025 (after the resolution window closes September 30). Q3 2025 tracking estimates show positive growth projections (1.6% to 3.9%), but these are not official BEA releases. No contradictory evidence found — all sources consistently indicate no Q3 2025 official BEA data was released in September 2025. The resolution criteria requires data 'released by the BEA' between Sept 1-30, and that data did not exist in that window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question is unresolvable. The resolution criteria require the BEA to release Q3 2025 GDP data between September 1-30, 2025. However, Q3 2025 doesn't end until September 30, 2025, and the BEA's advance estimate is scheduled for October 30, 2025 — well outside the resolution window. No Q3 2025 official BEA GDP data was released in September 2025. The resolution criteria explicitly state: 'If the data is delayed or not released, the question will be considered unresolvable.' Since the data was not released in the specified window (and structurally could not be), the question is unresolvable.

question: US x Venezuela military engagement by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela between August 21, and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Venezuelan military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count toward a "Yes" resolution; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not. 

Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory will qualify for a “Yes” resolution.

Missiles or drone strikes which are intercepted will not qualify regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage. Similarly, surface-to-air missile strikes impacting adversarial territory will not qualify for a "Yes" resolution (although surface to air missiles fired at an adversarial military aircraft would qualify).

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; Venezuela’s Milicia Nacional Bolivariana (militia) is a “special component” of the Venezuelan National Bolivarian Armed Forces (FANB); and Venezuela’s Coast Guard (Comando de Guardacostas) is a component of the Venezuelan Navy (Armada Bolivariana) and thus part of the FANB.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-10-07 and 2025-11-06, at least 5 additional warships are deployed to the Venezuelan coast, as reported by the U.S. Department of Defense. [10] The resolution will be based on the publicly available ship deployment data from the U.S. Department of Defense's website. [10] Note: The resolution criteria will be based on the specific ships that are deployed, not just the total number of ships. The resolution will be Yes if at least 5 additional warships are deployed, regardless of the type of ships. Sources: [10] - https://www.defense.gov/
subquestions.rationale: The deployment of additional warships to the Venezuelan coast could be an indicator of a potential invasion. If the U.S. is willing to escalate its military presence in the region, it could be a sign that an invasion is imminent.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires: (1) at least 5 additional warships, (2) deployed specifically to the Venezuelan coast, (3) between 2025-10-07 and 2025-11-06, (4) as reported by the U.S. Department of Defense (defense.gov). 'Additional' implies new ships beyond those already in the region before Oct 7. The threshold is 5 ships physically deployed (not just ordered).
evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched: 'US warships deployed Venezuelan coast 2025', 'United States Navy deployment Venezuela 2025', 'Pentagon Department of Defense warships Venezuela deployment count October November 2025', 'USS Gerald Ford carrier strike group five destroyers Caribbean arrive', 'defense.gov warships Venezuela deployment October 2025 additional ships'
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key events identified: (1) Before Oct 7: ~8 US warships already in SOUTHCOM region (Iwo Jima ARG: USS San Antonio, USS Fort Lauderdale; plus destroyers USS Jason Dunham, USS Stockdale, USS Gravely; cruiser; LCS; submarine USS Newport News). (2) Oct 24, 2025: Pentagon announced Ford Carrier Strike Group (USS Gerald R. Ford + 5 destroyers: Bainbridge, Mahan, Winston S. Churchill, Mitscher/Mitchener, Forrest Sherman) ordered to SOUTHCOM region. (3) Oct 26, 2025: USS Gravely arrived in Trinidad and Tobago (near Venezuela). (4) Nov 4-5, 2025: Ford CSG (Ford + Bainbridge) transited Strait of Gibraltar — still en route to Caribbean, had NOT yet arrived at Venezuelan coast before Nov 6. REJECTION: The Ford CSG was ordered within the window but did not physically arrive at the Venezuelan coast before the window closed (Nov 6).
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria explicitly requires deployment 'to the Venezuelan coast' as reported by defense.gov. Multiple sources confirm: (a) The Ford CSG (6 vessels including carrier + 5 destroyers) was ordered Oct 24 ([Aviationist](https://theaviationist.com/2025/10/24/ford-csg-ordered-to-caribbean/), [UPI](https://www.upi.com/Top_News/US/2025/10/24/carrier-strike-group-caribbean/5491761333868/)) but as of Nov 5 was still transiting the Atlantic ([Newsweek Nov 5](https://www.newsweek.com/photos-show-fully-stacked-us-carrier-strike-group-heading-caribbean-10994073), [Indian Express Nov 4](https://indianexpress.com/article/world/uss-gerald-r-ford-aircraft-carrier-caribbean-us-military-buildup-10346354/)). (b) Per Indian Express Nov 4: only Ford + Bainbridge had crossed Gibraltar; two destroyers (Churchill, Mahan) were in Mediterranean/Spain; two others (Forrest Sherman, Mitchener) were in Red Sea. (c) The 8 pre-existing ships were deployed before Oct 7 (since August 2025). (d) Additional ambiguity: resolution criteria requires ships 'deployed to the Venezuelan coast' — all deployment orders/announcements target the broader SOUTHCOM AOR (Caribbean Sea), not the Venezuelan coast specifically. (e) The resolution source (defense.gov) has not been directly verified to contain the specific deployment data cited in the criteria.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Pentagon announced the Ford CSG deployment order on Oct 24, 2025 — within the window. The Ford CSG transited Gibraltar approximately Nov 4, 2025. No confirmed timestamp of any of the Ford CSG ships physically arriving at the Venezuelan coast within the window (before Nov 6, 2025).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The 8 pre-existing ships were deployed before Oct 7, 2025 (since August 2025), so they don't count as 'additional' within the window. The USS Gravely arrived in Trinidad (near Venezuela) on Oct 26 — this is 1 ship. The Ford + escorts were ordered Oct 24 but had not arrived before Nov 6. No confirmed record of 5+ additional ships physically arriving at the Venezuelan coast within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: The Nov 5 Newsweek article ('Photos show fully stacked US carrier strike group heading to Caribbean') explicitly states the Ford was still 'heading to the Caribbean Sea' and had just crossed the Strait of Gibraltar on approximately Nov 4 — meaning it had NOT arrived at the Venezuelan coast before the Nov 6 deadline. This directly contradicts any claim of physical arrival. Additionally, the resolution criteria specifies defense.gov as the source, but no direct defense.gov data was found in news articles. The broader question of whether 'deployment' means 'ordered' vs 'physically arrived' creates fundamental ambiguity. Furthermore, even if we count ordered deployments, the Ford CSG ships were scattered (some in Red Sea, some in Mediterranean) and not all were heading to Venezuela immediately.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is ambiguous for several reasons: (1) The Ford Carrier Strike Group (6+ vessels) was ordered to the SOUTHCOM region on Oct 24, which is within the window, but physically had not arrived at the Venezuelan coast before Nov 6. (2) The resolution criteria requires ships 'deployed to the Venezuelan coast' — the DoD target area is the broader Caribbean/SOUTHCOM, not specifically the Venezuelan coast. (3) The resolution source (defense.gov) is not directly verified in available evidence. (4) There is genuine ambiguity about whether 'deployed' means 'ordered to deploy' or 'physically present.' Given these multiple ambiguities and the lack of direct, explicit evidence from defense.gov confirming 5+ additional ships physically arrived at the Venezuelan coast within the window, resolution is not definitively determinable.

question: Ukraine signs peace deal with Russia in 2025?

Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”. 

Only Ukraine’s signature is required; Russia’s signature or ratification is not.

Localized, temporary, or issue-specific arrangements—such as airstrike-limitation or deconfliction protocols, humanitarian pauses, evacuation corridors, prisoner-exchange or trade/export arrangements, border/DMZ adjustments, or ceasefires limited to a particular sector/front/municipality—will not qualify.

The document must bear a wet-ink or officially issued electronic signature of an authorized Ukrainian representative. Unsigned agreements (e.g., the 2023 Ohrid arrangement) will not qualify regardless of if they are otherwise officially enacted. 

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

question: Bank of Japan decreases interest rates after January 2026 meeting?
description:
The Statement on Monetary Policy for the Bank of Japan's Monetary Policy meeting for January is scheduled to be released on January 23, 2026 (https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmsche_minu/index.htm).

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the short-term policy interest rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Bank of Japan's January 2026 meeting.

If the short-term policy interest rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official website of the Bank of Japan (https://www.boj.or.jp/en/mopo/mpmsche_minu/index.htm), however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

This market may resolve as soon as the Bank of Japan's statement for their January meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

subquestions.question: Will Donald Trump's net approval rating drop by at least 2 percentage points between September 1 and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
As of August 2025, Trump's net approval rating has been relatively stable, fluctuating between -8.5 and -8.9 percentage points. However, the polling has plateaued at 55% since mid-July, which may indicate a possible drop in his approval rating. According to a Quinnipiac poll, voters are split on which party cares more about their needs, with 33% saying the Democratic Party, 33% saying the Republican Party, and 31% saying neither party. This could have significant implications for the 2026 midterm elections, where turnout is less automatic and media coverage is less saturating. [1] (NYMag, 2025-05-08) [2] (Newsweek, 2025-08-11)

Sources:
* NYMag: https://nymag.com/intelligencer/2025/05/polls-trump-job-approval-stabilizing-but-still-underwater.html
* Newsweek: https://www.newsweek.com/donald-trump-approval-rating-numbers-have-become-very-boring-nate-silver-1712738
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if the average net approval rating for Donald Trump, according to the RealClearPolitics poll aggregator, drops by at least 2 percentage points between September 1 and October 1, 2025. The resolution source will be the RealClearPolitics poll aggregator, specifically the average net approval rating indicated by the green trend line for the resolution date. [3] (RealClearPolitics, https://www.realclearpolitics.com/epolls/latest_polls/)

Sources:
* RealClearPolitics: https://www.realclearpolitics.com/epolls/latest_polls/
subquestions.rationale: A drop in Trump's net approval rating could indicate a decline in his popularity, which may be a sign of a potential drop in his overall approval rating by 2026. This question is relevant to the ultimate question because it asks about a specific event that could be an indicator of the ultimate outcome.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires the RealClearPolitics (RCP) average net approval rating for Trump to drop by at least 2 percentage points between September 1, 2025 and October 1, 2025. 'Net approval' = approval % minus disapproval %. The reference point is the RCP green trend line value on September 1 vs. October 1. A drop of ≥2 pp is required for Yes resolution.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Trump net approval rating RealClearPolitics September October 2025' — to find RCP-specific net approval data. 2) 'Trump approval rating poll average September 2025' — to find broader polling context. 3) 'RealClearPolitics Trump approval average -5.5 -6 September 12 2025' — to find specific RCP data points. 4) 'RealClearPolitics Trump approval October 1 2025 net margin' — to find end-of-period RCP data. 5) 'Trump RealClearPolitics approval average August 29 September 1 2025 margin' — to find start-of-period RCP data.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key RCP-specific data found: (a) Aug. 29, 2025: RCP margin = –5 pp [Yahoo/Economic Times article published Sept. 1, 2025]; (b) Sept. 8, 2025: RCP margin = –6.1 pp [Yahoo article published Sept. 8, 2025]; (c) Sept. 12, 2025: RCP margin = –5.5 pp [Yahoo article published Sept. 14, 2025]; (d) Sept. 16, 2025: RCP approval ~45.9% [Bloomberg/Alternet, Sept. 16]; (e) Sept. 22–23, 2025: RCP aggregate = –6 to –6.5 pp [USA Today article published Sept. 24; Democrat & Chronicle Sept. 23]; (f) Sept. 30, 2025: RCP = 46% approval [Free Republic article]; (g) Oct. 1, 2025: Multiple polls but no specific RCP net number cited — various polls show 40–49% approval ranges.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution requires the RCP 'green trend line' net approval to drop by ≥2 pp from Sept. 1 to Oct. 1, 2025. Available RCP data: ~–5 pp on Aug. 29 (near Sept. 1 baseline), –6.1 on Sept. 8, –5.5 on Sept. 12, –6 to –6.5 on Sept. 22–23, ~–6 on Sept. 30. The starting value on September 1 was approximately –5 pp, and the ending value around October 1 was approximately –6 to –6.5 pp — a decline of roughly 1 to 1.5 percentage points. This does NOT reach the 2 pp threshold. One source [Detroit Free Press, Oct. 1] notes a government shutdown but does not provide a specific RCP net number for Oct. 1. The Democrat & Chronicle article [Sept. 23] lists RCP at '46% favorable and 52% unfavorable' = –6 pp. The Aug. 27 Yahoo article lists RCP at 45.3% approval and 51.5% disapproval = –6.2 pp net. This suggests the Sept. 1 baseline may already have been around –5 to –6 pp, making a 2 pp drop by Oct. 1 unlikely given October data shows similar levels.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The specific RCP net approval value on September 1, 2025 is not explicitly stated; the closest data point is Aug. 29 at approximately –5 pp. For October 1, 2025, no specific RCP net value is directly cited in news articles, though nearby data (late September) shows approximately –6 to –6.5 pp, suggesting a decline of roughly 1–1.5 pp from Sept. 1 to Oct. 1.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No evidence that the 2 pp drop threshold was reached at any point during the window. The RCP net approval moved from approximately –5 pp (Sept. 1) to approximately –6 to –6.5 pp (late September/Oct. 1), a change of about 1–1.5 pp.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independent sources citing RCP data consistently show: (1) starting value near –5 pp around Sept. 1, (2) fluctuation between –5.5 and –6.5 pp through September, (3) ending value around –6 pp by late September/Oct. 1. The AP-NORC poll showing a 13-point plummet in net approval refers to a single poll, not the RCP aggregator. The Silver Bulletin average showing ~–8 pp is a different aggregator. The RCP aggregator consistently showed smaller fluctuations (–5 to –6.5 pp range). No article reports a 2+ pp drop in the RCP average during this period.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The RCP net approval moved from approximately –5 pp on September 1 to approximately –6 to –6.5 pp on October 1, a drop of roughly 1 to 1.5 percentage points. This falls short of the 2 pp threshold required for Yes resolution. However, neither the exact September 1 nor October 1 RCP green trend line values are explicitly documented in any article, making the precise calculation uncertain. The closest data (Aug 29 = –5 pp; Sept 22–23 = –6 to –6.5 pp) suggests a change of approximately 1–1.5 pp. Given that we cannot confirm an exact 2 pp drop occurred, and given the evidence consistently shows changes in the 1–1.5 pp range, the resolution should be No. However, since the exact RCP green trend line values for Sept. 1 and Oct. 1 are not explicitly stated, the evidence is not perfectly direct. The resolution is borderline between No and resolvable=false. Given the consistent pattern across multiple data points showing only ~1–1.5 pp change in RCP net approval, I will resolve as No.

question: Will Hamas agree to disarm by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Hamas officially announces it will disarm in the Gaza Strip by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only credible announcements, for example by the widely acknowledged leadership of Hamas, will qualify.

For the purposes of this market, "disarm" refers to a public commitment to relinquish or dismantle its military, whether partially or completely, in the Gaza Strip.

Announcements of partial disarmament (e.g., surrendering a class of weapons or agreeing to disarm in stages or a certain region) will qualify as long as it is part of an acknowledged disarmament process.

Only official announcements will qualify. Informal statements, plans contingent on future conditions, statements of intent without a formal policy directive, or any other statements that do not constitute a formal policy announcement will not be considered.

Primary resolution sources will include official statements from Hamas leadership; however, a wide consensus of credible reporting confirming a policy of disarmament has been instituted will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will Hamas's leader publicly commit to disarmament in the Gaza Strip by December 15, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: The Hamas leadership has been involved in peace talks with Israel, but the organization has consistently rejected full disarmament. However, there is a possibility that Hamas may be open to partial disarmament, which could be a step towards a broader peace agreement. The current number of Hamas fighters in the Gaza Strip is not publicly disclosed, but it is estimated to be in the tens of thousands. The organization's military capabilities are largely based on its use of tunnels and rocket launchers. The Hamas leadership has a history of making public statements about its commitment to resistance, but it has also been involved in secret negotiations with Israel. The current situation is complex, with various factions within Hamas holding differing views on the peace process. (Sources: [1], [8])
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-15, Hamas's leader makes a public statement committing to disarmament in the Gaza Strip. The statement must be made through an official Hamas channel, such as a press release or a public interview. The statement must explicitly mention disarmament and must not be conditional on any future events or actions. The resolution criteria will be based on news articles from reputable sources, such as the New York Times, BBC, or Al Jazeera. (Sources: [1], [8])
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because a public commitment to disarmament by Hamas's leader would be a significant step towards resolving the conflict and addressing the ultimate question of whether Hamas will agree to disarm by December 31.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Hamas's leader must make a public statement between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-15, via an official Hamas channel (press release or public interview), explicitly committing to disarmament in Gaza, without any conditions attached. Key entities: Hamas leader(s); threshold: explicit, unconditional commitment to disarmament; timing: window closes 2025-12-15.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Hamas leader disarmament Gaza 2025' (Nov 30–Dec 15) — to find any public commitments to disarm; Query 2: 'Hamas disarm weapons Gaza statement December 2025' (Nov 30–Dec 15) — to find any official Hamas disarmament statements.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple candidate events found: (1) Khaled Meshaal interview with Al Jazeera (Dec 10–13, 2025) — EXPLICITLY REJECTED disarmament, proposed only a 'weapons freeze'; (2) Khalil al-Hayya statement (Dec 6, 2025) — expressed willingness to hand over weapons ONLY IF Israeli occupation ends — explicitly conditional; (3) Taher al-Nunu (Dec 9, 2025) — stated Hamas weapons will be part of Palestinian state arsenal, rejecting forced disarmament; (4) Khalil al-Hayya televised address (Dec 14, 2025) — asserted weapons are a 'legitimate right'; (5) TASS report (Dec 5, 2025) citing Al Arabiya TV citing unnamed sources about Hamas agreeing to lay down heavy weapons — not an official Hamas channel statement. All candidate events either explicitly reject disarmament or make it conditional.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No statement within the window satisfies all criteria. Meshaal's statements [Al Jazeera, Dec 10-13](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/12/10/hamas-leader-vows-to-curb-gaza-attacks-on-israel-but-rejects-disarmament) explicitly reject disarmament. Al-Hayya's Dec 6 statement [France 24](https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20251206-hamas-says-it-will-hand-over-weapons-to-a-palestinian-authority-if-the-occupation-ends) is explicitly conditional ('if the occupation ends'). The resolution criteria specifically require the commitment to be unconditional. Al-Hayya's Dec 14 statement [Asharq Al-Awsat](https://english.aawsat.com/node/5219245) asserts weapons as a 'legitimate right.' None match the exact criteria.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Multiple exact timestamps exist for Hamas statements rejecting disarmament: Dec 6, Dec 9, Dec 10, Dec 11, Dec 13, Dec 14, 2025. No timestamp exists for an unconditional disarmament commitment.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event (unconditional disarmament commitment) was found anywhere in the window. Therefore, no first-occurrence analysis is needed.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to find any statement that could be interpreted as an unconditional disarmament commitment. The closest was al-Hayya's Dec 6 statement, but multiple reputable sources (France 24, Arab News, Malay Mail) explicitly frame it as conditional on the end of Israeli occupation. The TASS/Al Arabiya report (Dec 5) about unnamed sources is not an official Hamas channel statement and does not satisfy criteria. All evidence consistently shows Hamas rejecting unconditional disarmament throughout the resolution window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence overwhelmingly and consistently shows Hamas leaders rejecting unconditional disarmament throughout the entire resolution window (Nov 30–Dec 15, 2025). Every public statement from Hamas leadership either explicitly rejected disarmament or made any weapons handover conditional on the end of the Israeli occupation. The resolution condition — an explicit, unconditional public commitment to disarmament via an official Hamas channel — was definitively not met. Resolution: No, with the window closing at 2025-12-15T23:59:59Z.

subquestions.question: Will Israel announce a relocation plan for at least 50,000 Palestinians from Gaza to another country between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30?

Key thresholds: formal announcement, specific number ≥50,000, credible source requirement (NYT/BBC/Reuters only), timing window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Israel relocation plan Palestinians Gaza another country 2025' (to find any relocation plan announcements); Query 2: 'Israel Gaza Palestinians forced displacement relocation September 2025' (to find displacement/relocation news in the window); Query 3: 'Israel security cabinet approved plan relocate 50000 Palestinians third countries September 2025' (to find specific approval of 50,000 threshold); Query 4: 'Smotrich voluntary emigration directorate Gaza Palestinians relocation plan September 2025' (to find Smotrich's directorate and formal plan); Query 5: 'Israel NYT BBC Reuters Gaza Palestinians relocation emigration formal announcement September 2025' (to find specifically if NYT/BBC/Reuters reported on a formal announcement); Query 6: 'Israel Gaza voluntary emigration security cabinet approved formal announcement September 2025' (to check if security cabinet formally approved and announced).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Around Sept 11-12, Netanyahu convened internal discussions with defense officials and cabinet ministers about a 'voluntary emigration' plan starting in October — reported by Times of Israel and Channel 12/13, NOT by NYT/BBC/Reuters. (2) Smotrich 'Voluntary Emigration Directorate' — ongoing program, not a new September announcement, and Smotrich expressed skepticism about its viability. (3) Sept 18, Smotrich made 'real estate bonanza' speech at a Tel Aviv conference — this was a proposal, not a formal announcement. Rejection reasons: None of these events constitute a formal Israeli government ANNOUNCEMENT of a plan to relocate ≥50,000 Palestinians; no specific 50,000 figure is mentioned in any of the plans; the credible source requirement (NYT/BBC/Reuters) is not met — sources are Times of Israel, Anadolu Agency, Egypt Today, News18, etc.; the plans discussed had no finalized agreements with receiving countries.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No articles from NYT (nytimes.com), BBC News (bbc.com/news), or Reuters (reuters.com) were found reporting a formal Israeli government announcement of a plan to relocate ≥50,000 Palestinians to another country in the September 2025 window. [News18](https://www.news18.com/videos/israel-s-far-right-finance-minister-suggests-a-real-estate-bonanza-in-gaza-4k-video-n18g-9582215.html) (Sept 18) describes a 'controversial proposal' by Smotrich — not a formal government announcement. [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/israeli-security-officials-propose-gaza-displacement-plan-beginning-in-october-report/3685734) (Sept 12) says officials 'propose' a plan, noting Israeli officials 'remain skeptical about its feasibility.' evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event (formal Israeli government announcement of ≥50,000 Palestinian relocation plan, reported by NYT/BBC/Reuters) with an exact timestamp was found in the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying first occurrence was found — the condition was never met within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple lines of evidence confirm the No resolution: (1) The plans discussed were internal deliberations, not formal public announcements. (2) No specific numerical target of 50,000+ was set in any plan. (3) None of the three required credible sources (NYT, BBC, Reuters) published articles confirming a formal Israeli government announcement of a relocation plan. (4) Smotrich himself — one of the main proponents — expressed skepticism about feasibility and no countries being willing to accept Palestinians, undermining any claim of a formal plan. (6) Saudi Arabia, UAE, Jordan, Egypt, the Arab League all condemned Israeli displacement rhetoric, indicating no consensus or formal arrangement existed. (7) Israel blocked journalist access to Gaza per BBC/AFP/AP/Reuters joint film (Sept 24), further complicating any formal plan implementation.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The condition for Yes was not met during September 2025. While Israel had internal discussions about 'voluntary emigration' plans, there was no formal government announcement of a plan to relocate ≥50,000 Palestinians from Gaza to another country. Moreover, none of the required credible sources (NYT, BBC News, Reuters) reported such an announcement. The resolution window closed without the condition being met. Resolution: No, with resolution_datetime = 2025-09-30T23:59:59Z (the window closed with no qualifying event).

The strict ERO internal data shows ~35,500 over ~5 months = ~7,100/month, far below 62,500. Even using DHS's broad 713,000+ formal deportations over 13 months, that's ~54,800/month — still below 62,500. evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires that Pedro Sánchez face a formal no-confidence vote (moción de censura) in the Spanish Congress of Deputies between October 1-31, 2025. This is a specific constitutional procedure in Spain where the opposition formally files a motion in Congress and a vote is held. It is distinct from Senate committee hearings, budget votes, or arms embargo votes. The key entities are: Pedro Sánchez (PM), the Spanish Congress of Deputies, and a formal no-confidence/censure motion and vote.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Pedro Sánchez no-confidence vote Spanish Congress 2025' (Oct 1-31) — to find any direct evidence of such a vote. 2) 'moción de censura Sánchez Congreso octubre 2025' — Spanish-language query to find official/domestic coverage. 3) 'Spain no-confidence vote motion censure October 2025 Congress' (Sep-Oct) — broader window. 4) 'Sánchez oust vote dismiss Spain parliament October 2025' — alternative phrasing. 5) 'Spain PP Vox motion censure Sánchez government fall October 2025' — looking for opposition action. 6) 'Junts withdraw support Sánchez government collapse Spain 2025' — checking if Junts withdrawal triggered a no-confidence process.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found in October 2025: (a) October 8 — Spanish Parliament voted 178-169 to approve arms embargo on Israel. This is NOT a no-confidence vote. (b) October 30 — Sánchez faced a Senate committee hearing on corruption scandal. This is NOT a no-confidence vote in Congress. (c) October 27-30 — Junts announced withdrawal of support for Sánchez's government. Articles explicitly note this 'does not immediately topple' the government and mention Junts had 'consistently rejected supporting a motion of censure against Sánchez.' (d) No articles mention any formal no-confidence motion being filed or voted upon in the Spanish Congress of Deputies during October 2025. All opposition activity was in the Senate (committee hearing) or through withdrawal of coalition support, not through a formal congressional no-confidence vote.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: None of the events found match the resolution criteria. The arms embargo vote ([Euractiv, Oct 8](https://www.euractiv.com/news/spanish-parliament-backs-sanchezs-arms-embargo-on-israel/)) is a policy vote, not a no-confidence vote. The Senate hearing ([AFP, Oct 30](http://doc.afp.com/82F97CQ)) is a committee hearing, not a no-confidence vote, and occurs in the Senate (not the Congress). The Junts withdrawal ([AFP, Oct 30](http://doc.afp.com/82K89WF)) explicitly states it is 'unlikely to immediately topple' the government, and multiple sources note Junts 'consistently rejected supporting a motion of censure against Sánchez.' Multiple sources (e.g., [Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/Catalan-allies-on-brink-of-withdrawing-support-for-Spanish-government)) note that a no-confidence motion 'would require alliance with the conservative People's Party and far-right Vox — opponents of Catalan self-determination,' implying no such motion was initiated. The article from [cronicadecantabria.com](https://cronicadecantabria.com/cr/puigdemont-cita-este-lunes-a-la-cpula-de-junts-en-perpignan-francia-para-decidir-si-rompen-con-psoe/) explicitly states Junts 'consistently rejected supporting a motion of censure against Sánchez.'

evidence.step7_verification: Verification checks: (1) Multiple reputable sources (AFP, Euractiv, Straits Times, Yahoo News) cover Spanish politics extensively throughout October 2025 without mentioning any no-confidence vote. (2) Articles from October 30 explicitly frame the PP's strategy as pushing for 'early elections' through Senate pressure, not a formal congressional motion. evidence.step8_final_decision: No formal no-confidence vote (moción de censura) was held in the Spanish Congress of Deputies during October 1-31, 2025. The extensive news coverage of Spanish politics in October 2025 confirms the government faced political pressure (Senate hearings, Junts withdrawal), but no formal no-confidence motion was filed or voted upon in Congress. evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: OpenAI must officially announce (on its website, social media, or official blog) a plan to integrate advertisements into ChatGPT, GPT-4, or any successor general-purpose GPT model between 2025-12-06 and 2026-01-05, as reported by a reputable news source. evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'OpenAI ChatGPT advertisements ads integration announcement' (2025-12-06 to 2026-01-05) — to find direct official announcements; Query 2: 'OpenAI advertising revenue model GPT announcement' — to find revenue/monetization official announcements; Query 3: 'OpenAI official announcement ads ChatGPT plan blog post' — to specifically check for blog/official posts; Query 4: 'OpenAI scale back delay advertising plans code red' — to check for contrary evidence of delays.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Dec 7-8: Nick Turley (head of ChatGPT) posted on X denying live ad tests — this is an official denial, not an announcement of ads. (2) OpenAI spokesperson statement 'we're exploring what ads in our product could look like' — vague exploration statement, not an official plan announcement. evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No candidate event exactly satisfies the resolution criteria. The resolution requires an 'official announcement' of a 'plan to integrate advertisements.' Sources uniformly report: [Times of India](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/technology/tech-news/openai-may-soon-show-ads-inside-chatgpt-employees-reportedly-create-mockups/articleshow/126173586.cms) states 'OpenAI has not publicly announced advertising plans'; [Adweek](https://www.adweek.com/media/openai-chatgpt-advertising-android-code-framework/) states 'no official announcement has been made'; [Hans India](https://www.thehansindia.com/technology/tech-news/ads-could-soon-enter-chatgpt-conversations-as-openai-explores-new-revenue-path-1033656) states 'advertising remains in early planning stages with no public testing yet'; [News18](https://www.news18.com/tech/openai-to-start-showing-ads-on-chatgpt-heres-what-the-company-has-said-9756384.html) reports OpenAI's official position is denial of live ad tests; [Activist Post](https://www.activistpost.com/sam-altman-declares-code-red-for-chatgpt-as-rivals-catch-up-will-scale-back-advertising-plans/) reports advertising plans were explicitly delayed/scaled back. evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for a qualifying event because no qualifying event occurred. The closest thing to a statement was a spokesperson's 'exploring' comment (cited in articles around Dec 25, 2025), but this does not meet the criteria of an official plan announcement.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found within the window. Instead, the opposite occurred: OpenAI officially denied ads (Dec 7-8) and officially delayed advertising plans (Dec 11 code red).
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence actively disproves a Yes resolution: (1) Nick Turley's official statement on X: 'There are no live tests for ads' (Dec 7-8, 2025). subquestions.question: Will President Trump make a significant public gesture towards peace in the Russia-Ukraine conflict before 2025-12-01?
subquestions.background_information:
President Trump has claimed to have ended several conflicts, including the India-Pakistan military conflict, through trade measures and tariffs. However, these claims are disputed and have not been independently verified. Trump has also been critical of President Putin's handling of the Russia-Ukraine conflict, stating that it would have never happened if he had been president. This subquestion is relevant to the ultimate question as it could indicate whether Trump's peace efforts are genuine or simply a publicity stunt. If Trump makes a significant public gesture towards peace in the Russia-Ukraine conflict, it could suggest that he is serious about resolving the conflict and may have a positive impact on the ultimate question. 

Sources:
Business Standard - https://www.business-standard.com/article/current-affairs/us-president-donald-trump-claims-to-have-ended-seven-major-wars-116035901900_1.html
Face2Face Africa - https://face2faceafrica.com/article/putin-praises-trumps-peace-efforts-despite-failure-to-win-nobel-prize
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if President Trump makes a significant public gesture towards peace in the Russia-Ukraine conflict, such as a joint statement with President Putin or a public meeting with Ukrainian President Zelenskyy, between 2025-11-11 and 2025-12-01. The gesture must be significant enough to be widely reported by major news outlets and must include a clear call for peace in the Russia-Ukraine conflict. The resolution will be determined by reviewing news articles and official statements from Trump and other world leaders during the specified time period.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is relevant to the ultimate question as it could indicate whether Trump's peace efforts are genuine or simply a publicity stunt. If Trump makes a significant public gesture towards peace in the Russia-Ukraine conflict, it could suggest that he is serious about resolving the conflict and may have a positive impact on the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Trump makes a significant public gesture towards peace in the Russia-Ukraine conflict between 2025-11-11 and 2025-12-01. The resolution criteria lists 'such as' examples: a joint statement with Putin OR a public meeting with Zelenskyy. However, the key criteria is that it be 'significant enough to be widely reported by major news outlets and must include a clear call for peace.' Key entities: Trump, Putin, Zelenskyy. Timing: Nov 11 – Dec 1, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched: (1) 'Trump peace gesture Russia Ukraine conflict November 2025'; (2) 'Trump Putin joint statement meeting November 2025'; (3) 'Trump Zelenskyy meeting public statement peace November 2025'; (4) 'Trump call for peace Ukraine Russia ceasefire significant gesture November 2025'; (5) 'Trump Zelenskyy Mar-a-Lago meeting November 28 29 30 2025'; (6) 'Ukraine peace deal agreement signed ceasefire November 2025'; (7) 'Trump peace announcement Ukraine Russia Thanksgiving November 27 2025'
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Trump approved 28-point peace plan (~Nov 19-20, 2025), widely reported globally by NBC, AP, AFP, NYT, etc. Trump publicly stated 'We think we have a way of getting peace' on Nov 21. (2) Geneva multilateral talks Nov 23-24, with US-Ukraine joint statement on 'refined peace framework.' (3) Trump's Truth Social post Nov 24 saying 'something good just may be happening' re Ukraine peace. (4) Trump Nov 25 statement 'getting very close' to peace deal. (5) Trump dispatched Witkoff to Moscow to meet Putin (Nov 25-26). (6) Trump-Zelenskyy meeting: NOT confirmed within window — explicitly not scheduled as of Nov 25, and Trump was at Mar-a-Lago through Nov 30. (7) US-Ukraine talks in Florida Nov 30 with Rubio/Witkoff/Kushner — Trump did NOT personally meet Zelenskyy. Rejected as qualifying 'joint statement with Putin' or 'public meeting with Zelenskyy': No such events confirmed in window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria says 'such as a joint statement with President Putin or a public meeting with Ukrainian President Zelenskyy' — the word 'such as' indicates these are examples, not exclusive criteria. The overriding criteria is that the gesture be 'significant enough to be widely reported by major news outlets and must include a clear call for peace in the Russia-Ukraine conflict.' Trump's public approval of the 28-point peace plan on ~Nov 20, 2025 ([NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/world/ukraine/trumps-new-peace-plan-unsettles-ukraine-moment-maximum-weakness-rcna244920), [AP](https://apnews.com/article/trump-putin-gaza-ukraine-israel-russia-zelenskyy-c053b2163409a87e7276c427dd493e5d), [France 24](https://www.france24.com/en/video/20251120-us-russia-draft-peace-plan-for-ukraine-sparks-debate)) was massively covered globally. Trump made multiple explicit public calls for peace: 'We think we have a way of getting peace' (Nov 21), 'something good just may be happening' (Nov 24), 'Let's all hope that peace can be accomplished as soon as possible' (Nov 25). The US-Ukraine joint statement from Geneva talks (Nov 24) was also widely reported. These events collectively satisfy the criteria of a 'significant public gesture towards peace' widely reported by major news outlets with a clear call for peace.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Earliest qualifying event: Trump's public approval and statements about the 28-point peace plan, first widely reported on November 20, 2025. Trump's public statements 'We think we have a way of getting peace' date to November 21, 2025 ([PBS](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/watch-with-new-u-s-deal-trump-says-that-zelenskyy-is-going-to-have-to-accept-something), [AP News](https://apnews.com/video/hes-going-to-have-to-approve-it-trump-says-zelenskyy-needs-to-come-to-terms-on-new-us-peace-plan-ff60df1215f64d9695225119ffc67176)). The resolution criteria's listed example events (joint statement with Putin, public meeting with Zelenskyy) did NOT occur in the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The earliest qualifying occurrence appears to be around November 20-21, 2025, with Trump's public endorsement of the peace plan and explicit statements calling for peace. No earlier qualifying events (before Nov 11) are in scope per the start date.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: Some articles note Trump did NOT meet Zelenskyy personally (no Trump-Zelenskyy meeting was scheduled or confirmed in the window), and no joint statement with Putin was issued. However, the resolution criteria uses 'such as' framing, indicating the listed examples are illustrative rather than exhaustive. Trump's 28-point peace plan endorsement and associated public statements clearly constitute a 'significant public gesture towards peace' widely reported by all major global outlets. The plan itself is framed as a peace initiative calling for an end to the Russia-Ukraine conflict. Multiple sources confirm it received saturation coverage by major news outlets globally (NBC, AP, AFP, NY Times, Reuters, Bloomberg, Foreign Policy, France 24, etc.). Counter-argument: One could argue that promoting a controversial plan skewed toward Russia's interests is not a 'genuine' peace gesture. However, the resolution criteria does not require the gesture to be universally accepted as genuine — it requires it to be 'significant' and 'widely reported' with a 'clear call for peace,' which the plan undeniably satisfies.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Trump made a significant public gesture towards peace in the Russia-Ukraine conflict during the specified window. His public approval of the 28-point peace plan (Nov 20, 2025) and related public statements calling for peace were massively covered by all major international news outlets and included explicit calls for ending the Russia-Ukraine conflict. This satisfies the resolution criteria's requirement for 'a significant public gesture towards peace... widely reported by major news outlets... [with] a clear call for peace in the Russia-Ukraine conflict.' The first qualifying occurrence was approximately November 20-21, 2025. Resolution: YES.

question: NATO x Russia military clash in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is a military encounter between the military forces of a NATO country and Russia between September 23 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "military encounter" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between NATO and Russian military forces. Non-violent actions, such as airspace violations, firing of warning shots (such as the June, 2021 Black Sea Confrontations between Russian forces and HMS Defender), or cyberattacks will not qualify.

Interception of missiles or other one-way attack or loitering munitions (e.g. Shahed drones) which are targeting a 3rd party other than the listed countries or their respective forces will not alone qualify. Shooting down UAVs which are not munitions (e.g. MQ-9, Orlan 10, Orion, Bayraktar TB2, etc.) will qualify.

Intentional physical collisions, including aerial interceptions and naval ramming without the direct use of weaponry, such as the 2023 Black Sea incident—where a Russian Su-27 damaged a U.S. MQ-9 Reaper drone's propeller, leading to its crash— will not qualify regardless of damage.

Military contractors will qualify only if confirmed to be operating under the direct command or coordination of the respective state’s armed forces (e.g. the Battle of Khasham would not qualify).

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will there be at least 5 reported incidents of drone incursions into NATO airspace between 2025-09-24 and 2025-10-15?
subquestions.background_information:
In recent years, drone technology has become increasingly advanced, allowing countries to launch drone attacks with greater precision and accuracy. The use of drones in conflicts has been on the rise, and their potential for causing damage and disruption is a major concern. On September 9, 2025, 19 Russian drones entered Polish airspace, prompting a response from NATO forces. This incident highlights the need for effective drone defense systems and the importance of addressing the threat posed by drone technology.

Sources:

[3] 'Attack on Poland: Russia's Debris Still Falling' (2025-09-10, CEPA) - https://cepa.org/attacks-on-poland-russias-debris-still-falling/
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if there are at least 5 reported incidents of drone incursions into NATO airspace between 2025-09-24 and 2025-10-15, as documented by reputable sources such as the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) or the European Defense Agency (EDA). The resolution criteria will be based on the number of reported incidents, rather than the number of drones involved or the level of damage caused.

Sources:
[1] North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) - https://www.nato.int/
[2] European Defense Agency (EDA) - https://www.eda.europa.eu/
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because it addresses the threat posed by drone technology and the potential for drone attacks on NATO countries. If there are multiple incidents of drone incursions into NATO airspace, it may indicate a greater willingness by Russia to engage in aggressive behavior, which could increase the likelihood of a military clash.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: At least 5 reported incidents of drone incursions into NATO airspace between 2025-09-24 and 2025-10-15, documented by reputable sources. Observable evidence: news reports, official NATO/government statements listing drone incursion incidents in NATO member state airspace. Key threshold: 5 incidents (counting by incident, not number of drones). The resolution criteria specifies drone incursions specifically.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'drone incursions NATO airspace 2025' (Sept 24 - Oct 15) - to find general list of incidents. Query 2: 'drone violation NATO territory Europe October 2025' - to find specific incidents in the resolution window. Query 3: 'drone incursion NATO airspace September October 2025 specific incidents list' - for an enumerated list. Query 4: 'Danish airports drone closure Copenhagen Munich drone October 2025' - to confirm specific incidents within window. Query 5: 'drone Norway airspace violation Sweden Belgium September October 2025' - to find additional incidents. Query 6: '39 drone incidents OR drone incursions NATO countries September October 2025 count' - to find aggregate counts.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Confirmed incidents within the window (2025-09-24 to 2025-10-15): (1) Sept 24: Drones over Danish airports Aalborg, Billund, Copenhagen (AmmoLand, multiple sources); (2) Sept 25-26: Drone swarm over Germany Schleswig-Holstein near naval/critical infrastructure (Newsweek/Der Spiegel); (3) Sept 26: Drones near Sweden's Karlskrona naval base (Firstpost, NZ Herald); (4) Sept 27-29: Continued drone sightings over Danish military installations; Oslo Airport closed (Norway's News in English); (5) Sept 28: Drones over French military base Mourmelon-le-Grand (InfoWars/multiple); (6) Oct 2-3: Munich Airport closed due to drone sightings (multiple sources); (7) Oct 3-4: Munich Airport closed again; 15 drones near Belgium's Elsenborn military site (Star/Reuters); (8) Multiple additional incidents in Denmark, Germany, Norway throughout this period. ABC News (Oct 14) explicitly states at least 39 drone-related incidents in up to 12 countries between Sept 9 and Oct 6. The National Interest (Oct 5) states Russian drones violated NATO airspace 'at least five times' just since September 10 - and this count predates most of the Oct incidents.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The criteria require 5 drone incursion incidents specifically (not manned aircraft). Multiple sources confirm this threshold was vastly exceeded. [ABC News](https://abcnews.go.com/International/fresh-russian-incursions-raise-temperature-nato-baltic-sea/story?id=126293095) and [Australian Broadcasting Corporation](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2025-10-15/russias-shadow-drone-war-against-europe-nato-explained/105867182) document at least 39 total incidents Sept 9-Oct 6. The [National Interest](https://nationalinterest.org/blog/buzz/europe-is-learning-to-fear-russian-drones-sa-100525) explicitly notes 'at least five times' just from Sept 10. Within the specific window of Sept 24-Oct 15: (1) Sept 24 Danish airports; (2) Sept 25-26 German Schleswig-Holstein; (3) Sept 26 Swedish Karlskrona naval base; (4) Sept 27-29 Danish military installations/Norwegian airports; (5) Sept 28 French military base; (6) Oct 2-3 Munich Airport; (7) Oct 3-4 Munich (second closure) + Belgium Elsenborn. This clearly surpasses 5 incidents. The European Parliament resolution of Oct 9 [(europarl.europa.eu)](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/news/en/press-room/20251003IPR30664/call-for-a-unified-eu-response-to-russian-violations-and-hybrid-warfare-threats) explicitly condemns drone incursions in multiple NATO member states as confirmed incidents.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The first qualifying incident within the window occurred on 2025-09-24: drones observed over multiple Danish airports (Aalborg, Billund, Copenhagen) on the night of September 24, 2025, per AmmoLand (published 2025-10-07, citing the night of September 24, 2025). The 5th incident threshold was clearly reached by at least September 28-29, 2025, with incidents in Denmark (Sept 24), Germany Schleswig-Holstein (Sept 25-26), Sweden (Sept 26), Norway/Denmark (Sept 27-29), and France (Sept 28). This gives us at least 5 distinct incidents by 2025-09-28T00:00:00Z.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: Russia denied involvement in most incidents. Some individual reports questioned whether certain sightings (e.g., Bavaria) were genuinely drones. Dutch PM noted Oct 7 there was no 'concrete evidence' linking Russia specifically to drone incidents. However, the resolution criteria only requires 'reported incidents of drone incursions into NATO airspace' - not that Russia be confirmed as the actor. Numerous official sources including NATO, national defense ministries, and reputable media confirm at least 5 such reported incidents. The question asks for 'reported incidents,' not 'confirmed Russian-attributed incidents.' The breadth of evidence (39 incidents recorded per ABC, European Parliament condemnation, NATO Eastern Sentry launch, multiple airport closures) makes a No resolution impossible.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence overwhelmingly supports Yes. At least 5 reported drone incursion incidents into NATO member state airspace occurred within the 2025-09-24 to 2025-10-15 window, documented by multiple reputable sources including AP, NATO statements, European Parliament resolutions, national government statements, and major media. The 5th incident threshold was reached by approximately September 28, 2025, with incidents in Denmark (Sept 24), Germany (Sept 25-26), Sweden (Sept 26), Norway/Denmark (Sept 27-29), and France (Sept 28). The total incident count for the window was far higher, with at least 20+ incidents documented. Resolution: Yes.

subquestions.question: Will the European Commission propose new tariffs on steel imports exceeding a reduced quota before 2025-11-15?
subquestions.background_information:
The European Commission has proposed a 50% tariff on steel imports exceeding a reduced quota, cutting the duty-free quota by 47% (Bruegel.org, October 7, 2025) [1]. This move has raised concerns about consistency with decarbonisation goals and may undermine downstream industries (Bruegel.org, October 7, 2025) [1]. The EU claims the proposal complies with GATT Article XXVIII, but this does not justify breaching Free Trade Agreement (FTA) commitments. The plan would apply tariffs to FTA partners, violating their duty-elimination obligations—despite FTAs having bilateral safeguard provisions that do not permit automatic quota application post-safeguard (Bruegel.org, October 7, 2025) [1]. Sources:

Bruegel.org - https://www.bruegel.org/2025/10/the-eu-should-moderate-its-steel-protection-plan/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the European Commission officially proposes new tariffs on steel imports exceeding a reduced quota between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-15, as documented on the European Commission's official website [1]. The resolution criteria will be based on the European Commission's press releases and official documents. The proposed tariffs will be considered 'new' if they differ from the current tariffs in effect. The resolution criteria will be applied to the most recent version of the European Commission's proposed tariffs available on their website.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because a proposal for new tariffs on steel imports could indicate a willingness to impose new tariffs on other goods, including US goods. Additionally, the EU's proposed tariffs on steel imports could be a precursor to more protectionist policies, which could lead to a broader trade war with the US.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: The European Commission must have officially proposed NEW tariffs on steel imports exceeding a reduced quota BETWEEN 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-15. Observable evidence: An official Commission press release or document published in that date range, proposing tariffs different from the current tariffs. Key entities: European Commission, steel imports, tariff quota. The proposal must be 'new' (different from current tariffs) and documented on the EC's official website within the specified window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'European Commission steel import tariffs quota proposal 2025' (Oct 31 - Nov 15) — to find proposals in the window. 2) 'European Commission steel safeguard measures tariffs November 2025' (Oct 31 - Nov 15) — to find November-specific proposals. 3) 'European Commission steel import quota proposal October 7 2025 COM 2025 0726' — to determine exact date of the known proposal. 4) 'European Commission steel safeguard 50% tariff reduced quota proposal official' — to find official announcement details. 5) 'European Commission new steel tariff proposal November 2025 announcement' (Oct 31 - Nov 15) — to check for any new November proposals.
evidence.step3_event_detection: The European Commission officially proposed new tariffs on steel imports exceeding a reduced quota on October 7, 2025 (COM(2025)0726). This was a comprehensive overhaul: 50% tariff on imports exceeding reduced quota (vs. current 25%), and cutting the duty-free quota by 47% from ~34.5 million to 18.3 million metric tons. REJECTED: This event occurred on October 7, 2025, which is BEFORE the resolution window of October 31 – November 15, 2025. No separate new proposal was identified within the resolution window. During the window, news covered reactions, parliamentary questions, and Germany's support for the October 7 proposal — not a new proposal.

Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only finalized daily results from the Polymarket mindshare percentage shown on the Kaito Info Markets page at https://kaito.ai/mindshare-arena/infomarkets, specifically the daily values for Polymarket under 'Historical Data', will be used to resolve this market. The resolution source for this market is the Kaito Info Markets page found at https://kaito.ai/mindshare-arena/infomarkets. If this resolution source is unavailable at check time, this market will remain open until the Kaito Info Markets page comes back online and resolve based on the first check after it becomes available.
