subquestions.question: Will Polymarket's daily active users reach 50,000 on any given day before 2026-01-10?
subquestions.background_information: Polymarket has seen significant growth in 2025, with a 47% increase in the sector's total trading volume to $955 billion. The platform has also experienced explosive growth in daily active users, reaching nearly 58,000 in October 2025. [1] With the platform's continued expansion and regulatory acceptance, it is possible that Polymarket's daily active users could reach 50,000 on any given day before 2026-01-10. [2] However, it is also possible that the platform's user growth could slow down or plateau, making it unlikely to reach this milestone. [3] To determine the relevance of this question to the ultimate question, we must consider the relationship between Polymarket's user growth and its mindshare. If Polymarket's user base grows significantly, it is likely that the platform's mindshare will also increase, making it more likely to reach 80% mindshare by 2026-02-18. [4] On the other hand, if Polymarket's user growth slows down or plateaus, it is unlikely that the platform's mindshare will reach 80% by 2026-02-18. [5] Therefore, the question of whether Polymarket's daily active users will reach 50,000 on any given day before 2026-01-10 is relevant to the ultimate question because it provides insight into the platform's potential for continued growth and increased mindshare.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Polymarket's daily active users reach 50,000 on any given day between 2025-12-21 and 2026-01-10, as reported by the platform's official website [1]. The resolution will be based on the daily active user count at 23:59 UTC each day. If the platform's daily active user count reaches 50,000 on any given day during this period, the question will resolve to Yes. If the platform's daily active user count does not reach 50,000 on any given day during this period, the question will resolve to No.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because it provides insight into Polymarket's potential for continued growth and increased mindshare. If Polymarket's daily active users reach 50,000 on any given day before 2026-01-10, it is likely that the platform's mindshare will also increase, making it more likely to reach 80% mindshare by 2026-02-18.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Polymarket's daily active users must reach exactly 50,000 on any single day between 2025-12-21 and 2026-01-10 (inclusive), as measured at 23:59 UTC, based on data from Polymarket's official website. Key entities: Polymarket platform; key threshold: 50,000 daily active users; timing: any day in the window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Polymarket daily active users 50000 2025' (to find direct confirmation); 2) 'Polymarket user statistics traffic metrics December 2025' (broader search); 3) 'Polymarket daily active users drop decline 2025 statistics' (to find trend data); 4) 'Polymarket user count growth January 2026' (to check for post-window growth); 5) 'Polymarket active users December 2025 January 2026 growth spike' (spike search); 6) 'Polymarket return US users January 2026 traffic users surge' (US relaunch impact); 7) 'Polymarket official website stats daily active users metric 2025 2026' (official data); 8) 'Polymarket Dune analytics active traders daily January 2026' (on-chain data).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key candidate data: (1) The Intercept (Dec 29, 2025) explicitly states Polymarket's daily active users dropped from 100,000 (peak) to 5,000–10,000 as of late December 2025. (2) Cryptopolitan (Nov 7, 2025) noted ~72,000 DAU in October 2025. (3) Cryptopolitan (Nov 12, 2025) noted ~63,000 daily traders in November 2025. (4) No sources from the resolution window (Dec 21–Jan 10) report Polymarket's DAU reaching 50,000. (5) Polymarket returned to US users in January 2026, which could have driven some growth, but no data source reports a spike to 50,000. All sources suggest DAU was well below 50,000 (at 5,000–10,000) during the window. No evidence found of a qualifying event.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires data from Polymarket's official website showing 50,000 daily active users. No official website data was found in any article. The Intercept [https://theintercept.com/2025/12/29/polymarket-kalshi-betting-prediction-cnn-news-media/] reports Polymarket's DAU at 5,000–10,000 as of late December 2025, far below the 50,000 threshold. This source is a third-party news outlet, not Polymarket's official website, meaning the exact resolution criteria (official website data) cannot be directly verified. However, this same evidence strongly suggests the threshold was not reached.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Intercept article (Dec 29, 2025) provides the most direct data point within the window. It states Polymarket's DAU dropped to 5,000–10,000 (no exact timestamp for the user count measurement). The Cryptopolitan article from Nov 12, 2025 states Polymarket had ~63,000 daily active traders in November 2025. No data with an exact timestamp showing 50,000+ DAU during the resolution window was found.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (DAU ≥ 50,000) was found during the window. All evidence points to DAU being well below 50,000 (5,000–10,000) during this period. The trend before the window shows DAU falling from ~72,000 in October 2025 to ~5,000–10,000 by late December 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: (1) The Cryptopolitan Nov 2025 article mentions 63,000 daily active traders, but this was before the window (November, not December-January). (2) Polymarket returned to US users in January 2026, which could have driven growth, but no source reports DAU reaching 50,000. (3) The Polygon activity report from Jan 9, 2026 reports 1.4 million daily active users on Polygon chain, but this is the entire Polygon chain, not Polymarket specifically. (4) The Cryptopolitan Dec 24 article mentions 419,309 'active users' for Polymarket, but this is a cumulative/monthly count, not daily. The most relevant data within the window (The Intercept, Dec 29, 2025) explicitly states Polymarket's DAU was 5,000–10,000, far below 50,000. No evidence of a qualifying event exists. Also critically, the resolution criteria requires data from 'the platform's official website,' which was not directly accessible or reported in news articles during this period.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence strongly indicates that Polymarket's daily active users did NOT reach 50,000 during the resolution window. The Intercept article from December 29, 2025 (within the window) explicitly states DAU was 5,000–10,000. No news sources or official data report Polymarket reaching 50,000 DAU during this period. However, the resolution criteria specifies the official Polymarket website as the data source, and no such direct official data was found. Despite this, the strong evidence from multiple third-party sources consistently showing DAU well below 50,000 throughout the window, combined with the absence of any contradicting evidence showing a spike to 50,000, supports a No resolution. The question is resolvable because the evidence consistently and explicitly indicates the threshold was not reached during the window, even though it comes from third-party sources rather than the official website.

question: Will Trump try to fire Powell in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump publicly and unequivocally announces that he is removing Jerome Powell as Chair of the Federal Reserve before his term is up, or takes formal action toward doing so, such as issuing a directive or formal request by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Statements which are contingent (e.g. “Powell must step down or raise rates”), statements of intent (e.g.“I am planning to fire Powell”) or other informal statements which are not unequivocal will not qualify.

The resolution source will be official information from Donald Trump however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Trump publicly criticize Jerome Powell or the Federal Reserve by name in a major speech or public appearance before October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: Donald Trump has been critical of Jerome Powell and the Federal Reserve's interest-rate policy. This criticism has been a recurring theme in Trump's public statements and speeches. A recent example is his Truth Social post demanding the removal of Jerome Powell as Chair of the Federal Reserve. [1] However, market participants continue to assign low probabilities to any immediate change in Powell's leadership, perhaps reflecting a belief in the Fed's institutional stability or skepticism about Trump's follow-through. [2] Understanding Trump's behavior and public statements towards Powell and the Federal Reserve is crucial in determining the likelihood of Trump attempting to fire Powell. [3] Sources: [1] Trump Demands Fed Board Remove Chair Jerome Powell, But Polymarket Traders Aren't Buying It (https://finance.yahoo.com/news/trump-demands-fed-board-remove-chair-jerome-powell-but-polymarket-traders-aren-t-buying-it-155644946.html) [2] Markets rattled by 'credible threat' of Trump trying to fire Jerome Powell (https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/breaking-news/money/markets-rattled-by-credible-threat-of-trump-trying-to-fire-jerome-powell) [3] Will Anybody Save Federal Reserve Independence? (https://verdict.justia.com/will-anybody-save-federal-reserve-independence)
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, Trump delivers a major speech or public appearance where he criticizes Jerome Powell or the Federal Reserve by name, and this criticism is reported by a reputable news source such as The New York Times (https://www.nytimes.com/) or CNN (https://www.cnn.com/). The resolution will be based on official transcripts or recordings of Trump's speeches or public appearances, and will be considered final once a reputable news source has confirmed the criticism.
subquestions.rationale: Trump's public criticism of Powell and the Federal Reserve is a key indicator of his intentions towards the Fed Chair. If Trump continues to publicly criticize Powell, it may indicate that he is considering removing Powell as Fed Chair.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Trump delivers a major speech or public appearance between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 criticizing Jerome Powell or the Federal Reserve by name, reported by a reputable news source. Observable evidence: explicit quotes from Trump in speeches, press conferences, social media posts, or other public appearances criticizing Powell/Fed by name, confirmed by reputable news outlet. Key entities: Trump, Jerome Powell, Federal Reserve. Timing: Sept 1 – Oct 1, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Trump criticizes Jerome Powell Federal Reserve September 2025' — to find general reports of criticism; 2) 'Trump Powell Fed criticism speech September 2025' — to find speech-specific reports; 3) 'Trump Powell incompetent too late disaster speech public appearance September 2025' — to find specific quotes; 4) 'Trump Truth Social post Powell Federal Reserve criticism September 2025' — to find social media posts; 5) 'Trump Federal Reserve Powell criticism CNN New York Times September 2025' — to confirm reputable source reporting.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple qualifying events identified: (1) Sept 9 Truth Social post by Trump on Powell/BLS revision — reported by Fortune, CNBC; (2) Sept 10 Trump Truth Social post: 'Powell is a total disaster, who doesn't have a clue!!!' — reported by CNBC, Reuters/Market Screener, Business Standard; (3) Sept 15 Trump Truth Social: 'Too Late MUST CUT INTEREST RATES, NOW' — widely reported; (4) Sept 17 Vanity Fair reports Trump called Powell 'incompetent'; (5) Sept 27-28 Trump posts 'YOU'RE FIRED' cartoon depicting firing Powell — reported by CNBC and Benzinga. All events involve Trump directly criticizing Powell by name in public statements. No events rejected as they all fall within the window and are explicitly reported.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires a 'major speech or public appearance' reported by a reputable source. Trump's Truth Social posts are public statements widely covered by reputable media. The Sept 10 post ('Powell is a total disaster, who doesn't have a clue!!!') was reported by [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/09/09/white-house-biden-powell-trump-jobs-.html) and [Reuters/Market Screener](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/trump-says-fed-chair-powell-should-make-big-rate-cut-now-ce7d59ddd88af025). Vanity Fair (Sept 17) reports Trump 'publicly called Fed Chair Jerome Powell incompetent.' [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2025/09/27/trump-cartoon-firing-powell-fed.html) reported the 'You're Fired' cartoon on Sept 27. These are public criticisms of Powell/Fed by name reported by reputable news sources within the window. The resolution criteria says 'reputable news source such as NYT or CNN' — 'such as' indicates these are examples, not exclusives. CNBC, Reuters, Vanity Fair, Fortune, TIME all qualify as reputable sources.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Earliest qualifying event: September 9, 2025 — Fortune article titled 'Trump's fury at Jerome Powell' published 2025-09-09, reporting Trump's Truth Social post criticizing Powell. September 10, 2025 — CNBC reports Trump's Truth Social post: 'Powell is a total disaster, who doesn't have a clue!!!' The White House press secretary's statement calling Powell 'Too Late' was also published by CNBC on Sept 9. These timestamps are explicit in the articles.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The earliest qualifying event within the Sept 1 – Oct 1 window appears to be September 9, 2025, with the Fortune/CNBC reporting on Trump's criticism of Powell following the BLS revision. No earlier qualifying occurrence within the window was found (window starts Sept 1).
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: No evidence found that Trump praised or refrained from criticizing Powell during this period. Multiple independent reputable sources (CNBC, Fortune, TIME, Vanity Fair, Reuters) confirm Trump's ongoing criticism. The Sept 16 Investing.com article about the Miran appointment notes Trump 'also stated that the Fed needs to maintain its independence' — this is not contradictory as Trump was simultaneously criticizing Powell while nominally supporting Fed independence. The question's resolution criteria mentions 'such as The New York Times or CNN' — while direct NYT/CNN articles were not surfaced in the search results, CNBC (a major news network) and multiple other reputable sources explicitly report the criticism. The criteria uses 'such as' language indicating these are examples.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence clearly shows Trump publicly criticized Jerome Powell and the Federal Reserve by name multiple times between September 1-October 1, 2025, including: Sept 9-10 (Truth Social posts calling Powell 'a total disaster'), Sept 15 (demanding Powell cut rates), Sept 17 (calling Powell 'incompetent'), and Sept 27-28 (posting 'You're Fired' cartoon). These were all reported by reputable news sources including CNBC, Fortune, TIME, Vanity Fair, and Reuters. The first qualifying occurrence was September 9, 2025. Resolution: Yes.

question: Will NVIDIA be the second-largest company in the world by market cap on December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to the second-largest company in the world by market cap on December 31, 2025, as of market close.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will NVIDIA's market capitalization increase by at least 10% between 2025-10-14 and 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information: NVIDIA's market capitalization has been increasing rapidly in recent months, driven by the demand for its AI chips. As of October 2025, NVIDIA's market capitalization stands at over $4 trillion (Source: [1] Retail Drives Nvidia To Become World's First $4 Trillion Market Cap Company, Zero Hedge, 2025-07-09). The company's dominance in the AI GPU market, with a 92% market share, and its strong growth levels, with a projected 65% revenue increase in the first quarter of fiscal 2026, make it a prime candidate to capture a significant share of the growing global GPU market (Source: [5] Prediction: This Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock Will Be Worth $5 Trillion in 3 Years, The Motley Fool, 2025-05-20). However, NVIDIA's market capitalization can fluctuate rapidly due to changes in investor sentiment and market conditions. Therefore, it is essential to monitor NVIDIA's market capitalization closely to understand its trajectory and potential impact on its market value.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if NVIDIA's market capitalization increases by at least 10% between 2025-10-14 and 2025-10-31, according to the data provided by Yahoo Finance (<https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/NVDA/history?p=NVDA>). The resolution will be based on the closing market capitalization values on the last trading day of the resolution window.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because it monitors NVIDIA's market capitalization, which is a key indicator of its market value and potential dominance in the AI chip market. A 10% increase in market capitalization between 2025-10-14 and 2025-10-31 would suggest a strong upward trend, which could be an indicator of NVIDIA's potential to become the second-largest company in the world by market capitalization on December 31, 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition: NVDA market cap increases ≥10% from close on Oct 14, 2025 to close on Oct 31, 2025 (last trading day of window). Since shares outstanding is essentially constant, this is equivalent to stock price increasing ≥10%. Observable evidence: closing price on Oct 14, 2025 and Oct 31, 2025 from financial sources. Key entities: NVIDIA (NVDA), 10% threshold, window Oct 14–Oct 31.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'NVIDIA NVDA stock price market cap October 2025' (general period data); Query 2: 'NVIDIA NVDA stock closing price October 14 2025' (start date); Query 3: 'NVIDIA NVDA stock price close October 31 2025' (end date); Query 4: 'NVIDIA $5 trillion market cap October 29 2025 stock price' (for cross-reference data points).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Oct 14 close: Benzinga/Bloomberg reports $180.01, GuruFocus reports $180.03, Benzinga (different article) mentions $180.82 intraday on Oct 14 — the two close-price sources agree on ~$180.03. (2) Oct 31 close: Yahoo Finance (NVDA Shares Surge 3%) article confirms +2.99% on Oct 31; GuruFocus reports 'rose ~1% to about $205'; Benzinga (TSM article) says 'closing up 1.89%' on Oct 31; Defense World (Oct 31) shows market cap $4.93T; Nov 1 article shows NVDA closed at $202.81 on Nov 1 'down 2.04%', implying Oct 31 close was ~$207.04. The Oct 29 close was confirmed at $207.04 by Business Korea/MarketBeat. The Poolside/Blockonomi articles note '2% drop on October 31' — however this conflicts with the Yahoo Finance '2.99% surge' on Oct 31. Given the Yahoo Finance article is specifically titled about the 3% surge on Oct 31 and is timestamped Oct 31, and the Nov 1 article referencing Nov 1 close of $202.81 (down 2.04% from $207.04), Oct 31 close is most likely ~$207.04.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Oct 14, 2025 close: ~$180.03 [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/3145273/nvidia-nvda-upgraded-by-hsbc-amid-ai-growth-prospects) / ~$180.01 [Benzinga Korea](https://www.benzinga.com/content/48215377/4). Oct 31, 2025 close: ~$207.04 (supported by Business Korea reporting Oct 29 close was $207.04, with +2.99% on Oct 31 according to [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/nvidia-nvda-shares-surge-3-021819769.html), giving ~$213.23... However, [Defense World Oct 31 article](https://www.defenseworld.net/2025/10/31/nvidia-nasdaqnvda-earns-sell-rating-from-seaport-global-securities.html) reports market cap $4.93T which at ~24.3B shares = ~$203/share. Nov 1 article states NVDA closed at $202.81 on Nov 1 'down 2.04%', implying Oct 31 close was $202.81/0.9796 = ~$207.04. Percentage increase: ($207.04 - $180.03) / $180.03 = 15.0% — well above 10% threshold. Even using the lower bound of $180.82 (Oct 14) and $202.81 (which is actually Nov 1 close), the gain from Oct 14 to Oct 31 is at least 12%. The market cap per Defense World on Oct 31 was $4.93T vs ~$4.37T on Oct 15 per GuruFocus — a ~12.8% increase confirming the threshold was exceeded.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Oct 14, 2025 close: multiple sources confirm ~$180.01–$180.03, published Oct 14–15. Oct 31, 2025 close: inferred at ~$207.04 from multiple converging sources (Yahoo Finance Oct 31 article reports +2.99% on Oct 31; prior close Oct 29 confirmed at $207.04; Nov 1 article confirms Nov 1 close of $202.81 = $207.04 × 0.9796). The resolution date is 2025-10-31T23:59:59Z.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The question asks about increase from Oct 14 to Oct 31 close. There is only one relevant comparison: Oct 14 close vs Oct 31 close. No earlier 'first occurrence' check needed as this is a cumulative comparison over the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: Blockonomi and CoinCentral mention '2% drop on October 31' — this appears to describe intraday movement or a different reference period, not the closing change. The Yahoo Finance article explicitly titled 'NVIDIA (NVDA) Shares Surge 3% Today' dated Oct 31 confirms +2.99% close on Oct 31. The GuruFocus article (Oct 31) describes stock 'rising ~1% to about $205' which may be an intraday snapshot. The Defense World market cap of $4.93T on Oct 31 implies ~$203/share — slightly below $207.04 but still 12.75% above $180.03. All estimates of Oct 31 price range from ~$203–$207, each giving >10% gain from ~$180 on Oct 14. No conflicting evidence can bring the Oct 31 close below the ~$198 threshold needed for exactly 10% gain from $180.03.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Oct 14, 2025 close: ~$180.03. Oct 31, 2025 close: ~$203–$207 (multiple converging sources). Percentage increase: minimum ~12.7% using conservative estimates, up to ~15% using higher estimates. This clearly exceeds the 10% threshold. Resolution: Yes.

question: GOP uses 'Nuclear Option' to break filibuster by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the US Senate passes a motion to invoke cloture and end debate on any part of the legislative process, with such a cloture motion receiving Yea votes from fewer than three-fifths of the Senators by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve "No".

Confirmations are considered part of the Senate’s “advice and consent” function, not part of the Senate’s “legislative process,” and will therefore not count towards this market's resolution.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the U.S. government.

subquestions.question: Will Senate Republicans introduce a bill to change the Senate filibuster rules before 2025-11-15?
subquestions.background_information: The Senate filibuster rules have been a point of contention in recent years, with both parties using the 'nuclear option' to change the rules. In 2025, Senate Republicans have been discussing changing the rules to allow a simple majority to pass legislation, rather than the current 60-vote threshold. [1, The Hill, Chip Roy floats nuclear option on Senate filibuster to end shutdown, October 20, 2025, https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/3818500-chip-roy-floats-nuclear-option-on-senate-filibuster-to-end-shutdown/ ] [2, Spectrum News Bay News 9, Shutdown sparks new conversations on 'nuclear option', October 21, 2025, https://www.baynews9.com/content/news/baynews9/news/article.html?content_id=35815638&tkm=rss-35815638 ]
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if a bill is introduced to change the Senate filibuster rules between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-15 (inclusive), as reported by the Senate's official website: https://www.senate.gov/. The bill must be introduced by a Republican senator, as identified by the Senate's official directory: https://www.senate.gov/general/contact_information/senators_cfm.cfm.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because it asks about a specific action that Senate Republicans might take to change the Senate filibuster rules. If Republicans introduce a bill to change the rules, it could be an indicator that they are planning to use the 'nuclear option' to pass legislation, which could ultimately lead to the use of the 'nuclear option' to break the filibuster by December 31.

evidence.step1_decompose: A Republican senator must formally introduce a bill (legislation) to change Senate filibuster rules between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-15, as reported on the Senate's official website. Observable evidence would be a bill number (e.g., S. XXXX) with a Republican sponsor specifically targeting filibuster rule changes. Key distinction: advocacy/endorsement is not the same as formal bill introduction.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Senate Republicans bill filibuster rules change 2025' - to find formal legislation; 2) 'Senate filibuster reform legislation introduced November 2025' - to find any formal introduction; 3) 'Senate bill introduced filibuster rules change legislation November 2025' - to find specific legislation; 4) 'Republican senator introduced bill nuclear option filibuster Senate rules reform' - to find named sponsors of formal bills
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple Republican senators (Tuberville, Hawley, Johnson, Banks, Marshall) publicly endorsed eliminating the filibuster. Trump pressured Republicans at multiple meetings. However, ALL coverage consistently describes these as public statements, advocacy, and political pressure — NOT formal bill introductions. Senate Majority Leader Thune repeatedly stated 'votes aren't there' and no formal legislative action was taken. The government shutdown ended November 11 via a spending bill that overcame the filibuster with 60 votes (8 Democrats joined), demonstrating the filibuster was NOT changed.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article found reports a formal bill being introduced to change the Senate filibuster rules during the window. The Washington Examiner tracked every Republican senator's position on the filibuster (published Nov 6) without mentioning any formal legislation. The Hill reported Thune confirmed 'not enough votes' to invoke nuclear option. The shutdown resolution (Nov 11) used the existing filibuster procedure (60-40 vote), confirming no change was made. All news coverage frames the filibuster debate as advocacy and political pressure, not formal legislative action.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for a qualifying event because no qualifying event (formal bill introduction to change filibuster rules) was found in any source within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found at all, let alone a first occurrence.
evidence.step7_verification: Verification confirms: (1) Multiple sources report Republican senators publicly backed eliminating the filibuster — but this is advocacy, not bill introduction; (2) Senate Majority Leader Thune consistently stated there were 'not enough votes' and opposed changing the filibuster; (3) The government shutdown ended on November 11, 2025 via a 60-40 Senate vote — demonstrating the filibuster remained intact and in use; (4) No bill number or formal legislative action related to filibuster reform appears in any reporting; (5) The only bill referenced by Republicans (Senator Mike Lee's Clean Air Act bill, Senator Collins' Jan. 6 provision) is unrelated to filibuster reform.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence overwhelmingly shows that while there was intense public debate and advocacy among Republican senators about changing the filibuster rules, no Republican senator formally introduced a bill to change the Senate filibuster rules during the window. The debate remained at the level of public statements, political pressure, and advocacy. The government shutdown ended on November 11 through the existing filibuster procedure, confirming no change occurred. Resolution: No.

question: Will the federal government be shut down for 10–29 days in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve according to how many days the U.S. Office of Personnel Management announces that the U.S. federal government is at least partially shut down due to a lapse in appropriations by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM.

Days are counted based on notices checked at 10:00 AM ET each day. If the Office of Personnel Management announces a partial shutdown, this will count; however, announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather will not qualify. 

If there are multiple government shutdowns during the relevant period, this market only applies to the first shutdown, as the market will resolve after the end of the first shutdown. Notices of emergency furloughs or impacted government operations count toward the shutdown days.  

If no shutdown occurs during the period, this market will resolve to "No shutdown".

The resolution source for this market will be the website of the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/).

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Office of Personnel Management announce a pre-October 1, 2025, notice indicating a planned partial shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations?
subquestions.background_information: According to the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) [1], they engage in a coordinated approach with agencies to ensure the safety and security of the federal workforce and the communities in which they reside. In the event of a potential shutdown, they will notify the public through their website and social media channels. Given the current political climate and the looming deadline for the next fiscal year, it is possible that the OPM may announce a planned partial shutdown notice before October 1, 2025. A shutdown would affect all departments and agencies, with essential workers continuing to work without pay until the lapse ends [2].
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-17 and 2025-10-17 (inclusive), the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announces a pre-October 1, 2025, notice on their website [1] indicating a planned partial shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations. The notice should be clearly stated and not related to holiday or weather closures.
subquestions.rationale: The question is relevant to the ultimate question as it assesses the likelihood of a partial shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations, which would be a key factor in determining the outcome of the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: OPM must announce a pre-October 1, 2025 notice on their website (opm.gov) indicating a planned partial shutdown due to appropriations lapse, published between Sept 17-Oct 17, 2025. Observable evidence: Direct reference to OPM website posting, not holiday or weather-related.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'US government shutdown October 2025 appropriations lapse' - to find if shutdown occurred; 2) 'Office of Personnel Management OPM shutdown notice 2025' - to find specific OPM notices; 3) 'OPM website shutdown contingency plan lapse appropriations announcement September October 2025' - to find specific OPM website notice
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) OPM issued layoff guidelines Sept 29 per E&E News; (2) OPM confirmed deferred resignations would proceed Sept 30 per Bloomberg Law; (3) Washington Examiner (Sept 30) reports 'Federal agencies are preparing for a potential government shutdown following guidance from OPM'; (4) Government shutdown did begin Oct 1, 2025. However, none of the articles explicitly confirm a notice posted on OPM's own website (opm.gov) specifically titled as a 'planned partial shutdown notice.'
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The criteria requires a notice specifically 'on their website' indicating a 'planned partial shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations.' While OPM clearly issued guidance and shutdown preparation materials before Oct 1, the searched articles do not provide a direct citation or URL to a specific OPM.gov page with such a notice. The E&E News article from Sept 29 states OPM 'issued new guidelines' but does not confirm a specific website announcement format. Standard OPM shutdown preparation practice involves posting such notices, and multiple articles cite OPM guidance — but none provide the exact URL or direct quote from an OPM.gov announcement.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: OPM guidance was issued September 29, 2025 (E&E News) and September 30, 2025 (Bloomberg Law). These fall within the window. However, no direct URL to opm.gov announcing the planned shutdown was found in news articles.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first qualifying OPM guidance appears to be Sept 29, 2025 (layoff guidelines). Earlier occurrences within the Sept 17 window start date are not referenced.
evidence.step7_verification: The shutdown did occur on Oct 1, 2025 — confirmed by multiple high-quality sources (AP, JD Supra, Fox5DC, Indianapolis Recorder, etc.). OPM did issue pre-shutdown guidance. Standard practice in all previous shutdowns is that OPM posts a notice on their website. The question asks specifically about the OPM website posting. Multiple news sources reference OPM guidance consistent with such a posting, but none directly cite the opm.gov URL for a 'planned partial shutdown notice.' The government shutdown is confirmed; OPM's pre-shutdown guidance is confirmed; the specific website posting format cannot be 100% verified from available articles, but OPM historically always posts such notices as part of normal shutdown procedures, and news sources confirm OPM issued shutdown guidance dated September 29-30.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The U.S. government shutdown did begin October 1, 2025. OPM issued shutdown-related guidance by September 29-30, 2025. Standard OPM practice involves posting shutdown notices on opm.gov. Multiple news sources from within the resolution window cite OPM guidance for the shutdown. The resolution criteria states the notice should be 'clearly stated and not related to holiday or weather closures' — OPM's shutdown guidance clearly met this standard. Given the overwhelming evidence that (1) a shutdown began Oct 1, (2) OPM issued pre-shutdown guidance, and (3) this is consistent with standard OPM practice of posting shutdown notices, and given that the question was created anticipating a possible shutdown notice as a binary outcome, the resolution is Yes.

description:

subquestions.question: Will Taylor Swift have at least 3 songs in the top 10 of the Billboard Hot 100 for the week of October 4, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Based on recent trends, Taylor Swift has consistently had multiple songs in the top 10 of the Billboard Hot 100. With her new album 'The Life of a Showgirl' releasing on October 3, 2025, it is likely that she will have multiple songs in the top 10 for the week of October 4, 2025. According to Billboard, Taylor Swift's album 'The Tortured Poets Department' debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 and produced ten simultaneous Hot 100 top-10 hits [10]. This level of success suggests that she will have a significant presence on the Billboard Hot 100 for the week of October 4, 2025.

Sources:
Billboard - 'Taylor Swift's New Album Makes History On Spotify  --  A Month Before It Drops' (https://www.forbes.com/sites/johnniemacfarlane/2025/09/03/taylor-swifts-new-album-makes-history-on-spotify-a-month-before-it-drops/?sh=40c3b1a56f2c)
[5] KPop Demon Hunters Just Broke Another Big Record, But I Think Taylor Swift Could Stop It From Beating The Next One (https://www.cinemablend.com/news/kpop-demon-hunters-just-broke-another-big-record-but-i-think-taylor-swift-could-stop-it-beating-the-next-one)
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if at least 3 songs by Taylor Swift are in the top 10 of the Billboard Hot 100 for the week of October 4, 2025, as reported on Billboard.com (https://www.billboard.com/). The resolution window will be from October 1, 2025, to October 11, 2025.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because it is an indicator of Taylor Swift's current popularity and her ability to have multiple songs in the top 10 of the Billboard Hot 100. If Taylor Swift has at least 3 songs in the top 10 for the week of October 4, 2025, it suggests that she will have a strong presence on the chart for the week of October 18, 2025, which is the date of the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition: At least 3 Taylor Swift songs must appear in positions 1-10 of the Billboard Hot 100 chart specifically dated 'the week of October 4, 2025,' as reported on Billboard.com between October 1-11, 2025. Observable evidence: Billboard's official chart listing for that dated week showing Taylor Swift songs in top 10 positions. Key entities: Taylor Swift, Billboard Hot 100, top 10 positions, week of October 4, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Billboard Hot 100 top 10 October 4 2025' — to find the specific chart. 2) 'Taylor Swift Billboard Hot 100 October 2025' — to find any Taylor Swift chart presence. 3) 'Billboard Hot 100 chart October 4 2025 Taylor Swift top 10' — to specifically check Taylor Swift presence on that chart. 4) 'Billboard Hot 100 week of October 4 2025 chart dated' — to confirm the specific chart's contents.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Found the Billboard Hot 100 chart dated October 4, 2025 (published September 29, 2025). The top 10 for that chart: No. 1 Golden (HUNTR/X), No. 2 Alex Warren (Ordinary), No. 3 Soda Pop (Saja Boys), No. 4 Morgan and Tate, No. 5 Your Idol, No. 6 Manchild, No. 7 Lose Control, No. 8 Daisies (Bieber), No. 9 Love Me Not. Taylor Swift's album 'The Life of a Showgirl' was released October 3, 2025, which was AFTER the tracking period for the October 4 chart, making it impossible for those songs to appear on that chart. Taylor Swift's songs debuted on the chart dated October 18, 2025 (top 12 positions), not October 4.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Billboard Hot 100 chart dated October 4, 2025 contains NO Taylor Swift songs in the top 10. Source: [Billboard Hot 100 Top 10 Countdown For October 4th, 2025](https://www.billboard.com/video/billboard-hot-100-top-10-countdown-for-october-4th-2025/) published September 29, 2025. The chart shows HUNTR/X, Alex Warren, Saja Boys, Morgan Wallen/Tate McRae, Your Idol, Manchild (Sabrina Carpenter, not Taylor Swift), Lose Control, Daisies (Bieber), and Love Me Not. Taylor Swift's album was released October 3, 2025 — too late to appear on the October 4-dated chart. Taylor Swift's historic top-12 sweep occurred on the chart dated October 18, 2025, which is outside the question's scope.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Billboard Hot 100 chart dated October 4, 2025 was published/updated on Billboard.com on approximately September 29, 2025 (standard Billboard Tuesday update schedule, but this appears to have been published on September 29). This is within the resolution window as the chart is 'the week of October 4, 2025' and was available throughout the October 1-11 resolution window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No Taylor Swift songs appear in the top 10 of the October 4, 2025 chart. There is no earlier qualifying occurrence of Taylor Swift having 3+ songs in the top 10 for this specific chart date. The condition was definitively not met.
evidence.step7_verification: Cross-checked: The Billboard Hot 100 chart dated October 11, 2025 (published October 7, 2025) also shows NO Taylor Swift songs in the top 10 — it shows Golden (HUNTR/X), Ordinary (Alex Warren), Tit for Tat (Tate McRae), What I Want (Morgan Wallen/Tate McRae), Daisies (Bieber), Lose Control, Soda Pop, I Got Better (Morgan Wallen), Love Me Not, Your Idol. Taylor Swift's 12-song sweep of the top 12 only appeared on the chart dated October 18, 2025, confirmed by multiple sources (Billboard, Variety, Deadline, Music Business Worldwide) published October 13, 2025.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The Billboard Hot 100 chart dated 'the week of October 4, 2025' — the specific chart in question — contains zero Taylor Swift songs in the top 10. The condition of at least 3 Taylor Swift songs in the top 10 was definitively NOT met for this chart. Taylor Swift's album was released October 3, 2025, but appeared on the chart dated October 18, 2025, not October 4, 2025. Both the October 4 and October 11 charts (which were available and reported during the October 1-11 resolution window) showed no Taylor Swift songs in their respective top 10s. Resolution: No.

question: Will Michael Jackson be named in newly released Epstein files?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Trump Administration (including any federal court) publicly releases previously unreleased files pertaining to the illegal activities of Jeffrey Epstein which contain any mention of the listed individual between July 16 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only previously unreleased files which contain novel material not previously available to the public will qualify. Documents that are merely re-released, have had redactions removed, repackaged, or newly publicized versions of already available information do not qualify.

Any mention of the listed individual in connection with Jeffrey Epstein will qualify, regardless of if connected to nefarious or illegal activities.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform release at least 10,000 pages of previously unreleased documents related to Jeffrey Epstein between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-17?
subquestions.background_information:
The House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform has previously released thousands of documents related to Jeffrey Epstein. According to an article by Global News, the U.S. government is under legal obligation to release all unclassified documents related to Jeffrey Epstein by December 19, 2025, following the passage and signing of the Epstein Files Transparency Act by Congress and President Donald Trump [1]. This act mandates the Justice Department to make public investigative materials, including FBI reports, witness interview transcripts, photographs, videos, flight logs, travel records, and internal communications [2]. The law prohibits the release of any material containing victims' personally identifiable information, images of child sexual abuse, or depictions of death or injury [2].

Sources:
The Root: Folks Online Are Putting Bets On Who Might Be In The Epstein Files, You Won't Believe Who They're Thinking (https://theroot.com/folks-online-are-putting-bets-on-who-might-be-in-the-2025-11-23)
Global News: The Epstein files: What to know ahead of their release (https://globalnews.ca/news/8272451/epstein-files-release/)
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform releases at least 10,000 pages of previously unreleased documents related to Jeffrey Epstein between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-17, as reported by the official website of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (https://oversight.house.gov/).
subquestions.rationale: If the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform releases at least 10,000 pages of previously unreleased documents related to Jeffrey Epstein between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-17, it suggests that the committee is actively working to release the Epstein files, which could increase the likelihood of Michael Jackson being named in the newly released Epstein files.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: The House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform must release ≥10,000 pages of previously unreleased Epstein documents between 2025-11-30 and 2025-12-17, as reported by oversight.house.gov. Observable evidence: An official post on oversight.house.gov citing a release of ≥10,000 pages in the window. Key threshold: 10,000 pages. Timing: strictly between Nov 30 and Dec 17.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'House Committee Oversight Government Reform Epstein documents released 2025' (to find general releases). 2) 'Epstein files documents pages released Congress December 2025' (to find specific page counts). 3) 'House Oversight Epstein 10000 pages documents released December 2025' (to find threshold-meeting events). 4) 'Epstein documents 23000 pages House Oversight November December 2025' (to clarify timing of large releases). 5) 'Epstein 30000 pages previously unreleased House Oversight December 2025' (to find any large Dec release).
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key events identified: (1) November 12, 2025: Republicans released 20,000-23,000 pages from Epstein's estate — OUTSIDE window (before Nov 30). (2) September 2025: 33,295 pages from Pam Bondi subpoena released — OUTSIDE window. (3) December 3, 2025: Democrats released ~10 photos + 4 videos from Epstein's island — within window but not 10,000 pages. (4) December 4, 2025: ~150 more photos released — within window, not 10,000 pages. (5) December 4/5, 2025: ~5,000 pages from banks received but NOT publicly released (per Wired Dec 10 article). (6) December 12, 2025: 19 photos released from 95,000-photo trove — within window but not 10,000 pages. (7) December 15, 2025: Additional photos — within window but not 10,000 pages. (8) DOJ release mandated by Dec 19, 2025 — outside window. All large page-count releases predated the Nov 30 start of the window. No event within Nov 30–Dec 17 meets the 10,000-page threshold.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution requires ≥10,000 pages of previously unreleased documents within Nov 30–Dec 17, reported by oversight.house.gov. The Wired comprehensive guide ([Wired, Dec 10](https://www.wired.com/story/a-complete-guide-to-the-jeffrey-epstein-document-dumps/)) states that 'as of early December 2025, the committee had not released documents from the Treasury or banks, despite confirming compliance.' The 20,000-page release was November 12 ([HuffPost](https://www.huffpost.com/entry/trump-government-shutdown-elections-live-updates_n_69087d10e4b00afef15f855e/liveblog_6914b8c2e4b0c2898bed5047), [Telegraph](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/us/news/2025/11/12/republicans-release-23000-epstein-files/)). Within the resolution window, only photos/videos were released (Dec 3, 4, 12, 15), far fewer than 10,000 pages. No evidence of a ≥10,000-page release from oversight.house.gov in the Nov 30–Dec 17 window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event (≥10,000 pages released in window) can be assigned an exact timestamp, because no such event occurred in the window. The large document releases all predated Nov 30, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found within the Nov 30–Dec 17, 2025 window.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempts to find any large-scale (≥10,000 page) release within the window: None found. The Wired Dec 10 guide confirms bank documents were NOT publicly released as of early December. The DOJ release under the Epstein Files Transparency Act was scheduled for Dec 19, outside the window. Multiple sources confirm the large November release (20,000–23,000 pages) occurred on November 12. The question is whether any release from the committee itself (not DOJ) of ≥10,000 pages occurred Nov 30–Dec 17 — evidence uniformly shows this did not happen. Republican committee members released the 20,000+ pages in November, and Democrats released photos/videos in December, not large document sets. No contradictory evidence suggesting a 10,000+ page release occurred in the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The condition was not met. All large page-count document releases by the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform occurred before the Nov 30 start date of the resolution window. Within the Nov 30–Dec 17 window, the committee released only photos and videos (a few hundred items), not ≥10,000 pages of previously unreleased documents. The DOJ's large release was scheduled for Dec 19, 2025, which is outside the window. Resolution: No.

question: U.S. Government funding lapse on October 1?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a U.S government funding lapse occurs on October 1, 2025, 12:00 AM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A funding lapse is defined as the President failing to sign the relevant bill(s) extending government funding by September 30, 11:59 PM ET. If a bill extending the funding of the U.S. government is passed and signed by the acting President before October 1, 2025, 12:00 AM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

For this market to resolve to "Yes" any funding lapse will count. If only a portion of the US government is covered by any signed bill(s) extending funding of the US government, and a portion of the US government goes unfunded, this market will still resolve to "Yes".

The primary resolution for this source will be official information from the US government, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will the House of Representatives pass a short-term continuing resolution (CR) to extend current funding levels by September 25, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The House has a history of passing CRs to extend government funding. According to [1], the House passed a bipartisan letter warning of a looming partial government shutdown if a new budget or short-term extension is not passed by September 30. Given the proximity of the deadline, it's likely that the House will consider a CR to avoid a shutdown. However, the current Congress has been known to struggle with passing appropriations bills [8].

Sources:
1. Military Times, 'Another federal shutdown threat looms as Congress heads back to DC' (August 28, 2025) - https://www.militarytimes.com/news/pentagon-congress/2025/08/28/congress-faces-looming-partial-government-shutdown/

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the House of Representatives passes a short-term continuing resolution (CR) to extend current funding levels by September 25, 2025, according to a publicly available record of House votes (e.g. https://clerk.house.gov). Otherwise, this question resolves No.
subquestions.rationale: If the House passes a CR, it suggests that they are working towards a bipartisan solution to avoid a government shutdown, which is a positive indicator for the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition: The U.S. House of Representatives must pass a short-term continuing resolution (CR) to extend current funding levels between September 1, 2025 and September 25, 2025 (inclusive). Observable evidence: A recorded House vote passing such a bill. Key entities: House of Representatives, CR/short-term funding bill. Threshold: House majority vote. Timing: Before or on September 25, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'House of Representatives continuing resolution CR vote September 2025' — to find direct evidence of a House CR vote. Query 2: 'House passes short-term spending bill government funding extension September 2025' — to find news about such legislation passing. Query 3: 'House vote 217-212 continuing resolution September 19 2025 CR passing' — to verify the specific vote and date.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event: On September 19, 2025, the House passed a short-term CR (HR 531) by a vote of 217-212, extending government funding through November 21, 2025. Reported by multiple independent sources: AP News, Breaking Defense, WacoTrib, Anadolu Agency, KSL, HotAir, Talking Points Memo, Military Times, Court House News. No earlier qualifying event detected in the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The event explicitly satisfies all criteria: (1) The House of Representatives passed the bill; (2) It is described as a 'short-term continuing resolution' [Breaking Defense](https://breakingdefense.com/2025/09/house-passes-short-term-continuing-resolution/); (3) It extends current funding levels (FY24 levels, described as 'clean'); (4) The vote occurred on September 19, 2025, which is within the September 1–25, 2025 window; (5) Vote count: 217-212 [AP News](https://apnews.com/article/house-trump-funding-bill-republicans-shutdown-1fea0f79c85ec69b91d9789fbda00834). All criteria met exactly.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: September 19, 2025. All sources explicitly state the House vote occurred on September 19, 2025 (described as 'Friday'). The ISO 8601 date is 2025-09-19. An exact sub-day timestamp is not available, but the date is unambiguously within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying CR vote by the House was found in the September 1–25, 2025 window. All sources point to September 19, 2025 as the date of the House vote. No evidence of a prior CR vote in this window exists.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for contradictory evidence: None found. The Senate subsequently rejected the House-passed bill (voted 44-48 on the same day), but this does not affect the House vote outcome. The question only requires the House to pass the CR, not the Senate. Multiple high-quality sources (AP News, Military Times, Breaking Defense, Court House News) independently confirm the House vote. No conflicting reports on the House vote itself.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The House of Representatives explicitly passed a short-term continuing resolution (HR 531) on September 19, 2025, by a 217-212 vote, extending government funding at current levels through November 21, 2025. This event occurred within the September 1–25, 2025 window and directly satisfies all resolution criteria. Resolution: Yes.

subquestions.question: Will China resume rare earth exports to India by October 15, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: China has imposed restrictions on rare earth exports to India since April 2025, citing national security concerns. The restrictions have severely impacted India's auto and electronics sectors. However, China has signaled its willingness to strengthen dialogue and cooperation with India to maintain global industrial and supply chain stability. India has expressed concerns over the abrupt limitations on fertilizer exports, which impacted Di-Ammonium Phosphate (DAP) availability during the Rabi farming season. China's decision to lift restrictions on rare earth magnets, fertilizers, and tunnel boring machines to India is a significant shift for India's manufacturing and technology sectors. (Sources: [1](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/04/13/business/china-rare-earths-exports.html), [2](https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/india/china-yet-to-resume-rare-earth-exports-to-india-despite-wang-yis-assurance-2025-09-11.html), [3](https://www.republicworld.com/india-news/business/chinas-decision-to-lift-curbs-on-rare-earth-metals-mean-for-india-articleid-168334))
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if China resumes rare earth exports to India on or before October 15, 2025, as confirmed by official information from the government of India or credible sources. (Sources: [4](https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/china-to-lift-ban-on-rare-earth-fertiliser-exports-to-india/article36971216.ece), [5](https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/china-to-lift-ban-on-rare-earth-fertiliser-exports-to-india/article36971216.ece))
subquestions.rationale: China's decision to lift restrictions on rare earth exports to India is a significant indicator of its willingness to ease export restrictions. If China resumes rare earth exports to India, it suggests that China may be more likely to lift its export ban on rare earths in general, which is relevant to the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question asks whether China resumed rare earth exports to India on or before October 15, 2025. This requires explicit confirmation from the Indian Ministry of Commerce and Industry or reputable news sources (The Hindu, Economic Times) that actual shipments of rare earth materials resumed from China to India within the October 1–15, 2025 window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'China rare earth exports India resume 2025' (Oct 1–15) — to find direct confirmation of resumption; 2. 'China rare earth ban India lift October 2025' (Sep 1–Oct 15) — to find diplomatic developments and any lifting of restrictions; 3. 'China India rare earth light heavy magnets export resume SCO summit August 2025' (Aug 1–Oct 15) — to check partial resumptions after diplomatic activity; 4. 'China rare earth India export license approved October 2025' (Oct 1–15) — to find any confirmed licensing/shipment approvals.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (a) August 19, 2025: Wang Yi assured India that export restrictions on rare earth magnets, fertilizers, and tunnel-boring machines would be lifted (Economic Times). (b) After SCO Summit (Aug 31–Sep 1): China reportedly resumed exports of LIGHT rare earth magnets to India — but NOT heavy rare earths. (c) September 10-11, 2025: Reports confirmed that China had NOT yet resumed rare earth exports to India despite Wang Yi's assurance; 'none of our importers of rare earth magnets, including EV manufacturers, has received their supplies from China' (Hindu Businessline/Moneycontrol). (d) October 9, 2025: China tightened export controls further, expanding restrictions on rare earth technologies; India's import licenses for heavy rare earths remain pending; China demanded assurances from India that heavy rare earths would not be re-exported to the US, with India not yet agreeing. (e) October 10, 2025: Multiple sources confirm that heavy rare earth magnet shipments to India remain stalled; India's 50+ import applications remain blocked since April 2025. No reports of full resumption by October 15.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require a full resumption of rare earth exports to India. Evidence from October 9–12, 2025 explicitly states: (1) Heavy rare earth magnet shipments remain stalled [Economic Times, Business Standard, Business Today, Oct 9]; (2) India has not agreed to China's demand for non-re-export guarantees [RT India, Oct 10]; (3) China further tightened export controls on Oct 9, 2025, making resumption even less likely; (4) Over 50 import license applications from Indian companies remain pending [Economic Times, Oct 10]. While light rare earth magnets apparently had some partial resumption after the SCO Summit (Aug-Sep), this was partial and inconsistently reported, and by October 9–10 articles still describe India as having supply disruptions. There is no explicit confirmation of full resumption within the October 1–15 window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp of a resumption event within October 1–15, 2025 was found. The most recent explicit evidence from October 9–12, 2025 states the opposite — exports remain restricted, heavy rare earth licenses pending, and India has not agreed to China's conditions.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying resumption event was found anywhere in the search window. The evidence consistently shows exports did NOT resume (for heavy rare earths) during this period. Some partial light rare earth resumption may have occurred after the SCO Summit in late August/early September, but heavy rare earth exports — which appear to be the primary concern — remained stalled throughout, and Chinese export conditions were actually tightened on October 9, 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence check: The August 19 Economic Times article stated China 'lifted restrictions' on rare earth magnets for India — this could suggest some resumption before October 1. However, subsequent reporting from September 10–11 explicitly contradicts this, stating NO supplies had actually been received by Indian importers. By October 9–10, multiple credible sources (Economic Times, Business Standard, Business Today, RT India) explicitly confirm heavy rare earth exports to India remain stalled and that China is seeking additional guarantees India has not yet provided. China's October 9 tightening of controls across the board further corroborates a No resolution.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence overwhelmingly and explicitly shows that China did NOT resume full rare earth exports to India during the October 1–15, 2025 window. As of October 9–12, 2025 (the most recent evidence in the window), heavy rare earth magnet shipments to India were explicitly confirmed as still suspended, with China demanding additional guarantees India had not agreed to, and China actually expanding export restrictions. The window closed on October 15, 2025, with no evidence of resumption. Resolution: No.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: OpenAI makes an official announcement between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-15 about restructuring its for-profit arm into a PBC that is NOT controlled by its nonprofit division. This FAILS the 'not controlled by its nonprofit division' criteria. No new announcement within Oct 1-15 window. No evidence of any announcement matching the specific criteria (PBC NOT controlled by nonprofit) within the resolution window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The September 11, 2025 announcement is outside the window (before October 1, 2025). No qualifying announcement with an exact timestamp was found within 2025-10-01 to 2025-10-15. The October articles only reference the pre-existing September announcement.

No contradictory evidence exists suggesting a new announcement was made in the Oct 1-15 window where nonprofit loses control.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. The announcement that OpenAI would restructure into a PBC was made on September 11, 2025 - before the question window. Furthermore, that announcement explicitly stated the nonprofit WOULD RETAIN CONTROL, which is the opposite of the resolution criteria ('not controlled by its nonprofit division'). During October 1-15, 2025, no new announcement was made about a different PBC structure where the nonprofit does not control. The window closed with no qualifying event.

question: Will the Fed cut-pause-pause in 2025?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal fund range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings in 2025 (September 16-17, October 28-29, and December 9-10).

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered. 

Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the December meeting by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.background_information:

If Maxwell is in talks with the US Congress, it could indicate that she is more likely to provide testimony in the future.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Maxwell's attorneys must PUBLICLY CONFIRM (not just that Congress reached out or that Maxwell offered conditions) that they are IN TALKS with US Congress to provide testimony, between Oct 1-15, 2025. Observable evidence: a news report from a reputable source quoting or paraphrasing Maxwell's attorneys confirming active, mutual discussions with Congress. Key entities: Maxwell's attorneys (David Oscar Markus), US Congress (House Oversight Committee), confirmation must come from attorney side, not Congressional side.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Maxwell attorneys Congress testimony talks October 2025' - to find attorney confirmation; 2) 'Ghislaine Maxwell Congress testimony October 2025' - broader search; 3) 'Maxwell attorney Markus confirms Congress testimony talks October 2025' - specific attorney confirmation; 4) 'Ghislaine Maxwell attorney publicly confirm congressional testimony negotiations' - exact criteria match.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (a) House Oversight Committee contacted Maxwell's attorneys 'soon after' SCOTUS rejection Oct 7-10 [Washington Examiner, Oct 10]; (b) Maxwell's attorney David Markus wrote July 29 letter outlining conditions for testimony; (c) Forbes Oct 9 article: committee will provide update 'soon' on whether she will appear; (d) The Hill Oct 7: 'a date is being set' per Rep. Garcia, immunity request was rejected; (e) Reports that Maxwell 'previously offered to testify before Congress under conditions of immunity, but her offer was rejected' [TheBlaze, Oct 7]. All of these are rejected as resolution criteria matches because: they show Congress reaching out TO Maxwell, not Maxwell's attorneys confirming ACTIVE talks; they reflect prior conditional offers that were rejected; the situation is still unclear/pending as of Oct 10.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires Maxwell's attorneys to PUBLICLY CONFIRM they are IN TALKS with Congress. The evidence shows: [Washington Examiner](https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/house/3845304/oversight-committee-ghislaine-maxwell-testify/) reports the committee contacted Maxwell to testify, but does not quote Maxwell's attorneys confirming talks. [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/alisondurkee/2025/10/09/will-ghislaine-maxwell-speak-with-congress-supreme-court-rejection-clears-way-for-her-to-testify/) describes the situation as uncertain. [The Hill](https://thehill.com/homenews/house/5543253-garcia-trump-ghislaine-maxwell-pardon/) indicates Maxwell's attorneys' immunity request was rejected, implying talks broke down on conditions. No source shows Maxwell's attorneys publicly confirming active talks with Congress in Oct 1-15.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No exact timestamp found for the specific event of Maxwell's attorneys publicly confirming talks with Congress. The closest events are: SCOTUS rejection Oct 6-7, committee outreach 'soon after' Oct 7 (no attorney response confirmed), Forbes article Oct 9 (still uncertain), Hill article Oct 7 (immunity rejected - suggesting no active talks).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found within or outside the window. The prior July 29 letter from Markus with conditions predates the window and those conditions (immunity) were rejected.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: The Hill (Oct 7) explicitly states Maxwell's attorney had requested immunity in exchange for testimony and 'the committee rejected the request' - this strongly suggests there are NO active talks in progress; the prior conditional offer was rebuffed. The committee is trying to compel testimony via subpoena, not negotiating. No CNN or other major outlet reported Maxwell's attorneys confirming talks. The Forbes article's framing ('Will Maxwell Speak With Congress?') confirms the situation remained unresolved and uncertain through Oct 9.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution criteria requires Maxwell's attorneys to publicly confirm they are IN TALKS with Congress between Oct 1-15, 2025. The evidence shows the opposite dynamic: Congress reached out to compel testimony after SCOTUS rejection, Maxwell's prior immunity conditions were rejected, and as of Oct 9-10 the situation was still uncertain with no confirmed talks from Maxwell's attorney side. The condition for Yes resolution is not met.

subquestions.question: Will the US announce a military operation against Colombia before 2026-02-05?
subquestions.background_information: On January 5, 2026, US President Donald Trump threatened potential military intervention in Colombia if Venezuela's leadership does not cooperate with the US on oil and drug trafficking efforts [8]. This threat suggests a heightened risk of military action against Colombia in the near term. The current state of US-Colombia relations is complex, with Colombia's President Gustavo Petro warning that any US attack on its sovereignty would be a declaration of war [9]. Given the tense situation, it is essential to monitor the US's actions in Colombia.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the US announces a military operation against Colombia between 2026-01-06 and 2026-02-05, as reported by a reputable news source such as Reuters [1] or CNN [2].
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because a US military operation against Colombia could be a precursor to a broader conflict in the region, which could in turn increase the likelihood of a US strike against Venezuela.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: The US must formally announce a military operation directed against Colombia between 2026-01-06 and 2026-02-05. Observable evidence would be an explicit US government announcement (press release, presidential statement, Pentagon briefing) of a military operation targeting Colombia, as reported by a reputable news source. Key entities: US government/military vs. Colombia. The operation must be against Colombia, not in cooperation with Colombia.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'US military operation against Colombia 2026' (Jan 6 - Feb 5) — to find direct evidence; 2) 'United States Colombia military attack announcement' (Jan 6 - Feb 5) — to find formal announcements; 3) 'Trump Colombia military strike invasion announcement 2026' (Jan 15 - Feb 5) — to find any later announcements; 4) 'US military strike operation Colombia drug trafficking ground attack 2026' (Jan 6 - Feb 5) — to find operational details; 5) 'Trump Petro White House meeting February 3 2026 outcome Colombia' (Feb 3-5) — to verify the diplomatic outcome.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Trump's verbal suggestion on ~Jan 4-5, 2026 that a military operation against Colombia 'sounds good' — REJECTED: This is a rhetorical threat/comment, not an announcement of an operation. (2) Colombia-US joint pledge against narco-bosses (Feb 3, 2026) — REJECTED: This is cooperative action WITH Colombia, not against it. (3) Colombia's military strike killing 7 ELN guerrillas (Feb 4, 2026) — REJECTED: This was conducted by Colombian forces with no US troops involved. (4) Trump-Petro White House meeting (Feb 3, 2026) — REJECTED: This was a diplomatic meeting, resulting in cooperation, not an adversarial military operation. (5) US maritime strikes in Caribbean/Pacific — REJECTED: These are against drug trafficking vessels, not against Colombia as a state.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event found that matches the criteria of 'US announces a military operation against Colombia.' All evidence points in the opposite direction: after initial threats in early January 2026, relations rapidly de-escalated through diplomatic channels. By January 7-9, 2026, a phone call between Trump and Petro led to a White House invitation. By February 3, 2026, Petro met Trump in person at the White House in a cooperative meeting. The February 4 military strike was by Colombia's military alone, against ELN guerrillas, with no US troops. Multiple sources confirm the trajectory was toward diplomatic rapprochement, not military confrontation.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event timestamp can be extracted because no qualifying event occurred. The closest event — Trump's verbal suggestion that military action 'sounds good' — predates the resolution window (it occurred around January 4-5, 2026, before the window opens on January 6). Even if it were within the window, it is a rhetorical comment, not a formal announcement of a military operation.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found within the window. Trump's threats predated or were at the very start of the window and were rhetorical in nature. The entire period showed diplomatic de-escalation culminating in a White House meeting on February 3, 2026.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Multiple sources (AFP, Reuters-cited articles, Al Jazeera, Straits Times, Newsweek) consistently confirm that: (1) the US never launched a military operation against Colombia; (2) after early threats, the situation rapidly de-escalated; (3) the February 3 White House meeting marked a diplomatic thaw; (4) the February 4 military operation was Colombia's own against ELN, with no US involvement. There is no contradictory evidence suggesting a US military operation against Colombia was announced.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. No US military operation against Colombia was announced during the resolution window (2026-01-06 to 2026-02-05). Instead, the period was characterized by initial threats (rhetorical, not operational) that quickly gave way to diplomatic rapprochement. By February 3, 2026, Trump and Petro met at the White House in a cooperative context focused on joint anti-drug efforts. The window closed on February 5, 2026, without any qualifying announcement. The resolution_datetime is 2026-02-05T23:59:59Z (end of the window with no qualifying event).
