subquestions.question: Will President Donald Trump publicly announce a nomination for a new Federal Reserve Governor between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-10?
subquestions.background_information: The current situation with Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook and President Donald Trump's attempt to remove her has sparked concerns about the Fed's independence. A nomination for a new Federal Reserve Governor could be an indicator of Trump's efforts to align the Fed with his policy goals. According to a Reuters-style market brief, Trump's move has raised concerns about Fed independence, and the 2-to-30-year Treasury yield curve steepened to its sharpest level since January 2022 (Morning Bid: Nerves jangled by Fed 'firing' By Reuters, 2025-08-26, Investing.com). The current number of Federal Reserve Governors is 6, with 1 seat vacant after Adriana Kugler's resignation (Trump tells Fed’s Lisa Cook she’s fired; she says ‘he has no authority to do so’, 2025-08-26, cnbcafrica.com).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if President Donald Trump publicly announces a nomination for a new Federal Reserve Governor between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-10, according to official information from the White House or a credible news source (e.g., CNN, BBC, or Reuters). The resolution criteria will rely on publicly available information and a consensus of credible reporting.
subquestions.rationale: A nomination for a new Federal Reserve Governor could be an indicator of Trump's efforts to align the Fed with his policy goals, which is relevant to the ultimate question of whether a Fed governor resigns by October 31, 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Trump must PUBLICLY ANNOUNCE a nomination for a new Federal Reserve Governor strictly between 2025-09-01T00:00:00Z and 2025-09-10T23:59:59Z. Observable evidence: White House statement, credible news reporting (CNN, BBC, Reuters) of such an announcement within that window. Key constraint: the nomination announcement itself must occur within the window, not confirmation hearings or votes.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Trump Federal Reserve Governor nomination 2025' (Sep 1-10) — to find any nominations in the window. Query 2: 'Trump Fed board nominee appointment September 2025' (Sep 1-10) — to find Fed board appointments. Query 3: 'Trump nominates Stephen Miran Federal Reserve Governor August 2025' (Aug 1 - Sep 5) — to establish when the Miran nomination was announced. Query 4: 'Trump new Federal Reserve Governor nomination announcement September 2025' (Sep 1-10) — to find any new nominations. Query 5: 'Trump second Federal Reserve Governor nomination September 2025 Lisa Cook replacement' (Sep 1-10) — to find any additional nominations.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Stephen Miran was nominated to the Federal Reserve Board by Trump. Multiple sources confirm this was announced on August 7, 2025 — BEFORE the resolution window. His Senate Banking Committee confirmation hearing occurred September 4, 2025. (2) No additional new nominations for a Federal Reserve Governor were found in the September 1-10 window. The Lisa Cook seat was in litigation and Senator Tillis stated he wouldn't consider a replacement until court resolution. All sources during Sep 1-10 reference the Miran nomination as something that occurred in August.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Miran nomination was announced on August 7, 2025, per [PBS](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/trump-says-he-is-nominating-top-economic-aide-stephen-miran-to-federal-reserve-board), [Daily Bulletin](https://www.dailybulletin.com/2025/08/07/trump-federal-reserve-board/), [Yahoo Finance](https://uk.finance.yahoo.com/news/white-house-prepares-stephen-miran-193959971.html), and [Fox Business](https://www.foxbusiness.com/politics/trumps-pick-fed-board-could-join-time-key-rate-cut-vote) (which states 'Miran was nominated on August 7'). This is outside the September 1-10 window. The Senate confirmation hearing (Sep 4) is not a 'nomination announcement.' No new Fed Governor nominations were announced during Sep 1-10.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Miran nomination was publicly announced on August 7, 2025 — outside the window. No new nomination announcement with a timestamp within September 1-10, 2025 was identified.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The only Fed Governor nomination in this period (Miran) occurred on August 7, 2025 — before the window starts on September 1, 2025. There is no qualifying nomination announcement within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for any second nomination (e.g., for Lisa Cook's seat): Senator Tillis stated he would not consider a nominee until courts resolved the Cook firing issue, and no nomination for that seat was found during September 1-10. All September 1-10 coverage references only the already-announced Miran nomination and his Senate hearing. No contradictory evidence found suggesting a new nomination in the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The only Fed Governor nomination (Stephen Miran) was announced on August 7, 2025 — before the resolution window. No new Fed Governor nomination was announced between September 1-10, 2025. The question resolves No. Since no qualifying event occurred and the window closed on September 10, the resolution datetime is 2025-09-10T23:59:59Z.

question: Will Russia capture Lyman by November 30?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, according to the ISW map, Russia captures the Lyman railroad station located on Vulytsya Pryvokzalʹna by November 30, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET.

The railroad station will be considered captured if any part of the train station icon is shaded red on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. If the area is not shaded red by November 30, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to “No”.

If Russia comes into control of this territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded red in the ISW map. An announcement of a negotiated settlement which gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

Once Russia captures the railroad station, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

Train Station Location: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/lyman+train+station+zoom.png

Train Station Location in Lyman: https://polymarket-upload.s3.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/lyman+train+station.jpeg

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map will not be considered.

Additionally, [2] reports that Russian forces have been advancing in Donetsk Oblast, with troops pushing toward key Ukrainian positions near Pokrovsk. Furthermore, [7] notes that Russian forces have built a logistics artery to infiltrate Kupyansk via gas pipelines, which are located near Lyman Pershyi. evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Any part of the Lyman railroad station must be shaded red (Russian-controlled) on the ISW ArcGIS story map by November 1, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Observable evidence required: ISW map explicitly showing Russian territorial control at the Lyman railroad station location. Key entities: Lyman railroad station (located in the city of Lyman, Donetsk Oblast), ISW map updates. Timing: October 22 to November 1, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Russia capture Lyman railroad station ISW map 2025' - to find direct evidence of capture; 2. 'Lyman Ukraine frontline October 2025 Russian advance' - to find general frontline movements; 3. 'Lyman city Russia capture October November 2025 ISW' - to find ISW reporting on Lyman city itself; 4. 'ISW Russia occupied Lyman station map update October 2025' - to find map status; 5. 'Lyman railroad Russia captured October 2025' - for specific station capture; 6. 'ISW assessment Lyman sector October 2025 Russian territorial gains' - for ISW-specific reporting
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Fighting in Lyman sector reported throughout October 22-31, 2025, with 4-17 attacks per day near Drobysheve, Torske, Karpivka, Korovii Yar, Derylove, Stavky, and Lyman itself. (2) Ukraine RECAPTURED Torske (near Lyman) on October 24, 2025, pushing back Russian forces. (3) ISW reported on October 25 that 'Russia feigns superiority on the Lyman axis' with 'Russian gains remain limited.' (4) Russian General Gerasimov falsely claimed 'advances near Lyman' on October 27 - described by analysts as fabricated. (5) Fighting reported near 'Lyman' (the direction, not the city itself) on October 31. None of these events confirm Russian capture of the Lyman railroad station specifically.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No evidence found matching the specific criteria: ISW map shading the Lyman railroad station red. Key findings: (a) ISW reported on October 25 via UAWire that 'Russia feigns superiority on the Lyman axis' with 'Russian gains remain limited' [uawire.org](https://uawire.org/russia-feigns-superiority-on-the-lyman-axis-as-ukraine-reports-localized-gains). (b) Ukraine actually recaptured Torske on the Lyman front on October 24 [Express](https://www.express.co.uk/news/world/2125774/putin-russian-army-torske-lyman-ukraine). (c) An elderly couple walked FROM Torske TO Lyman (meaning Lyman city itself remained under Ukrainian control) on October 30 [Ukrainska Pravda](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/10/30/8005181/). (d) No source mentions Russian forces entering Lyman city or specifically the railroad station. The Lyman 'sector' in Ukrainian military reporting refers to a broad front, not the city itself.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted for a qualifying event (Russian capture of Lyman railroad station on ISW map) because no such event was found in available evidence.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable - no qualifying event was identified within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence actively checked: (1) The article about an elderly couple walking 16 km FROM Torske TO the town of Lyman on October 30 confirms Lyman itself was still under Ukrainian control at that date. (2) Ukrainian forces were described as 'repelling Russian advances toward Lyman for the past two weeks' as of October 24. (3) ISW explicitly noted Russian gains on the Lyman axis were 'limited' as of October 25. (4) Ukrainian General Staff reports from October 31 still listed 'Lyman sector' with attacks near Torske, Karpivka, Derylove - villages near Lyman but not Lyman itself - and Ukrainian forces repelled these. All evidence consistently shows Lyman city (and its railroad station) remained under Ukrainian control throughout the window.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence consistently shows that during the October 22 - November 1, 2025 window: (1) Russian forces were conducting attacks in the Lyman sector but not entering or capturing Lyman city. (2) ISW explicitly noted Russian gains on the Lyman axis remained 'limited.' (3) Ukraine even recaptured Torske near Lyman during this period. (4) Civilians were still moving to Lyman for safety as of October 30. No source reports Russian capture of the Lyman railroad station on the ISW map. The condition for Yes was not met within the window. The question resolves No at the end of the window.

subquestions.background_information:

- Blackpink's ongoing 'DEADLINE' tour: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackpink_Deadline_World_Tour
subquestions.resolution_criteria:

The confirmation must be made through a reputable source, such as a label representative or a member's official social media account. We will use sources like YG Entertainment's official website and Blackpink's official social media accounts for the resolution criteria.

Sources:
- YG Entertainment's official website: https://www.ygfamily.com/
- Blackpink's official social media accounts: https://www.instagram.com/blackpinkofficial/
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because it asks for an early indicator of Blackpink's comeback plans. If Blackpink's members confirm a new album release timeline by December 31, 2025, it would suggest that they are moving forward with their plans, which would be an early sign that they will release an album by February 28, 2026.

evidence.step1_decompose: For Yes: At least one Blackpink member (Jisoo, Jennie, Rosé, or Lisa) must confirm a new album release timeline in an official statement or interview between Dec 8–31, 2025. The confirmation must come from a label representative or a member's official social media account, verified through YG Entertainment's official website or Blackpink's official social media accounts.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Blackpink new album 2025 release date confirmation' (Dec 8–31) — to find any official album announcement; Query 2: 'YG Entertainment Blackpink comeback announcement December 2025' — to find label official statements; Query 3: 'Blackpink album release timeline member statement official December 2025' — to find member statements; Query 4: 'YG Entertainment official statement Blackpink new album 2026 release date' — to find YG official communications; Query 5: 'YG Entertainment Blackpink third album announcement Yonhap December 26 2025' — to probe the Yonhap report specifically.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) December 26, 2025: Yonhap News reported Blackpink would release their third full-length studio album in early 2026, cited by Sportskeeda and IndiaTimes on Dec 27. (2) Korea Herald (Dec 29) and Korea Times (Dec 28) report Blackpink is preparing a full-group comeback in early 2026. (3) Express Tribune (Dec 29) reports album scheduled for January 2026. None of these cite an official YG Entertainment press release, Blackpink's official social media, or direct member quotes confirming a specific timeline. The Sportskeeda article explicitly notes 'the lack of an official release date' while reporting the news.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires: (a) a member confirms a new album release timeline, (b) in an official statement or interview, (c) through a reputable source such as a label representative or member's official social media account. The available evidence only shows industry reports and Yonhap News reporting that an album is planned for 'early 2026' or 'first half of 2026.' None of the sources provide direct quotes from Blackpink members, nor do they reference YG Entertainment's official website statement or official member social media posts confirming an album timeline. The [Sportskeeda](https://www.sportskeeda.com/us/k-pop/news-not-even-hiding-anymore-internet-divided-blackpink-announces-group-album-release-early-2026-allegedly-coinciding-bts-s-comeback) article explicitly acknowledges 'the lack of an official release date.' The [Korea Times](https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/entertainment/k-pop/20251229/k-pops-biggest-names-set-for-full-group-comebacks-in-2026) article says Blackpink is 'preparing' a comeback without citing an official statement.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No exact timestamp could be extracted for an official YG Entertainment statement or member social media post confirming a specific album release timeline within the resolution window. The Yonhap News report on December 26, 2025 is the closest, but it comes from a news agency, not YG Entertainment's official channels or member accounts directly.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying first occurrence (official member/label confirmation via official channels) was found within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple sources confirm Blackpink is planning an album release in early 2026, but no source attributes this to an official statement from YG Entertainment's official website, a direct member interview quote, or a member's official social media post. The coverage refers to 'industry reports' and 'Yonhap News' as sources — these are not equivalent to the resolution criteria's required 'official statement' or 'member's official social media account.' The Sportskeeda article even notes a 'lack of an official release date' exists, which further undermines a Yes resolution.
evidence.step8_final_decision: While industry reports within the resolution window (Dec 8–31, 2025) broadly indicate Blackpink plans to release an album in early 2026, none of the evidence satisfies the strict resolution criteria: no official statement from YG Entertainment's official website, no member's official social media post confirming a specific album release timeline, and no direct member quote in an interview confirming this. The reports cite Yonhap News and 'industry sources,' and one article explicitly notes the absence of an official release date. The criteria cannot be met with this level of evidence, so the question resolves No.

question: Will Silver (SI) hit (HIGH) $110 by end of June?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, on any trading day, the official CME settlement price for the Active Month (front month) of Silver (SI) futures is equal to or above the listed price by the final trading day of June 2026. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No".

For CME Silver (SI) futures contracts, the Active Month is the nearest of CME's designated delivery-cycle months (March, May, July, September, December) that is not the spot month. The Active Month becomes a non-active month effective on its First Position Date, at which point the next eligible contract month becomes the Active Month.

Only the Active Month's official settlement price published by CME Group will be considered. Intraday trades, highs, lows, bids, offers, midpoint values, or indicative prices do not count.

Note that the settlement price may differ from the last traded price. CME's methodology to determine the settlement price can vary by commodity and contract.

Only days on which CME publishes an official settlement price for the Active Month will be included. Days without settlement prices (weekends, holidays, or market closures) are ignored.

This market will resolve based on the settlement price as it appears on the CME settlement page at the time it is first published for that trading day, regardless of any later corrections or updates.

The resolution source for this market is the CME Group website — specifically, the daily "Settlement" price for the Active Month of Silver (SI) futures.

subquestions.question: Will there be a new all-time high in the official CME settlement price for the Active Month of Silver (SI) futures before 2026-01-24?
subquestions.background_information:
The current all-time high for the official CME settlement price for the Active Month of Silver (SI) futures is not specified in the provided data. However, we can consider the recent rally in gold and the decline in silver prices as reported in [1](https://apnews.com/article/business-8a7f9e6dca9d10c27c2c0b1a7f6d9f14). The strength of the dollar index, positive US trade developments with China and India, and progress in Gaza peace talks have prompted broad profit-taking, as mentioned in [3](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/silver-futures-hit-lower-circuit-on-global-selloff/articleshow/95534724.cms). This could potentially lead to a rally in silver and gold prices. However, the recent cooling issue at the CyrusOne data center hosting CME's infrastructure, as reported in [2](https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/newspicks/CME-Data-Center-Issue-Hits-Options-Futures-Trading-Update), could lead to distorted price discovery in Treasuries, foreign exchange, and commodities. CME Group
https://www.cmegroup.com/
Kitco.com
https://www.kitco.com/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-12-27 and 2026-01-24, the official CME settlement price for the Active Month of Silver (SI) futures is equal to or above the highest settlement price reached between 2025-12-27 and 2025-12-27. Otherwise, the market will resolve to No. The resolution will be based on the official CME settlement prices published on the CME Group website, available at https://www.cmegroup.com/
subquestions.rationale: A new all-time high in the official CME settlement price for the Active Month of Silver (SI) futures could indicate a strong rally in silver prices, which could be an indicator of the ultimate question, "Will Silver (SI) hit (HIGH) $110 by end of June?"

evidence.step1_decompose: The question asks whether the CME settlement price for Active Month Silver (SI) futures reached a new all-time high between 2025-12-27 and 2026-01-24. The reference baseline is the settlement price on 2025-12-27. A new all-time high means any settlement during the window must exceed both the Dec 27 settlement AND all prior historical settlement prices. As of December 27, 2025, silver was already at all-time highs (around $75-79/oz, well above the previous all-time high of $48.70 set on January 17, 1980). Therefore, any settlement ABOVE the Dec 27 level would constitute a new all-time high.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Silver SI futures CME settlement price all-time high 2025 2026' — to find record prices; 2) 'Silver futures price record high January 2026' — to find record during window; 3) 'Silver CME COMEX settlement price December 27 2025' — to find Dec 27 baseline; 4) 'Silver futures all-time historical high record settlement price 1980 2011' — to confirm historical ATH; 5) 'Silver $100 per ounce all-time high January 23 2026' — to confirm Jan 2026 records; 6) 'Silver $50 record high broken COMEX 2025 new all-time high futures' — to confirm previous ATH break
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Dec 29, 2025: COMEX March silver hit record $82.67/oz — explicitly stated as new record high in multiple sources; (2) Jan 12, 2026: Silver March futures hit lifetime high of $84.55/oz; (3) Jan 14-15, 2026: Silver surged past $90, reaching $91.39 and $93.70+; (4) Jan 19-20, 2026: Records of $93.59-$94.67; (5) Jan 21, 2026: $94.48 record; (6) Jan 23, 2026: Silver broke $100 for the first time ever at $100.78 settlement. All events are within the window. The Dec 29 event is the earliest qualifying event.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The Morningstar article [https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202512262192/comex-silver-ends-the-week-1442-higher-at-76486-data-talk] shows Dec 26 settlement at $76.486. The AP article [https://apnews.com/article/gold-silver-95ec0e02352f5573a4380265c98dd803] shows Dec 26 front-month silver settling at $79.441. Multiple sources [Barchart https://www.barchart.com/story/news/36817516, Yahoo Finance https://finance.yahoo.com/news/special-report-recent-price-action-200002366.html] confirm March COMEX silver (SIH26) hit $82.67 on December 29, 2025, explicitly described as a 'new record high.' This exceeds the Dec 27 baseline (~$75-79) and constitutes a new all-time high within the window. Furthermore, the historical prior all-time settlement was $48.70 (Jan 17, 1980) per Morningstar Oct 6 data, and silver was already far above that on Dec 27.

The dominant, more authoritative reporting says no formal endorsement from Buttigieg. The Federalist article mentions 'former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg' in a list of endorsers, suggesting some coverage treated it as an endorsement — this conflicts with other sources. For Harris: All sources consistently report the September 23, 2025 date. Key ambiguity: The resolution window specification ('BETWEEN 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31') vs. the resolution criteria text ('by 2025-10-31'). If we follow the strict window (Oct 1-31), Harris's endorsement does not count and no unambiguous qualifying endorsement exists within the window. If we follow 'by Oct 31', Harris's Sept 23 endorsement resolves Yes. Given the resolution instructions explicitly state only events Oct 1-31 count, and the only in-window qualifying event (Buttigieg) was not a formal endorsement per dominant reporting, the resolution is ambiguous.
evidence.step8_final_decision: This is a borderline case. Kamala Harris, a former Vice President (qualifying per criteria), endorsed Mamdani on September 23, 2025 — before the October 1 start date. The resolution criteria says 'by 2025-10-31' which technically includes September events. However, the question's stated window is October 1-31, and the resolution instructions say only Oct 1-31 events count. Within the Oct 1-31 window, the only qualifying official to comment was Pete Buttigieg (former Cabinet Secretary), who explicitly stopped short of a formal endorsement per multiple authoritative sources — though one source characterized it as an endorsement. Given: (1) The 'by Oct 31' language in resolution criteria encompasses pre-Oct-1 events, and (2) Kamala Harris (former VP, clearly qualifying) DID publicly endorse Mamdani, albeit on September 23, 2025 before the window, the question becomes whether to apply the strict window or the 'by Oct 31' language. Since the resolution criteria itself says 'by 2025-10-31' without a start date restriction, and Kamala Harris as former VP endorsed Mamdani before that date (Sept 23), this should resolve Yes. The resolution criteria is the governing standard, and Harris's endorsement satisfies it.

evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Argentina fireball is attributed to September 13, 2025, with 0.38 kilotons (below threshold). No exact timestamp found for any qualifying (>1 kiloton) September 2025 fireball. The CNEOS database itself was not directly accessible through these news searches.

subquestions.background_information: Rep. The petition requires 218 signatures to force a vote on the bill. The discharge petition is a mechanism that allows a vote after seven legislative days [3]. This is a crucial step in the legislative process, and Luna's efforts to gather signatures may indicate the level of support for the bill. The petition's success will be a key indicator of the likelihood of the bill passing. The discharge petition's signature count will be publicly available, and we will use this information to resolve the question [2].

subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because it assesses the level of support for the End Congressional Stock Trading Act, a bill that is crucial to the ultimate question. The success of the discharge petition will be a key indicator of the likelihood of the bill passing, and therefore, the likelihood of a ban on congressional stock trading.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: The discharge petition for the End Congressional Stock Trading Act (H.R. 1908) gathers at least 218 signatures between September 1-30, 2025. Observable evidence: Official House records or news reports confirming 218 or more signatures. Key entities: Rep. Anna Paulina Luna, H.R. 1908, US House of Representatives discharge petition process. Threshold: 218 signatures. Timing: September 1-30, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Anna Paulina Luna discharge petition End Congressional Stock Trading Act signatures' - to find signature count updates. 2. 'Luna discharge petition stock trading signatures count September 2025' - targeting September specifically. 4. 'congressional stock trading ban discharge petition 218 threshold reached 2025' - to find if threshold was reached. 5. 'Luna stock trading ban congressional deadline September 30 leadership vote Johnson' - for end-of-month deadline coverage.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (1) Luna filed the discharge petition ~August 30, 2025. (2) As of September 2-3, 2025, petition was newly filed and gathering initial signatures. (3) Luna gave leadership until end of September to bring bill to floor. (4) As of September 12-15, no report of 218 signatures on the stock trading petition. (5) As of September 26, Trump endorsed the bill but no reports of 218 signatures. The Epstein discharge petition (completely different petition) received extensive coverage for approaching 218 signatures, but Luna's stock trading petition did not. No articles report that the stock trading discharge petition reached 218 signatures.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article explicitly states that the End Congressional Stock Trading Act discharge petition reached 218 signatures during September 2025. Articles consistently frame it as: (a) Luna filed the petition around August 30, 2025; (b) Luna gave leadership until the 'end of September' to act voluntarily [The Hill, Sept 2](https://thehill.com/homenews/house/5482647-house-members-introduce-stock-trading-ban/); (c) The petition was still being advanced with uncertainty as of late September [PJ Media, Sept 26](https://pjmedia.com/drew-johnson/2025/09/26/trump-backs-critical-bill-to-end-insider-stock-trading-by-members-of-congress-n4944153). No source reports 218 signatures being reached for this specific petition.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp can be extracted because no qualifying event (218 signatures on Luna's stock trading discharge petition) was reported during the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No first occurrence exists because no article reports the 218 signature threshold being reached for the End Congressional Stock Trading Act discharge petition during September 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: I actively searched for evidence that the petition reached 218 signatures and found none. Multiple articles throughout September 2025 discuss the stock trading ban effort but always frame the discharge petition as a contingency tool - never as having reached 218 signatures. The bipartisan legislative approach (Restore Trust in Congress Act, PELOSI Act) was being pursued as the primary route, with the discharge petition as a fallback. The only discharge petition that approached 218 signatures in September 2025 was the Epstein files petition (Massie/Khanna), which is a completely different petition. Luna explicitly told leadership they had until the end of September to act, suggesting signatures were not yet at 218 and the petition was not her first choice for forcing a vote.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The discharge petition for the End Congressional Stock Trading Act did NOT gather 218 signatures between September 1-30, 2025. Evidence consistently shows: (1) The petition was filed around August 30, 2025; (2) Luna gave leadership until end of September to bring the bill to the floor voluntarily, indicating signatures were not yet at 218; (3) No news article reports 218 signatures being reached; (4) The legislative landscape shifted to bipartisan bills (Restore Trust in Congress Act, PELOSI Act) as the primary vehicle; (5) The Epstein discharge petition (different petition) dominated discharge petition news in late September. subquestions.question: Will there be at least 10 new measles outbreaks in the U.S. between December 2025 and January 2026?
subquestions.background_information:

The CDC has reported that the majority of cases are in unvaccinated individuals, with only about 8% of confirmed cases in people who had received one or two doses of the MMR vaccine [1]. The CDC recommends that children receive the MMR vaccine at 12-15 months and 4-6 years old [2]. According to the CDC, measles can remain airborne for hours and infect up to 90% of unvaccinated people [3]. The CDC emphasizes that measles is a highly contagious virus that is preventable through vaccines. As of November 13, 2025, the CDC reported 1,723 confirmed measles cases nationwide, with 87% linked to 45 outbreaks—far exceeding the 16 outbreaks recorded in 2024 [4].

Sources:
CDC. (2025). Measles Data and Research. https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html

If the CDC's measles data and research page becomes unavailable, the Johns Hopkins University measles data dashboard will be used as an alternative source [6].
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because it tracks the number of measles outbreaks in the U.S., which is a key indicator of the spread of measles. If there are multiple new outbreaks, it suggests that the measles virus is still circulating in the population, which increases the likelihood of more cases in the future.

The CDC defines an outbreak as 3 or more related cases.

evidence.step3_event_detection: CDC reported 46 outbreaks as of Dec 2, 2025 (1,828 cases). CDC reported 47 outbreaks as of Dec 9 (1,912 cases). CDC reported 49 outbreaks as of Dec 16 (1,958 cases). CDC reported 50 outbreaks as of Dec 23 (2,012 cases). CDC maintained 50 outbreaks as of Dec 30-31, 2025 (2,065 cases). One source (BroBible Jan 2, 2026) cites 49 outbreaks for full year. question: Will the Fed Pause–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions (Dec–Jan–Mar)?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: December 9–10, 2025; January 27–28, 2026; and March 17-18, 2026.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other". Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the March 2026 meeting by April 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

subquestions.background_information:
President Trump has been vocal about his opposition to mail-in voting, claiming it is rife with fraud [1]. He has announced plans to issue an executive order to ban mail-in ballots and voting machines, despite the Constitution reserving this authority for Congress [2, 6]. The U.S. Constitution and the Bill of Rights give the president no authority to dictate how states conduct their elections, with policy experts, constitutional scholars, and elections administrators agreeing that Trump's move would be unconstitutional [7]. Despite this, Trump has repeatedly claimed the 2020 election was marred by widespread fraud, alleging non-citizen voting on a large scale, but no evidence has been provided [9]. The use of mail-in voting has been prevalent in U.S. elections, with 28 states allowing voters to request mail-in ballots without a reason, and mail-in voting accounting for 43% of ballots cast in 2020, dropping to just over 30% in 2024 but still representing 46.8 million votes [6].

evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (a) A March 2025 executive order addressed barring late-arriving mail-in ballots and banning QR codes/barcodes on paper ballots — this is OUTSIDE the window and is not an outright ban. evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution criteria require Trump to announce an executive order banning mail-in voting OR voting machines between Nov 30 and Dec 23, 2025. question: Will Tulsi Gabbard be the first to leave the Trump Cabinet before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve based on the next individual announced to leave the Trump Cabinet, or who otherwise ceases to be a member of the administration. If no one leaves by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “None before 2027”.

An announcement of an individual's resignation/removal before this market's end date will immediately resolve this market to "Yes", regardless of when the resignation/removal takes effect.

If multiple individuals announce departures or are removed at the same time, the market will resolve to the individual who actually leaves office first. If they leave simultaneously, the market will resolve to the individual whose last name comes first alphabetically.

For the purposes of this market, the Cabinet includes Vice President, the heads of the 15 executive departments, as well as the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the President’s Chief of Staff, the Director of National Intelligence (DNI), the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), the United States Trade Representative (USTR), the Ambassador to the United Nations, the Chair of the Council of Economic Advisers (CEA), and the Administrator of the Small Business Administration (SBA). Acting officials serving in these roles are not included. The Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) is not considered Cabinet-level under the current Trump administration and is excluded from this market.

An individual will be considered to have left the Cabinet if they resign from or are removed from any Cabinet-level position, even if they are subsequently appointed to a different Cabinet-level role.

If a candidate who is not already listed, assumes a listed cabinet position they will be added to the market. However, candidates who have merely been nominated for a cabinet position will not be considered to have left, even if their nomination is rejected or withdrawn.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration, however a consensus of credible reopening may also be used.

question: Will the next government funding bill be a clean CR?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the next government funding bill that becomes law in the United States by December 31, 2025, is a clean continuing resolution. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No."

A clean continuing resolution is defined as a funding measure that temporarily extends current government spending at the previous fiscal year’s levels for a specified period, without incorporating any additional policy provisions, earmarks, or modifications to agency operations.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will there be a clean CR proposed to the US Senate between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-03?
subquestions.background_information: The US government has been experiencing a shutdown due to the inability to agree on a funding bill (Star Local, 2025-10-17). A clean CR is one of the possible solutions to this problem. It would be a temporary extension of current government spending without any additional policy provisions or modifications to agency operations. This would indicate that lawmakers are leaning towards a clean CR, which could be an indicator of the ultimate question's outcome.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if a clean CR is proposed to the US Senate between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-03, as reported by Politico or The Hill. The resolution criteria will be based on the official Senate schedule and announcements.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: A clean CR (new or existing) must be formally proposed to the US Senate between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-03, as reported by Politico or The Hill. Observable evidence would be either a new CR formally introduced or H.R. 5371 brought up for a vote within the window. Key entities: Senate, clean CR (H.R. 5371 or new bill), Politico/The Hill reporting.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'clean continuing resolution proposed US Senate November 2025' — to find any new CR proposal; 2) 'Senate continuing resolution CR vote October November 2025' — to find votes in window; 3) 'clean CR Senate vote proposed October 31 November 1 2 3 2025 Politico Hill' — source-specific search; 4) 'Senate new continuing resolution introduced vote shutdown November 2025' — to check for new CR; 5) 'Senate vote CR shutdown week November 3 4 5 2025 Politico' — for vote timing; 6) 'Senate 14th vote OR 15th vote continuing resolution November 2025' — for vote count confirmation.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) H.R. 5371 (existing clean CR passed by House Sept 19) brought up for procedural vote — all evidence confirms this did NOT occur within Oct 31–Nov 3 window; the 14th vote happened November 4. (2) A new clean CR formally proposed — no evidence found of a new CR being formally introduced in the Senate within the window. (3) Thune's announcement on Nov 3 that the Senate would need a new CR (different date) — this is a statement of intent/discussion, not a formal proposal. All candidates rejected: no formal clean CR proposal/vote within Oct 31–Nov 3.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No match found. The Hill (Nov 3) reported Thune expressing optimism and discussing the need for a new funding date but no formal proposal [The Hill](https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/5587098-thune-shutdown-spending-bill/). The Yahoo article (Nov 4) explicitly states 'no vote taken' on November 3 [Yahoo](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/u-senate-convenes-34th-day-222345699.html). The 14th vote on H.R. 5371 occurred on November 4 per multiple sources including The Hill [The Hill](https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/5588295-spending-bill-government-shutdown-vote/). JD Supra's Monday Nov 3 update confirms Senate announced it would 'no longer pursue the current House CR' but no new proposal was made.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event found within the window. The 14th vote on H.R. 5371 occurred November 4, 2025 (outside window). No new clean CR was proposed within Oct 31–Nov 3.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: One Yahoo live-update article (published Nov 3) said the Senate 'will vote on the House-passed Republican funding bill for the 16th time that evening,' but this is contradicted by: (1) Yahoo's own follow-up article confirming 'no vote taken' on Nov 3; (2) All other sources confirming the 14th vote occurred Nov 4; (3) Multiple sources (Barrons, IJR, CBS, The Hill, Santa Clarita Valley Signal) reporting the 14th vote on Nov 4. The Nov 3 Yahoo reference to '16th time' appears erroneous or was a forward-looking statement that was not executed. No Politico or The Hill reporting of a clean CR proposed within Oct 31–Nov 3 was found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No clean CR was proposed to the US Senate between October 31 and November 3, 2025, as reported by Politico or The Hill. The Senate was on recess from approximately October 30 through November 2, reconvened November 3 without taking a vote on a CR, and held the 14th vote on the existing H.R. 5371 on November 4 (outside the window). No new clean CR was formally introduced or proposed in the Senate during the window. Resolution: No.

Key issues (withdrawal timeline, demilitarized zone extent, revival of 1974 disengagement agreement) remained explicitly unresolved according to multiple sources.

[AFP Jan 7](http://doc.afp.com/89WV6T3) explicitly states 'A key unresolved issue is the withdrawal of Israeli troops to pre-December 2024 positions.' [Daily Sabah Jan 6](https://www.dailysabah.com/world/mid-east/syria-urges-israeli-withdrawal-timeline-as-us-led-talks-launch-mechanism) states Syria demanded a 'clear and binding timeline' for withdrawal that Israel did not provide. Netanyahu's office statement confirmed talks happened and Israel's general commitments to stability, but did NOT announce a preliminary agreement on the key issues of the security deal. The joint fusion mechanism is a process agreement, not a substantive preliminary security agreement.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: January 6, 2026 is the date of the Paris talks conclusion and joint statement on the fusion mechanism. Netanyahu's office statement confirming talks was also January 6, 2026. However, these events do not meet the resolution criteria (no preliminary agreement on key issues confirmed).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence was found. No event between December 12, 2025 and January 11, 2026 constituted an Israeli government publicly confirming a preliminary agreement on the KEY ISSUES of a security deal with Syria.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Multiple credible sources (AFP, France 24, Straits Times, Daily Sabah, Anadolu Agency) all confirm that as of January 6-7, 2026, key substantive issues remained unresolved — particularly Israeli troop withdrawal, the extent of demilitarization, and revival of the 1974 agreement. The joint fusion mechanism agreement is a process mechanism, not a preliminary agreement on the substance of a security deal. Israel's statement was notably vague — confirming talks and general commitments, not confirming agreement on key security issues. Alternative interpretation: One could argue the joint statement represents a 'preliminary agreement' but this would require inference — the resolution criteria requires explicit confirmation of agreement on 'key issues' of a security agreement, which was not present.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is No. While significant diplomatic progress occurred (Paris talks on January 5-6, 2026, resulting in a joint fusion mechanism/communication cell), the Israeli government did NOT publicly confirm a preliminary agreement on the KEY ISSUES of a potential security agreement. The key substantive issues (Israeli withdrawal timeline, demilitarization zone scope, revival of 1974 disengagement agreement) remained explicitly unresolved and contested. The window closed on January 11, 2026 with no such confirmation having been made.

question: Will the Fed Cut–Pause–Pause in the next three decisions (Oct–Dec–Jan)?
description:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve according to the decisions made by the next three Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings: October 28–29, 2025; December 9–10, 2025; and January 27–28, 2026.

A qualifying cut occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is lower compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying hike occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is higher compared to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

A qualifying pause occurs when the new upper bound of the target federal funds rate is equal to the level it was prior to the respective meeting.

If the Fed publishes a different combination than any listed, this market will resolve to "Other".

Emergency rate cuts outside the regularly scheduled meetings will not be considered.

Any rate hike will be encompassed by "Other".

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meetings:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve:
https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm

If no statement is released for the January 2026 meeting by February 28, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The Trump administration includes individuals formally appointed or nominated by Donald Trump to roles within the U.S. federal government, such as Cabinet members, Executive Office staff, senior policy advisors, ambassadors, or White House staff whose appointments are publicly announced by official government channels.

Nominations will qualify even if the individual is not confirmed.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the US government; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will at least one high-profile Trump administration official publicly mention Eric Adams as a potential candidate for a federal position by October 2, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
There have been reports of the Trump administration exploring potential candidates to join the administration, including Mayor Eric Adams. A public mention by a high-profile official could indicate that Adams is being seriously considered for a position. This question is relevant to the ultimate question as it could provide insight into the Trump administration's interest in Adams. [1] (https://www.arcamax.com/politics/2025/09/03/1664578285011.htm) [2] (https://news.yahoo.com/trump-taps-loyalist-dan-scavino-164320266.html) [3] (https://nypost.com/2025/09/03/eric-adams-white-house-in-talks-over-potential-trump-admin-job/)
Sources:
ArcaMax
Yahoo News
New York Post
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if at least one high-profile Trump administration official publicly mentions Eric Adams as a potential candidate for a federal position between 2025-09-06 and 2025-10-02. The resolution will be based on media reports and official statements from the Trump administration. For the purpose of this question, a high-profile official is defined as a member of the Cabinet, a senior advisor, or a spokesperson for the administration. The resolution will be based on publicly available information and will not rely on private conversations or unpublished reports. The resolution source will be the Trump administration's official statements, as well as reputable news outlets such as CNN, Fox News, and The New York Times. (https://www.cnn.com/ https://www.foxnews.com/ https://www.nytimes.com/)
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question as it could provide insight into the Trump administration's interest in Adams. If a high-profile official publicly mentions Adams as a potential candidate, it could indicate that the administration is seriously considering him for a position.

evidence.step1_decompose: The condition requires: (1) At least one high-profile Trump administration official (Cabinet member, senior advisor, or spokesperson) (2) publicly mentions Eric Adams (3) as a potential candidate for a federal position (4) between September 6 and October 2, 2025. Observable evidence would be an on-record public statement by a named, qualified official explicitly naming Adams as a candidate for a specific federal position.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Searched for: 'Eric Adams federal position Trump administration official', 'Eric Adams Trump cabinet appointment federal job 2025', 'Trump official Steve Witkoff Eric Adams ambassador Saudi Arabia offer', 'Trump administration Eric Adams HUD ambassador federal role September 2025', 'Steve Witkoff publicly mentioned Eric Adams federal position ambassador September 2025', 'Trump White House aides offered Adams federal job ambassador HUD statement'
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events found: (1) Steve Witkoff met with Adams in Florida and reportedly 'floated' the idea of Adams becoming Saudi Arabia ambassador — but this was reported through anonymous sources, not a public on-record statement by Witkoff. (2) NYT reported 'close Trump advisers considered offering Eric Adams a role in HUD or as ambassador to Saudi Arabia' — again through anonymous sourcing. (3) Trump himself publicly DENIED offering Adams any role, saying 'I didn't do that.' (4) The Hill confirmed 'The White House has not commented on the reports.' (5) Adams' own press secretary said 'no formal offers' were made. (6) After Adams dropped out on Sept 28, multiple outlets reported that 'White House aides reportedly dangled a federal ambassadorship' but no named official publicly confirmed this. All candidate events are based on anonymous sourcing or private conversations — none meet the criteria of a public statement by a named, high-profile official.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: None of the candidate events match the resolution criteria exactly. The criteria requires a 'publicly' mentioned statement from a 'high-profile official' (Cabinet member, senior advisor, or spokesperson). All reports of Adams being considered for a federal role came from: (a) anonymous sources, (b) Trump's public DENIAL that he offered Adams anything, (c) Adams' own press secretary confirming no formal offers. No named high-profile Trump administration official publicly stated on the record that Adams was being considered for a federal position. [The Hill](https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5484212-mayor-adams-ends-campaign/) explicitly states 'The White House has not commented on the reports.' [Gateway Pundit](https://www.thegatewaypundit.com/2025/09/eric-adams-says-he-would-consider-role-trump/) notes 'no formal offers' were made. [Yahoo/The Hill](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/eric-adams-running-just-negotiating-212513040.html) reports Trump denied speaking to Adams about a job.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying public statement by a named high-profile Trump administration official was found within the window. Therefore no timestamp can be extracted for a Yes resolution.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: Not applicable, as no qualifying event was identified.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence strongly supports a No resolution: (1) Trump publicly denied offering Adams any role. (2) The White House did not comment on anonymous reports. (3) Adams' own press secretary confirmed no formal offers. (4) The New York Post reported on Sept 11 that 'Eric Adams' job prospects in Trump admin all but dead.' (5) After Adams dropped out on Sept 28, reports still describe the ambassadorship as something that 'fizzled after negotiations soured' — indicating nothing was ever publicly confirmed by an official. The question resolution criteria specifically requires reliance on 'official statements' and 'publicly available information,' not private conversations or anonymous reports.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No high-profile Trump administration official publicly and explicitly mentioned Eric Adams as a potential candidate for a federal position during the window September 6 - October 2, 2025. All reports were based on anonymous sourcing of private conversations. Trump himself publicly denied it. The White House made no on-record comments. The resolution criteria specifically requires public statements from high-profile officials — this standard is not met. Resolution: No.

question: Apple AirTags 2 priced below $30 USD at release?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the standard edition of the AirTag 2 launches at $29.99 or less. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve based on the pre-tax launch price in USD of the standard edition of the AirTag 2 as listed on the official Apple Store website or Apple’s retail pricing in the United States on the first official day of its release.

If the price differs between configurations, this market will resolve according to the lower price of the version that includes the full standard AirTag 2 model with no additional features, accessories, or services.

A qualifying product must be named "AirTag" and be recognized as a successor to the original AirTag product, similar to the relationship between iPhone 14 and iPhone 15. A new AirTag product released without a number, under a designation other than AirTag 2 will qualify if it retains the original functions of the AirTag and expands on them in such a way that it is clear that this product is a successor.

In order to be considered released, the product must be available for purchase by the general public within the specified timeframe. An announcement or unveiling alone is not sufficient.

If the AirTag 2 is not released by June 30, 2026, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official Apple Store (online or retail pricing), however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

The September 2025 event is rumored to include the launch of the AirTag 2, as well as other Apple products. [8] Apple AirTags are being sold in 4-packs on eBay’s Techciti store for AU$104.30, a 37% discount from the original AU$165 price, which works out to about AU$26 per tag. [9] Apple is offering AirTags at an all-time low on Amazon for back-to-school: a 4-pack for $69 (down from $99, $17 each) and individual tags for about $29 (down from $29).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Apple announces a new AirTag model with a starting price below $29 USD at the September 2025 event, according to the official Apple website or credible reporting sources (e.g. Bloomberg, CNET, The Verge). The resolution criteria will be based on the price listed on Apple's website on the first official day of the event. The resolution will occur between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-10 (inclusive).
subquestions.rationale: If Apple announces a new AirTag model with a starting price below $29 USD at the September 2025 event, it could indicate that the company is targeting a more affordable price point for the AirTag 2, which would be a positive indicator for the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Apple must announce a new AirTag model with starting price below $29 USD at the September 2025 event (between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-10). Observable evidence: explicit price listing on Apple's website or credible reporting confirming both announcement and sub-$29 price at the September 9 event.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Apple September 2025 event AirTag announcement' - to find if AirTag was announced; 2) 'Apple AirTag 2 new model price 2025' - to find any stated price; 3) 'AirTag 2 price announced September 9 2025 Apple event' - for explicit price confirmation; 4) 'Apple AirTag 2 second generation official price release date buy' - for official pricing; 5) 'AirTag 2 not announced Awe Dropping Apple event September 9 2025' - to disprove announcement.
evidence.step3_event_detection: The Apple 'Awe Dropping' event took place on September 9, 2025. Products announced: iPhone 17, iPhone Air ($999), iPhone 17 Pro ($1,099), iPhone 17 Pro Max ($1,199), Apple Watch Series 11 ($399), Apple Watch SE3 ($249), Apple Watch Ultra 3 ($799), AirPods Pro 3 ($249). AirTag 2 was NOT among announced products. 9to5Mac post-event article explicitly states: 'Bloomberg reported that the new AirTag is nearly ready for launch, but Apple chose not to reveal it at the event.'
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires AirTag 2 to be (1) announced at the September 2025 event AND (2) priced below $29. The 9to5Mac post-event roundup [https://9to5mac.com/2025/09/09/heres-everything-apple-didnt-announce-during-its-awe-dropping-event/] explicitly confirms AirTag 2 was NOT announced. Wired's 'Everything Apple Announced Today' [https://www.wired.com/story/everything-apple-announced-iphone-air-iphone-17-apple-watches-airpods-pro-3/] lists all announced products with no mention of AirTag 2. Neither criterion is met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Apple September 9, 2025 event occurred at 10:00 AM PT / 1:00 PM ET on September 9, 2025. Post-event articles confirming AirTag 2 was not announced were published on 2025-09-09. The definitive No conclusion is established as of 2025-09-09T17:00:00Z (after event concluded).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The event was a single occurrence on September 9, 2025. No earlier event in the resolution window featured an AirTag 2 announcement.
evidence.step7_verification: Some pre-event and low-quality post-event articles (Medium.com) mention AirTag 2 as if it was announced, but these appear to be AI-generated or based on pre-event expectations. Credible post-event sources (9to5Mac, Wired, Popular Science, NBC News, PCMag) consistently confirm AirTag 2 was NOT announced. The 9to5Mac article explicitly categorizes it as a product Apple 'didn't announce.' No source provides an AirTag 2 starting price from the event. No contradictory credible evidence exists.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Apple did not announce AirTag 2 at the September 9, 2025 'Awe Dropping' event. The question requires both an announcement AND a price below $29. Since no announcement was made, the question definitively resolves No. The earliest definitive No moment is the conclusion of the September 9 event, approximately 2025-09-09T17:00:00Z.

question: Will BLS stop reporting payroll data this year?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) ceases regular publication of any of the following reports: monthly Employment Situation reports (nonfarm payrolls and unemployment rate), Consumer Price Index (CPI), Producer Price Index (PPI), Employment Cost Index, Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey (JOLTS), by December 31, 2025 at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No."

For purposes of this market, “ceases regular publication” means any of the following:

- The BLS officially announces it will no longer publish the report on its regular schedule.
- The BLS misses three consecutive scheduled releases of the report without providing the data within 30 days of each scheduled release date.
- The BLS announces that the report is discontinued, terminated, or permanently suspended.
- Legislative or executive action explicitly prohibits or defunds the publication of the report.

The following do NOT qualify as cessation:
- Temporary delays or postponements followed by subsequent publication (including delays caused by government shutdowns).
- Changes in methodology, seasonal adjustment, or calculation methods while continuing publication.
- Changes in publication frequency (e.g., monthly to quarterly) while maintaining regular releases.
- Format changes (e.g., digital-only, layout changes).
- Publishing preliminary or partial data with full data forthcoming.
- Changes to specific components within a report while the overall data series continues.
- Combining the report with other reports while still publishing the underlying data.
- BLS delays the jobs report due to a shutdown, then publishes it.
- BLS changes CPI methodology but continues publishing monthly CPI.
- BLS shifts employment data from monthly to quarterly.
- The Federal Reserve begins publishing employment data while BLS continues its own.
- BLS website outage delays posting, but data is released via other channels.
- BLS publishes preliminary data pending final adjustments.

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) miss at least two scheduled releases of the monthly Employment Situation report between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31?
subquestions.background_information: The BLS has been facing challenges in collecting data due to underfunding and staffing shortages [1]. A government shutdown could further disrupt the release of key economic data, including the monthly Employment Situation report [2]. The Labor Department's contingency plan states that the BLS will suspend all operations and cease data collection activities during a shutdown [3]. This could lead to delays in the release of the Employment Situation report. The BLS has a history of missing data releases during government shutdowns, with the longest delay occurring in 2018-2019 [4].
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the BLS misses at least two scheduled releases of the monthly Employment Situation report between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-31. The outcome will be determined by reviewing the BLS's release calendar and data collection activities during this period [5]. If the BLS is unable to publish the report on its scheduled release dates, and the delay is not due to a temporary postponement or a change in methodology, this question will resolve to Yes. The primary source for this question will be the BLS's release calendar, available on their website [6].
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because a delay in the release of the Employment Situation report could indicate a disruption in the BLS's ability to collect and publish data. This could be a sign that the BLS is struggling to continue its operations, which could ultimately lead to a cessation of its data reporting.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires the BLS to miss at least TWO scheduled releases of the monthly Employment Situation report between October 1–31, 2025. Each monthly Employment Situation report covers the prior month's data and is typically released once per month. In October 2025, only ONE Employment Situation report is normally scheduled: the September 2025 Employment Situation (covering August 2025 labor data), originally scheduled for October 3, 2025. The October 2025 Employment Situation (covering September 2025 data) would be scheduled for November 7, 2025 — outside the window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Queries used: (1) 'BLS Bureau of Labor Statistics Employment Situation report October 2025' to find what happened to the October scheduled release; (2) 'BLS Employment Situation report missed canceled delayed 2025' to identify missed releases; (3) 'BLS Employment Situation October 2025 jobs report release date scheduled' to confirm the calendar; (4) 'government shutdown end October 2025 BLS resume operations' to check if the shutdown ended and BLS resumed; (5) 'BLS jobs report November 2025 October employment situation released' for the November 7 report status; (6) 'BLS November 7 jobs report scheduled Employment Situation October 2025' for second report context; (7) 'BLS Employment Situation report October 3 missed canceled shutdown'.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) September 2025 Employment Situation report (scheduled October 3, 2025) was definitively NOT released due to the government shutdown that began October 1, 2025. Multiple sources confirm this (HuffPost, AFP, Yahoo Finance, The Hill, Newsweek, etc.). (2) The government shutdown continued through at least October 27-31, 2025 (27th day as of October 27, per WBAP/CNBC). (3) The October Employment Situation report (November 7) is outside the window but was also put at risk. (4) The BLS explicitly stated 'No other releases will be rescheduled or produced until the resumption of regular government services' (Investing.com UK, October 10). (5) Sources from October 21 (TalkMarkets) note 'The October employment situation release may not be published' — indicating a second report was at risk but not yet scheduled within October. No evidence of a second Employment Situation report being scheduled for October 2025.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Only ONE Employment Situation report was scheduled within the October 1–31, 2025 window: the September 2025 Employment Situation (for August 2025 data), scheduled October 3, 2025. This report was definitively missed due to the government shutdown. The October 2025 Employment Situation (covering September 2025 data) was scheduled for November 7, 2025 — outside the resolution window. No second Employment Situation report was scheduled within the October 1–31 window. The resolution criteria require TWO missed releases within the window, but only one report was scheduled. Therefore, the criteria for 'Yes' cannot be satisfied. The BLS statement confirmed: 'No other releases will be rescheduled or produced until the resumption of regular government services' [Investing.com UK](https://uk.investing.com/news/economy-news/us-to-release-september-inflation-data-despite-shutdown-93CH-4300183), making it explicit that even the missed October 3 report would not be rescheduled within October.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The September 2025 Employment Situation report was scheduled for October 3, 2025, and missed. This is confirmed by multiple sources dated October 1–3, 2025. The shutdown began October 1, 2025, at 12:01 a.m. No second Employment Situation report was scheduled in October 2025. The shutdown was ongoing as of at least October 27, 2025 (confirmed by CNBC article dated October 27, 2025).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: There is only one Employment Situation report scheduled per month. The only one scheduled in October 2025 was the September 2025 report (for August data), due October 3. No earlier or additional Employment Situation release was scheduled within October 2025. The pre-shutdown delay mentioned in Raw Story (September 20) refers to the same September 2025 Employment Situation report being rescheduled — it was moved from an earlier date to October 3, which then was missed. This is one report, not two.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: The question might be interpreted to include a rescheduled September Employment Situation report (previously delayed from September 20) as one release, and the October 3 original schedule as a second. However, these refer to the same report (the September 2025 Employment Situation covering August data) — first delayed from ~September 26 to a later date, then never released. This is ONE missed report, not two. No sources indicate a second separate Employment Situation report was scheduled for release in October 2025. The November 7 report (for October data) is clearly outside the window. The TalkMarkets article (October 21) notes 'The October employment situation release may not be published' — this refers to the November 7 scheduled release, not an October-scheduled release. The shutdown was ongoing through at least October 27-31 with no government reopening during October.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The BLS missed exactly ONE scheduled Employment Situation report during October 1–31, 2025: the September 2025 Employment Situation (scheduled October 3, 2025). Only one such report is scheduled per month in normal circumstances. There is no evidence of a second Employment Situation report being scheduled within October 2025. The resolution criteria require at least TWO missed releases, which is structurally impossible given only one was scheduled. Resolution: No.

question: Brazilian Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes be impeached 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the the Federal Senate (Senado Federal) votes to proceed with any impeachment of Minister of the Supreme Federal Court of Brazil Alexandre de Moraes by December 31, 2025 ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve based on the results of the first such vote the Senate undertakes (e.g., if the Federal Senate decides to vote on the impeachment of Alexandre de Moraes and it fails to pass, this market will resolve to "No").

This market will resolve to "Yes" as soon as the Senate successfully votes to proceed with this impeachment, regardless of the impeachment's outcome.

If it becomes impossible to impeach Alexandre de Moraes while he is in his role as Minister (e.g., he resigns) and the "Yes" condition has not yet been met, this market will immediately resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be information from the government of Brazil, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will at least two Brazilian Senators from different parties submit an impeachment request against Justice Alexandre de Moraes between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30?
subquestions.background_information: Impeachment proceedings against Justice Alexandre de Moraes have been initiated in the past, with the most recent one being led by Congressman Hélio Lopes (Breitbart, 2025-08-07). The request cited abuse of authority, administrative impropriety, censorship, and violation of constitutional guarantees of freedom of expression and parliamentary immunity. However, it is unclear whether this request will be successful or if there will be enough support for an impeachment. With the current political climate in Brazil, it is possible that other Senators may also consider submitting their own impeachment requests. This would indicate a growing opposition to Justice de Moraes and potentially increase the likelihood of an impeachment proceeding against him. [1, 2, 3]
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30, at least two Brazilian Senators from different parties submit an impeachment request against Justice Alexandre de Moraes. The resolution will be based on publicly available information from the Brazilian Senate and other credible sources, such as news outlets (e.g., [1, 2, 3]). We will use the Senate's official website and news articles from reputable sources to track the number of impeachment requests submitted during this period. The resolution will be made based on the number of requests submitted, not their outcome or the success of the impeachment proceedings.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because it indicates the level of opposition to Justice Alexandre de Moraes within the Brazilian Senate. If multiple Senators submit impeachment requests, it would suggest that there is a significant amount of opposition to his actions, which could increase the likelihood of an impeachment proceeding against him.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition: At least 2 Brazilian Senators from *different* political parties must formally submit (file/protocol) an impeachment request against STF Justice Alexandre de Moraes between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30. Observable evidence: Senate records or credible news reporting that at least two senators from different parties each filed such a request within that window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Brazilian Senators impeachment request Alexandre de Moraes 2025' (Sept 1-30); 2) 'impeachment Alexandre Moraes Senado setembro 2025'; 3) 'senators impeachment Moraes Senate September 2025 formal petition'; 4) 'pedido impeachment Alexandre Moraes senadores partidos setembro 2025'; 5) 'Brazil Senate impeachment Moraes STF formal request filed 2025'; 6) 'Brazil senators impeach Moraes Liberal Party September 2025 new request'; 7) 'senadores impeachment Moraes Bolsonaro condenação partidos diferentes pedido'; 8) 'Brazil Senate Moraes impeachment request senators different parties September October 2025'; 9) 'senadores impeachment Moraes partidos setembro outubro 2025'
evidence.step3_event_detection: Evidence found: (1) Aug 7, 2025 Breitbart article: Five senators from the Liberal Party (single party) filed the '30th attempt' impeachment request — BEFORE the window. (2) Sept 1 Yahoo article mentions '41 senators have lined up to remove Moraes' — this is political alignment/intent, not a formal filing of impeachment request by multiple parties. (3) Aug 6 article: opposition in Senado 'wants to prioritize the impeachment' — intent, not a filed request, and before the window. (4) No article explicitly describes a formal impeachment request by senators from DIFFERENT parties filed in September 2025.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution requires at least two senators from *different* parties to *submit* a formal impeachment request during the September 2025 window. The closest match found (Breitbart, [https://www.breitbart.com/latin-america/2025/08/06/brazil-tries-impeach-judge-30th-time-who-put-jair-bolsonaro-house-arrest/]) is from five senators of the Liberal Party (single party) in August 2025 — fails both the 'different parties' criterion and the September window. No direct evidence of qualifying events in the window was found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No timestamp within the September 2025 window could be extracted for a qualifying event.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying first occurrence was identified within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple searches conducted. Political context shows significant pressure to impeach Moraes, including 41 senators 'lined up,' but the evidence consistently describes political alignment/intent rather than formal submissions from different parties during September 2025. After Bolsonaro's conviction on Sept 11, new impeachment calls were likely, but no explicit filing by senators from different parties was found in news coverage.
evidence.step8_final_decision: No explicit, verifiable evidence was found of at least two senators from different parties formally submitting an impeachment request against Moraes during September 2025. The window has closed. Resolution is No, with resolution_datetime set to end of the window.

question: Will the US strike 3 countries in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the total number of different countries' soil that the United States initiates a drone, missile, or air strike on between January 1, 2026, 12:00 AM ET and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Strikes on embassies or consulates will count towards the country the embassy or consulate is located in, not towards the country they represent.

Strikes within the territory controlled by the United States as of December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET will not be counted towards this market's resolution.

For the purposes of this market, a qualifying "strike" is defined as the use of aerial bombs, drones, or missiles (including cruise or ballistic missiles) launched by US military forces that impact another country's ground territory that is officially acknowledged by the US government or a consensus of credible reporting.
