question: Will Trump try to fire another Fed Governor by October 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Donald Trump publicly and unequivocally announces that he is removing another Fed Governor before their term is up, or takes formal action toward doing so, such as issuing a directive or formal request between August 25 and October 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Statements which are contingent (e.g. “Powell must step down or raise rates”), statements of intent (e.g.“I am planning to fire Powell”) or other informal statements which are not unequivocal will not qualify.

The resolution source will be official information from Donald Trump however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will President Trump make a public announcement about a plan to replace at least one more Federal Reserve Governor by October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
Since President Trump has already announced the removal of one Federal Reserve Governor, Lisa Cook, on August 28, 2025, it's essential to understand the current context and potential implications. According to a CNN International article, Trump stated that he 'would do this if she didn't resign' and another Trump administration official said, 'The president is a man who sticks to his word.' [1] This suggests that Trump may be willing to follow through on his promises to remove other governors. Furthermore, the article notes that the Fed's independence could be challenged by Trump's actions. [1] The current number of Federal Reserve Governors is seven, with five of the 12 regional-bank-appointed members voting on a rotational basis. [7] If Trump secures a majority of four governors, he could effectively control the Federal Open Market Committee. [7]

Sources:
CNN International - 'We just jumped into the unknown:' Inside Trump's attempt to put his mark on the Fed
https://www.cnn.com/2025/08/28/business/trump-fed-lisa-cook/index.html
World Socialist - With the Lisa Cook sacking Trump steps up drive to take over Federal Reserve
https://www.wsws.org/en/articles/2025/08/27/trum-a27.html
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if, between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01, President Trump makes a public announcement on or before October 1, 2025, about a plan to replace at least one more Federal Reserve Governor, and the announcement is confirmed by a reliable news source, such as The New York Times or Reuters. The resolution will be based on the official statement or a transcript of the announcement. The resolution source will be official information from Donald Trump, however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.
subquestions.rationale: This subquestion is relevant to the ultimate question because it assesses President Trump's intentions and actions regarding the Federal Reserve. If Trump makes a public announcement about a plan to replace another governor, it may indicate his willingness to continue challenging the Fed's independence and potentially undermine their decision-making process. This could be a crucial indicator of his likelihood to try to fire another Fed Governor by October 31, 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: The question requires Trump to make a PUBLIC ANNOUNCEMENT between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01 about a PLAN TO REPLACE AT LEAST ONE MORE Federal Reserve Governor. 'At least one more' implies beyond what was already announced or in process. Before the window: (1) Adriana Kugler resigned Aug 8, 2025, and Trump announced Miran's nomination on Aug 7 to replace her; (2) Trump fired Lisa Cook on Aug 25, 2025 (before the window opened). Observable evidence needed: Trump specifically announces a new plan to replace a Federal Reserve Governor during the September 1–October 1, 2025 window — either naming a new replacement for Cook (whose removal was blocked) or announcing a plan to remove/replace a different sitting governor.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Trump replace Federal Reserve Governor announcement 2025' (Sept 1-Oct 1) — to find any new replacement announcement. Query 2: 'Trump Federal Reserve Board Governor fired replacement September 2025' — to find firing/replacement events. Query 3: 'Trump nominate Federal Reserve Governor permanent replacement announcement September October 2025' — to find new nominations. Query 4: 'Trump Lisa Cook replacement nominee announced September 2025' — to find if Trump named a specific successor for Cook during the window.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Trump's Aug 25 firing of Lisa Cook — this is BEFORE the window, so does not count as a new announcement within the window. (2) Trump's ongoing SCOTUS petition (filed Sept 19) to allow Cook's removal — this is continuation of the Aug 25 action, not a new plan to replace a governor, and no specific successor was named. (3) Trump announced Sept 6 his top three finalists (Hassett, Warsh, Waller) for Fed CHAIR position — this is about the Fed Chair succession, not specifically a Federal Reserve Governor replacement plan in the same sense. (4) Miran confirmed to board Sept 15 — this was a nomination announced Aug 7, before the window. (5) No evidence found of Trump announcing a new plan to replace any additional Federal Reserve Governor (beyond Cook/Kugler actions already announced before Sept 1).
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require an announcement of a 'plan to replace at least one MORE Federal Reserve Governor.' The ongoing Lisa Cook removal effort was announced Aug 25, before the window. The SCOTUS petition filed Sept 19 is a legal continuation, not a new announcement of a replacement plan. The Sept 6 announcement about Fed Chair finalists [Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/world-news/trump-names-hassett-warsh-and-waller-as-top-three-finalists-for-fed-chair-125090600131_1.html) concerns the Chair succession (Powell's term ends May 2026), not a new plan to replace a Governor. No new nomination or announcement about replacing an additional Fed Governor (beyond what was already in progress before Sept 1) was found within the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event with an exact timestamp within the Sept 1–Oct 1, 2025 window was found. The Trump administration continued its legal battle to remove Cook (SCOTUS petition Sept 19), discussed Fed Chair candidates (Sept 6), and confirmed Miran (Sept 15–16), but none of these constitute a new announcement about a plan to replace an additional Federal Reserve Governor.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying first occurrence was found within the window. The actions most proximate to the resolution criteria (Cook's firing, Miran's nomination) both occurred before September 1, 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Multiple sources confirm the Lisa Cook removal was announced Aug 25 (before window), and the SCOTUS petition was a continuation of that effort. The Sept 6 finalists announcement was for Fed Chair, not Governor. No new plan to replace an additional Governor was announced during the window. There is no evidence of Trump naming a successor for Cook or announcing a plan to replace another governor during September 1–October 1, 2025.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question asks whether Trump made a public announcement about a plan to replace AT LEAST ONE MORE Federal Reserve Governor between September 1–October 1, 2025. The key relevant actions (Cook's firing announcement Aug 25, Miran's nomination Aug 7) both occurred BEFORE the resolution window. During the window, Trump continued legal proceedings regarding Cook's removal (SCOTUS petition Sept 19) and discussed Fed Chair candidates (Sept 6), but there was no new, distinct announcement of a plan to replace an additional or new Federal Reserve Governor. The resolution window closed on October 1, 2025 with no qualifying announcement. Resolution: No.

question: Will Trump lower tariffs on Canada by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Donald Trump signs any federal legislation or performs any executive action that lowers, pauses, delays, or removes any tariffs on imports from Canada by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Actions that lower, pause, delay, or remove any tariffs on Canadian imports will qualify, including changes to the reciprocal tariff, or any other existing or new tariffs specifically targeting Canadian goods.

Only the removal of tariffs specifically targeting Canada will qualify. For example, the removal of the 10% general tariff on all imports into the U.S., or a tariff on specific Canadian provinces or entities, will not count toward this market’s resolution.

Item-specific tariff exemptions, such as those outlined in the U.S. Customs and Border Protection notice dated April 11, 2025, which excluded 25 HTSUS codes covering electronics, will not qualify.

Any action officially enacted within the market’s time frame will qualify, regardless of when the change goes into effect.

This market’s primary resolution source will be official information from the Trump administration; however, a consensus of credible information from major news outlets or government statements will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will President Trump impose new tariffs on Canadian goods before November 15, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: The Trump administration has been imposing tariffs on various countries, including Canada. Recently, it updated tariffs on several trading partners and set import taxes ranging from 10% to 41% (Source: [1] Pittsburgh's Action News 4, New tariffs on Canada take effect Friday; Dozens of other countries delayed, 2025-08-01). The current tariffs on Canadian goods are 25% on most items, but the administration has imposed 35% tariffs on some goods not covered by the U.S.-Mexico-Canada trade agreement. The administration has also signed an executive order imposing additional tariffs on Canada. The tariff changes have already affected small businesses in British Columbia, Canada, with 46% of businesses surveyed by the Canadian Federation of Independent Business (CFIB) expecting to be impacted (Source: [2] My Cowichan Valley Now, B.C. small businesses brace for end of U.S. duty-free exemption, 2025-08-22).
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Trump administration imposes new tariffs on Canadian goods between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-15, as reported by the U.S. Customs and Border Protection website [3] (https://www.cbp.gov/) or the official White House press releases [4] (https://www.whitehouse.gov/).
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because it assesses the likelihood of President Trump imposing new tariffs on Canadian goods, which could be an indicator of his willingness to lower tariffs on Canada in the future.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: Trump administration imposes new tariffs on Canadian goods between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-15. Observable evidence: Official announcement or CBP/White House confirmation of new tariff taking effect on Canadian goods within the window. Key entities: U.S. government (CBP/White House), Canadian goods. Timing: Oct 31 to Nov 15, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Trump new tariffs Canada November 2025' (Nov 1-15 window) — to find new tariffs within window. Query 2: 'Trump Canada tariffs imposed October November 2025' (Oct 25-Nov 15) — to find announcements and implementations. Query 3: 'Trump 10% tariff Canada implemented effective date November 2025' — to check if Ontario-ad tariff was formalized. Query 4: 'Section 232 tariff trucks buses Canada effective November 1 2025' — to confirm truck/bus tariff effective date. Query 5: 'Trump Canada 10 percent tariff formally signed executive order' — to check formal implementation.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate event 1: Section 232 tariffs on medium/heavy-duty trucks (25%) and buses (10%) effective November 1, 2025. Confirmed by multiple sources (CBC News, Macau Business, JD Supra Section 232 article, ConnectGujarat). Canada accounts for ~20% of U.S. truck imports, and Canadian manufacturers are directly affected. This is a new tariff that took effect within the window. Candidate event 2: Threatened 10% additional tariff on all Canadian goods (retaliation for Ontario ad). Announced October 25-27 via Truth Social, but Treasury Secretary Bessent explicitly confirmed on November 2, 2025 that it 'has not yet been implemented' (Epoch Times). As of November 3, Globe and Mail reported 'no executive order has been issued' and 'no implementation date has been announced.' Some later opinion pieces (Project Syndicate Nov 12, interest.co.nz Nov 13) loosely claim it was 'imposed,' but these are contradicted by direct official statements from November 2-3 and appear to conflate the threat with formal implementation. Candidate event 1 (truck/bus tariffs) is the most clearly confirmed new tariff within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Section 232 truck/bus tariffs: [CBC News Nov 1](https://www.cbc.ca/news/business/truck-bus-tariffs-9.6962040) confirms 'Starting November 1, 2025, new U.S. tariffs on medium and heavy-duty trucks and buses went into effect' and these 'are expected to significantly impact Canadian truck and bus manufacturers.' [Macau Business Nov 1](https://www.macaubusiness.com/us-tariffs-on-heavy-trucks-buses-come-into-effect/) states 'On November 1, 2025, new U.S. tariffs on medium- and heavy-duty trucks took effect' with Canada accounting for ~20% of imports. [JD Supra Section 232 article Nov 5](https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/section-232-in-the-spotlight-the-4242946/) confirms 'Medium- and heavy-duty trucks face a 25% tariff, effective November 1, 2025.' These are new tariffs (not existing ones) that directly apply to Canadian-made trucks and buses. The White House announced them on October 27 per [Truckinginfo](https://www.truckinginfo.com/10247976/trump-announces-25-tariff-on-heavy-duty-trucks). This satisfies: (a) new tariffs, (b) on Canadian goods (trucks/buses from Canada are subject to this), (c) imposed within the window (November 1 is within Oct 31–Nov 15). The Ontario-ad 10% tariff: explicitly NOT yet implemented as of Nov 2-3 per Bessent statements.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Section 232 truck/bus tariff: effective date November 1, 2025. This is explicitly stated in multiple sources as a precise date. The White House announcement was October 27, 2025, with the proclamation specifying November 1 as the effective date. This is within the resolution window of Oct 31–Nov 15, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The Section 232 truck/bus tariff effective date of November 1, 2025, is the first qualifying event within the window. There is no evidence of any other new tariff on Canadian goods between Oct 31 and Nov 1. The October 31 start date of the window means November 1 is within scope.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradiction check: Could the truck/bus tariffs be considered 'not new' to Canadian goods? No — these were newly announced on October 27 and newly effective on November 1, 2025; they did not exist before. Could USMCA exemptions disqualify this? Partial exemption: USMCA-compliant trucks face tariff only on non-U.S. content, and Canadian buses face 10% with no USMCA exemption (per SooToday article confirming 'no exemptions or carve-outs' for buses). Canadian trucks not fully USMCA-compliant face 25% on non-U.S. content — this is still a new tariff burden. The CBP/White House requirement: the Section 232 proclamation would be on the White House website; the implementation would be tracked by CBP. Multiple high-quality sources confirm effective date. The Ontario-ad 10% tariff: not formally implemented within the window based on Bessent's explicit Nov 2 statement and Globe and Mail Nov 3 report.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution = Yes. The Section 232 tariffs on medium/heavy-duty trucks (25%) and buses (10%) took effect on November 1, 2025, which is within the resolution window (Oct 31–Nov 15, 2025). Canada is a directly affected country (~20% of U.S. truck imports, with Canadian manufacturers explicitly cited as impacted). This constitutes new tariffs on Canadian goods being imposed within the window. Multiple credible sources confirm the November 1 effective date. The tariff was announced via White House proclamation on October 27. The additional threatened 10% tariff (Ontario ad) was NOT formally implemented within the window per explicit Treasury Secretary Bessent statements on November 2.

The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act was referred to the Senate Banking Committee on September 18, 2025, but no markup vote occurred before October 1.

evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independent sources (CoinDesk, Forbes, Cointelegraph, Coingape, CNBC, The Hill) consistently confirm that: (1) Senate Banking Committee delayed its markup from September 30 to October (week of Oct 20); (2) Senate Agriculture Committee had not even published a draft as of late September 2025, with its markup planned for October. A government shutdown looming on September 30 further confirmed the impossibility of meeting the deadline. evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Neither the Senate Banking Committee nor the Senate Agriculture Committee reported out the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act (or its Senate equivalent, the Responsible Financial Innovation Act of 2025) before October 1, 2025. question: Will Crude Oil (CL) hit (HIGH) $70 by end of June?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, on any trading day, the official CME settlement price for the Active Month (front month) of Crude Oil (CL) futures is equal to or above the listed price by the final trading day of June 2026. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No".

For CME Crude Oil (CL) futures contracts, the active month is the nearest of the contract months listed. The active month becomes a non-active month effective two business days prior to the spot month expiration. For example; if the spot month expires on a Friday the next listed contract will be considered the Active Month on the Wednesday prior to the spot month expiration.

Only the Active Month's official settlement price published by CME Group will be considered. Intraday trades, highs, lows, bids, offers, midpoint values, or indicative prices do not count.

Note that the settlement price may differ from the last traded price. CME's methodology to determine the settlement price can vary by commodity and contract.

Only days on which CME publishes an official settlement price for the Active Month will be included. Days without settlement prices (weekends, holidays, or market closures) are ignored.

This market will resolve based on the settlement price as it appears on the CME settlement page at the time it is first published for that trading day, regardless of any later corrections or updates.

The resolution source for this market is the CME Group website — specifically, the daily "Settlement" price for the Active Month of Crude Oil (CL) futures.

question: Will the U.S. national debt hit $38 trillion in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the U.S. national debt reaches the listed value this year at any point by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be the U.S. Treasury Department (https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current). If treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current becomes unavailable, another credible source will be used.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. national debt increase by at least $0.5 trillion between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-15?
subquestions.background_information: The current U.S. national debt is over $37 trillion [1]. The Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget projects that the national debt could exceed $53 trillion by 2035 [9]. The Congressional Budget Office estimates that debt held by the public could rise from 100% of GDP in 2025 to 156% by 2055 [6]. This question considers the rapid growth of the national debt in recent years, with a trillion-dollar increase every 5 months [5].
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the U.S. national debt increases by at least $0.5 trillion between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-15, as reported by the U.S. Treasury Department [2]. The resolution criteria will use the monthly debt data provided by the Treasury Department, available at https://www.treasurydirect.gov/NP_WS/debt/current. If the Treasury Department's website becomes unavailable, another credible source will be used.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because a significant increase in the national debt in a short period could indicate a trend towards hitting $38 trillion in 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: U.S. national debt increases by ≥$0.5 trillion (i.e., ≥$500 billion) between 2025-10-01 and 2025-10-15, as reported by the U.S. Treasury Department. Observable evidence: the debt level on or around Oct 1 compared to Oct 15 must show a ≥$500B increase. Key threshold: if starting around $37.5-37.88 trillion, the ending figure must reach ~$38.0-38.4 trillion.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'U.S. national debt October 2025 Treasury' (Oct 1–15 window) — found multiple debt figures in the $37.5–37.9T range; Query 2: 'US national debt total October 1 2025' (Sept 28–Oct 5 window) — confirmed ~$37.5–37.88T around Oct 1–3; Query 3: 'US national debt $37 trillion October 15 2025 Treasury Department' (Oct 13–20) — found Oct 15 figure of $37.8T; Query 4: 'US national debt exact figure October 2025 Daily Treasury Statement' (Oct 1–16) — confirmed daily rate of ~$6B/day; Query 5: 'US national debt increase 500 billion October 2025' (Oct 1–20) — no extraordinary increase found.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate data points found: (1) End of September 2025 (FY end): ~$37.5–37.64 trillion per American Spectator, Magnolia Reporter; (2) Oct 2, 2025: $37.88 trillion per Yahoo Finance/Schweikert Daily Debt Monitor; (3) Oct 3, 2025: $37.85 trillion per JEC Senate; (4) Oct 7, 2025: $37.8 trillion per The Hill/Treasury data; (5) Oct 8, 2025: $37.86 trillion per Daily Caller/U.S. Treasury Fiscal Data; (6) Oct 8, 2025: 'exceeding $37.9 trillion' per News Ghana; (7) Oct 15, 2025: $37.8 trillion per Economic Times. Daily rate of increase is approximately $6 billion/day per multiple sources (JEC Senate, Yahoo Finance, Cryptopolitan). No events detected that would cause a $500B jump in this 15-day window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: For Yes resolution: debt on Oct 1 (~$37.5–37.88T) + $0.5T = required Oct 15 figure of ~$38.0–38.4T. Actual Oct 15 figure: $37.8 trillion per [Economic Times](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/us/us-debt-crisis-hits-record-levels-is-the-us-economy-in-danger-americas-37-8-trillion-national-debt-spirals-out-of-control-interest-payments-top-1-2-trillion-how-rising-u-s-debt-could-jolt-the-stock-market-j-p-morgan-has-this-to-say/articleshow/124582365.cms). At $6B/day over 14 days = ~$84 billion total increase, far short of $500 billion. The criteria are NOT met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Starting figure: ~$37.5 trillion (end of September 2025, confirmed by multiple sources including American Spectator on Oct 2, 2025 and Magnolia Reporter on Oct 7, 2025 citing end of fiscal year Sept 30). Ending figure: $37.8 trillion as of October 15, 2025 (Economic Times, published Oct 15, 2025). Maximum estimated increase: approximately $0.3 trillion over the period, well below the $0.5 trillion threshold.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple high-quality independent sources (Economic Times, The Hill citing Treasury data, JEC Senate, Daily Caller citing U.S. Treasury Fiscal Data, Yahoo Finance) all show debt in the $37.5–37.9T range throughout Oct 1–15. The daily growth rate (~$6B/day) is consistent across sources and mathematically precludes a $500B increase in 15 days (which would require ~$33B/day). September 2025 saw a record $198 billion budget surplus, suggesting debt may have slightly decreased entering October. No extraordinary debt events (emergency borrowing, accounting changes) were reported. No contradictory evidence found supporting a $500B increase.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The U.S. national debt was approximately $37.5 trillion at the start of October 2025 and $37.8 trillion on October 15, 2025. This represents an increase of approximately $0.3 trillion (or less), far below the $0.5 trillion threshold required for Yes resolution. The daily growth rate of ~$6 billion makes a $500 billion increase in 15 days physically impossible under normal circumstances, and no extraordinary events were reported. Resolution: No.

question: Will CME self certify a sports contract in 2025?

(2) DraftKings acquired Railbird (October 21-22), but explicitly stated initial offering would NOT include sports contracts. (3) Kraken acquired Small Exchange (October 16), no evidence of sports event contract self-certification. (4) All CFTC self-certification processes were frozen due to government shutdown starting October 1 with no end during window. No candidate events match criteria within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No filing found matching the criteria: (a) The CFTC's self-certification process was suspended due to the government shutdown (Federal Register order of October 1, 2025 restricted CFTC processing to safety/property emergencies only). (b) CFTC public database showed no new submissions since late September 2025. (c) DraftKings' Railbird explicitly excluded sports from initial rollout. (d) Kraken's Small Exchange acquisition was for crypto derivatives, not sports event contracts. None of these constitute a qualifying sports-based event contract self-certification within the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying timestamp found within the window. The government shutdown lasted at least 34 days as of November 5, 2025, covering the entire resolution window. The CFTC was functionally unable to receive/process/publish new self-certifications.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found within window. The only recent sports-based event contract self-certification was Polymarket/QCEX, filed approximately October 1-2, 2025, before the window start of October 9, 2025.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple sources confirm: (1) CFTC issued Federal Register order on October 1, 2025 limiting processing to safety/property emergencies. (2) 'The Desk: November' (published Nov 5) confirms shutdown was in 34th day with no press releases from CFTC since September 30. (3) The Covers.com article on Polymarket explicitly states 'The CFTC's public database shows no new submissions since late September.' (4) DraftKings acquiring Railbird does not constitute a sports contract filing. (5) Legal uncertainty around sports event contracts may have further discouraged new filings even if the process were available.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is NO. The U.S. government shutdown beginning October 1, 2025 effectively suspended the CFTC's self-certification process throughout the entire resolution window (October 9–November 8, 2025). No new sports-based event contract self-certifications were filed or made publicly verifiable by the CFTC during this period. New entities (DraftKings/Railbird, Kraken/Small Exchange) acquired DCM licenses but did not file sports event contract self-certifications within the window. question: Russia x Ukraine buffer zone agreement by December 31?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if there is an agreement on an official buffer zone between Russia and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "buffer zone" is defined as a neutral or otherwise militarily restricted area that lies between the territories of Russia and Ukraine and is intended to reduce or manage conflict between them.

A qualifying buffer zone does not need to cover a minimum geographic area, nor require the withdrawal of all categories of weapons or personnel. It is sufficient that the agreement explicitly demonstrates mutual intent to suspend offensive military action within the designated zone, for example, by stipulating the withdrawal of heavy artillery, armored vehicles, etc.

If the agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes," regardless of whether the buffer zone is established formally by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

Informal statements, plans contingent on future conditions, statements of intent without a formal policy directive, announcements of a partial implementation, or any other statements that do not constitute a formal policy announcement will not be considered.

A mutual agreement on a buffer zone will suffice for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of potential subsequent violations of such an agreement.

This market's resolution will be based on official announcements from both Russia and Ukraine; however, a broad consensus of credible media reporting stating an official agreement regarding a buffer zone between Russia and Ukraine has been reached will suffice.

question: Will Lionel Messi announce his retirement in 2025?
description:
This polymarket will resolve to "Yes" if Lionel Messi officially announces his retirement from club soccer by December 31, 2025, at 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, it will resolve to "No".

To resolve "Yes", the announcement must clearly state that Messi is retiring from club-level professional soccer. The announcement must come from Messi himself or his official representatives.

Retirement from international soccer alone will not qualify. 

The retirement must be intended to take effect immediately or prior to the start of the next club season following the announcement.

The primary resolution source will be official statements from Lionel Messi. A consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Lionel Messi officially announce his intention to retire from club soccer by October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:

[1] Messi is 38 years old and has previously signaled that the 2026 title defense would mark the end of his international career. [2] It is uncertain whether Messi will continue to play for Inter Miami beyond the 2025 season. [3] If Messi announces his intention to retire from club soccer, it could be an indicator that he is planning to retire from professional soccer altogether.

Sources:
Kashmir Life: https://kashmirlife.com/2025/08/29/messi-hints-at-retirement-after-2026-world-cup/
Yahoo Sports Canada: https://ca.yahoosports.com/2025/08/28/barcelona-and-argentina-icon-lionel-messi-hints-at-date-for-international-retirement/
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Lionel Messi officially announces his intention to retire from club soccer in a public statement, interview, or social media post between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01. The announcement must be made by Messi himself or his official representatives. Resolution will be based on official statements from Lionel Messi and a consensus of credible reporting. [4] If Messi's camp or representatives make a statement confirming his intention to retire from club soccer, it will be considered a resolution. [5]
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question as it addresses Messi's plans for club soccer, which could be an indicator of his overall retirement plans. If Messi announces his intention to retire from club soccer, it could suggest that he is planning to retire from professional soccer altogether, which would be consistent with the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Messi (or official representatives) publicly announces retirement from club soccer between 2025-09-01 and 2025-10-01. Observable evidence: an official statement, interview, or social media post explicitly stating Messi's retirement from club (not international) soccer.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Lionel Messi retirement announcement club soccer 2025' (Sep 1–Oct 1 2025) — to find any retirement from club statement. 2) 'Messi retire Inter Miami announcement September 2025' — to find any Inter Miami-related retirement announcement. 3) 'Messi officially announces retirement club football statement September 2025' — to find official statement. 4) 'Messi Inter Miami future plans contract 2025 season' — to find context about his club career. 5) 'Messi retirement from club soccer official statement 2025' — final verification search.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (a) Sergio Busquets announced retirement on Sep 26, 2025 — REJECTED: Busquets is Messi's teammate, not Messi himself. (b) Messi's emotional post-match interview after Argentina vs Venezuela (Sep 5) with vague retirement hints — REJECTED: these were about international football, not club soccer, and were non-committal ('we'll see', 'day by day'). (c) Messi signing a new multi-year contract extension with Inter Miami (~Sep 18, 2025, per ESPN, Bleacher Report, Sporting News, multiple sources) — this is the OPPOSITE of a retirement announcement.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No event matches the resolution criteria. [Busquets retirement](https://www.marca.com/en/football/mls/2025/09/26/68d61814268e3e367b8b4574.html) was Busquets, not Messi. Messi's international retirement hints were non-committal and not about club soccer. [Messi's new contract extension](https://bleacherreport.com/articles/25250321-lionel-messi-inter-miami-reportedly-nearing-multi-year-contract-extension) (Sep 18, 2025) kept him at Inter Miami through 2027–2028, directly contradicting any retirement from club soccer. [Yahoo Sports Canada](https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/news/inter-miami-already-wants-sign-152000435.html) confirmed a verbal agreement for a contract through 2028.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No retirement-from-club-soccer announcement timestamp can be extracted. The most relevant timestamp is September 18, 2025 — when Messi's contract EXTENSION (multi-year) was reported as near-final, making club retirement during the window definitively foreclosed.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (Messi announcing retirement from club soccer) exists within the window. The opposite occurred — a multi-year contract extension was reported.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence firmly supports No resolution: multiple reputable outlets (ESPN via Bleacher Report/Sporting News/theScore, Yahoo Sports Canada, Miami Herald) all reported in mid-to-late September 2025 that Messi was extending his Inter Miami contract through 2027 or 2028. Messi was still actively playing for Inter Miami in September 2025 and scoring goals. The only retirement news was Busquets (his teammate). Messi's international retirement hints were vague and did not address club soccer.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. Not only did Messi not announce retirement from club soccer between Sep 1–Oct 1, 2025, but he was actively finalizing a multi-year contract extension with Inter Miami during this exact window, making club retirement definitively impossible within the resolution period. The window closed on October 1, 2025 with no qualifying event.

question: Will the 10-year Treasury yield dip below 3.9% in 2025?
description:

subquestions.question: Will the 10-year US Treasury yield fall by at least 20 basis points from its current level by 2025-12-01?
subquestions.background_information: The current 10-year US Treasury yield is 4.09% (as of November 2025, [1]). According to a Reuters poll, bond strategists expect the yield to rise modestly to 4.10% in three and six months, and to 4.21% within a year (assuming no inflation surprises) [2]. However, market expectations for a December 2025 Federal Reserve interest rate cut have shifted, with the probability dropping from approximately 90% before the Federal Open Market Committee meeting to about 70% as of November 4, 2025 [3]. This shift could potentially lead to a decrease in the 10-year yield. A drop of 20 basis points would be a significant indicator of a potential decrease in the yield.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the 10-year US Treasury yield is lower than 4.09% - 0.20 by any date between 2025-11-17 and 2025-12-01. The resolution source will be the Department of the Treasury's Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates for the column '10 Yr' (https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2025).
subquestions.rationale: A decrease in the 10-year US Treasury yield could indicate a potential decrease in interest rates, which could be a positive indicator for the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: For Yes resolution, the 10-year US Treasury yield must fall below 3.89% (4.09% - 0.20% = 3.89%) at any point between 2025-11-17 and 2025-12-01, as measured by the Department of the Treasury's Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates. Observable evidence: an explicit report of the 10-year yield at or below 3.89% on any Treasury business day within the window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) '10-year US Treasury yield November 2025' to find daily levels; 2) 'Treasury yield 10-year rate basis points November December 2025' for additional coverage; 3) '10-year Treasury yield below 3.89% November 2025' to look for threshold breach; 4) 'US Treasury 10-year yield December 1 2025' for end-of-window data; 5) 'Treasury yield 3.89 percent record low November 2025' to find any extreme low.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate data points from news: Nov 17: 4.14-4.15%; Nov 18: 4.12%; Nov 20: 4.14%; Nov 21: 4.06%; Nov 24: 4.05%; Nov 25: 4.02%; Nov 26: 3.997% (Morningstar) / 4.02% (InstaForex close); Nov 28: 3.99%-4.015%. The lowest explicitly reported value was 3.997% on Nov 26, 2025 (Morningstar). No data points at or below 3.89% were found. No articles reported the 10-year yield falling below 4% in sustained fashion, with the lowest being ~3.99%.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution threshold is 3.89%. All reported yield levels during the window (Nov 17–Dec 1) were in the range of approximately 3.99%–4.15%, consistently above 3.89%. The closest approach was 3.997% on [Nov 26](https://www.morningstar.com/news/dow-jones/202511266335/10-year-treasury-yield-falls-to-3997-data-talk), which is still 10.7 basis points above the 3.89% threshold. The resolution condition was not met.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The lowest confirmed 10-year yield in the window was 3.997% on November 26, 2025 (Morningstar). This is 10.7 bps above the 3.89% threshold — not a qualifying event.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence (yield at or below 3.89%) was found at any point during the window. The question cannot resolve Yes.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple independent sources (Morningstar, InstaForex, Yahoo Finance, CBS News, Market Screener) all consistently show the 10-year yield stayed in the 3.99%–4.15% range throughout the window. No source reported a yield near or below 3.89%. The window closed on December 1, 2025, with the yield approximately around 4%. A TheStreet article from November 30 notes the 10-year Treasury yielding 'about 4%' by November 30. No contradictory evidence suggesting the yield reached 3.89% exists.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The 10-year US Treasury yield never fell to or below 3.89% during the resolution window (2025-11-17 to 2025-12-01). The lowest level explicitly reported was 3.997% on November 26, 2025, which is 10.7 basis points above the threshold. The question resolves No. Since the window closed on December 1, 2025 without the condition being met, the resolution datetime is 2025-12-01T23:59:59Z.

question: Russian strike on a NATO member by December 31?

The article from Al Jazeera (Feb 12) notes 'Ukrainian forces reportedly held the settlement of Zaliznychne in Zaporizhia despite Russian claims' — suggesting ISW may not have confirmed all Russian claims.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Russian MoD claimed 3 settlements on Jan 30 (within the window start), then additional settlements through Feb 10. evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The 10-settlement threshold appears to have been crossed somewhere between Feb 6-10, 2026, based on the accumulation of settlement claims and ISW-referenced AFP data. No earlier qualifying occurrence (before Jan 30) is relevant.

question: Will Maduro's rule survive a US military engagement?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if both of the following conditions are met. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

1. There is a military engagement between the military forces of the United States of America and Venezuela by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET.

A "military engagement" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between US and Venezuelan military forces. Non-violent actions, such as warning shots or missile launches that land in territorial waters or pass through airspace, will not qualify as a military engagement. Intentional ship ramming that results in significant damage to (e.g., a hole in the hull) or the sinking of a military ship by another will count as a military engagement; however, minor damage (scrapes, dents) will not.

Any U.S. military kinetic strike that impacts Venezuelan land territory will qualify as a military engagement.

Missiles or drone strikes which are intercepted will not qualify as a military engagement regardless of whether they land on adversarial territory or cause damage. Similarly, surface-to-air missile strikes impacting adversarial territory will not qualify as a military engagement (although surface to air missiles fired at an adversarial military aircraft would qualify).

Note: the U.S. Coast Guard is a branch of the U.S. Armed Forces; Venezuela’s Milicia Nacional Bolivariana (militia) is a “special component” of the Venezuelan National Bolivarian Armed Forces (FANB); and Venezuela’s Coast Guard (Comando de Guardacostas) is a component of the Venezuelan Navy (Armada Bolivariana) and thus part of the FANB.

2. President Nicolás Maduro is NOT removed from power within the first 30 days after such an engagement ends, with no subsequent engagement occurring.

President Nicolás Maduro will be considered to be removed from power if he resigns, is detained, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as President of Venezuela within this market's timeframe.

A military engagement which occurs will be considered to have ended once no qualifying incidents occur for 24 consecutive hours following the initial engagement. The relevant thirty day period will begin on the calendar day following this 24 hours. If multiple military engagements occur, the 30-day period will be counted from the first day following the ending of the most recent engagement.

If Maduro is removed from power prior to a qualifying military engagement occurring this market will immediately resolve to "No".

Note: If a qualifying military engagement occurs by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will remain open until either Maduro is removed from power or a thirty day period has passed with no subsequent military engagements occurring. 

The primary source of resolution for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

After the Ford's arrival: total rose to ~15,000 troops (reported November 30, December 1-2). Pre-window baseline: ~10,000 troops before Nov 15, with Ford CSG entering the SOUTHCOM area of responsibility on Nov 4 but not specifically the Caribbean Sea until Nov 16. No events rejected — the Nov 16 entry event is clearly within the window and well-documented.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The DVIDS official US military press release ([DVIDS, Nov 16](https://www.dvidshub.net/news/551190/gerald-r-ford-carrier-strike-group-enters-caribbean-sea)) states: 'The Gerald R. Ford Carrier Strike Group, centered on the USS Gerald R. Ford (CVN 78), entered the Caribbean Sea on November 16, 2025, after transiting the Anegada Passage.' The Ford carries 'over 4,000 Sailors.' The strike group includes three destroyers (each with ~280-330 personnel), putting combined crew at minimum 4,840+ and more likely 5,000+. The [AP (Nov 16)](https://apnews.com/article/aircraft-carrier-venezuela-trump-ford-strikes-drugs-241ea9e039d717b9f80f793922cb7cc9) reports the total deployment now includes 'approximately 12,000 sailors and Marines' in the operation — up from the pre-window ~10,000. The wbch.com article explicitly states 'The deployment includes 4,000 sailors and Marines, joining 10,000 troops already in the region.' This constitutes an additional 4,000+ from the Ford alone. The accompanying destroyers add ~1,000 more, giving a net additional deployment of approximately 5,000+ within the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: November 16, 2025 — the USS Gerald R. Ford Carrier Strike Group entered the Caribbean Sea, per official DVIDS press release and confirmed by AP, Newsweek, NDTV, and multiple other sources. This is within the resolution window (Nov 15–Dec 15, 2025).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying occurrence within the window exists. The Ford CSG entered the Caribbean Sea on November 16 — the earliest date confirmed. Before the window (pre-November 15), the US had ~10,000 troops already deployed; the Ford was in SOUTHCOM waters but had not entered the Caribbean Sea itself. The net additional deployment of ~5,000 occurred on/after November 16 when the Ford CSG entered the Caribbean.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: One source (Chosun.com, Nov 12) states the Ford entered SOUTHCOM 'area of responsibility' on November 11, but this is the broader SOUTHCOM region, not specifically the Caribbean Sea. DVIDS (official) confirms Caribbean Sea entry on November 16 — within the window. The pre-window troop count of ~10,000 is confirmed by multiple sources (Oct 17 Zero Hedge citing Indian Express, TASS Nov 1 citing 10,000 troops). The post-window arrival figure of ~15,000 is confirmed by New York Post (Nov 30), DW (Nov 29), Linda Ikeji (Dec 1), Times of India (Dec 2). The net addition of ~5,000 troops (from 10,000 to 15,000) is explicitly supported and the Ford CSG entry on November 16 accounts for this. Alternative interpretation: some might argue the question requires 'troops' as specifically Army soldiers/Marines rather than Navy sailors. However, the resolution criteria references 'troops' generically and all DoD/Pentagon reports use 'troops,' 'sailors and Marines,' and 'military personnel' interchangeably when counting total personnel. The resolution criteria does not limit to a specific military branch.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence clearly supports a Yes resolution. Within the resolution window (November 15–December 15, 2025): (1) The USS Gerald R. Ford Carrier Strike Group, carrying 4,000+ sailors plus ~1,000 more on three accompanying destroyers (totaling ~5,000+), entered the Caribbean Sea on November 16, 2025. (4) This explicitly satisfies the criterion of 'at least 5,000 additional troops to the Caribbean between 2025-11-15 and 2025-12-15.' subquestions.question: Will at least 5,000 federal workers accept the Deferred Resignation Program (DRP) between September 1, 2025, and October 1, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: The Trump administration has introduced the Deferred Resignation Program (DRP), which allows federal workers to resign while staying on paid leave for several months. This program is part of the administration's effort to slash the size of the U.S. government. According to the White House, about 75,000 federal workers accepted the administration's first offer [1]. The new programs have stipulations for certain employees, such as those planning to retire in the fall or working in critical positions [8]. subquestions.rationale: Tracking the number of federal workers who accept the DRP can provide insight into the administration's efforts to reduce the federal workforce, which could be an indicator of whether at least one Trump cabinet member will leave their position by December 31, 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition: At least 5,000 federal workers must ACCEPT the DRP between September 1-October 1, 2025, per OPM official data. Observable evidence: OPM published data showing ≥5,000 new DRP acceptances in that specific window. Key entities: OPM, DRP program. Threshold: 5,000 workers. Timing: September 1 - October 1, 2025 (acceptances, not departures).
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1. 'Deferred Resignation Program federal workers OPM September 2025' - to find any new DRP acceptances in September; 2. 'DRP federal employees acceptance numbers 2025' - to find total acceptance data; 3. 'OPM DRP second round September 2025 new acceptances' - to find September-specific new rounds; 4. 'federal employees deferred resignation program when did it open close deadline' - to establish DRP timeline; 5. 'EPA deferred resignation program September 2025 ORD' - to check EPA new round; 6. 'OPM website DRP data September 2025 federal workers accepted 5000' - to verify OPM data directly
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (A) 154,000 total DRP acceptances already counted by August 2025 (not new in September window); (B) ~103,000 formal resignations on September 30, 2025 (departure of previously accepted participants, not new acceptances); (C) DHS I&A second DRP round in September 2025 (targeting ~200 employees, far below 5,000); (D) EPA ORD new DRP round opened in late September 2025 (small sub-agency, likely far below 5,000). Events A and B rejected as they don't represent new acceptances in the September 1-October 1 window. Events C and D represent new September DRP activity but at far smaller scale than 5,000.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require new DRP acceptances during September 1-October 1, 2025, ≥5,000, per OPM official data. The evidence shows: (1) The main DRP ('Fork in the Road') accepted ~154,000 participants by August 2025, with acceptances predominantly in January-February 2025. (2) New agency-level DRP rounds in September 2025 targeted only hundreds of employees (DHS I&A: ~200; EPA ORD: small sub-agency of ~1,500 total staff with 326 already departed). (3) No OPM data explicitly reports 5,000+ new DRP acceptances during September 1-October 1, 2025. [Sources: Yahoo/OPM](https://ca.news.yahoo.com/why-100k-us-federal-workers-172500749.html), [E&E News EPA](https://www.eenews.net/articles/epa-re-ups-early-out-offers-for-research-staffers/), [Defense One DHS I&A](https://www.defenseone.com/policy/2025/10/dhs-intelligence-office-sent-deferred-resignation-offers-shed-staff-recent-months/408661/)
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No explicit OPM data timestamp found for new DRP acceptances during September 1-October 1, 2025 meeting the 5,000 threshold. The 154,000 figure (pre-September) and the 103,000 resignation figure (September 30 execution date, not new acceptances) are clearly timestamped but don't match criteria.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence of 5,000+ new DRP acceptances within the September 1-October 1, 2025 window was found in any source. The only documented new DRP rounds in September 2025 involve far fewer participants.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to find contradictory evidence: Searched for any agency announcing large-scale new DRP acceptances in September. Found only DHS I&A (~200 target) and EPA ORD (sub-agency). The IRS article (August 22) shows IRS stopped accepting new DRP volunteers. The resolution source (OPM website) was not directly accessible; no news articles cite specific OPM monthly data reports showing new September 2025 DRP acceptances of 5,000+. The question's framing suggests a new/second round DRP in September 2025, but all evidence indicates the main program was concluded by August 2025 at 154,000 total participants.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question asks specifically about new DRP acceptances in September 1-October 1, 2025. All evidence indicates: (1) The main DRP collected its 154,000 acceptances primarily in early 2025; (2) Second-round DRP offers in September 2025 were limited to small agency-specific programs targeting hundreds, not thousands; (3) No OPM published data confirms 5,000+ new DRP acceptances in the September window; (4) The resolution source (OPM website) does not appear to have published such data. The condition was not met, and the window closed October 1, 2025 without confirmed resolution. However, there is substantial ambiguity about whether the question is asking about 'acceptances' (signing the DRP) vs. 'departures' (September 30 resignations), and whether OPM published specific September-window data. Given the lack of direct evidence from OPM specifically tracking September 1-October 1 acceptances, this is not resolvable with certainty.

Only agreements that are publicly announced and acknowledged by both the U.S. and Russia will qualify. The agreement must pertain to nuclear arms control or limitation—such as a treaty, framework, or memorandum—addressing matters including (but not limited to) nuclear warheads, delivery systems, verification mechanisms, or strategic stability.

An extension, amendment, or replacement of the New START treaty will qualify, provided it is publicly announced as a concluded agreement by both parties within the time frame. Exploratory discussions or stated intent to extend without a finalized agreement will not qualify.

Agreements that include both the United States and Russia as named parties—whether bilateral or as part of a broader multilateral framework—will qualify, provided the agreement directly addresses nuclear arms control.

The agreement does not need to be ratified or implemented for this market to resolve "Yes"; a formal announcement of a concluded agreement is sufficient.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official statements from the U.S. government (e.g., the White House, State Department) and/or the Russian Federation (e.g., the Kremlin, Ministry of Foreign Affairs). However, a clear and overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming that such an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will Russia and the US announce exploratory talks on a new nuclear arms control agreement by November 15, 2025?
subquestions.background_information:
The current state of nuclear arms control is uncertain, with the New START treaty set to expire in February 2026.
According to [1], Russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed a one-year extension of the treaty, but the US has yet to respond.
In [2], Putin's proposal is seen as a strategic calculation to project responsibility and shift blame to Washington if the offer is rejected.
However, [3] suggests that a consensus on strategic stability is essential for further nuclear arms reduction.
This background information highlights the need for exploratory talks on a new agreement.
Sources:
  UK & French arsenals must be part of any US-Russia arms control deal, says Kremlin (https://www.firstpost.com/world/uk-french-arsenals-must-be-part-of-any-us-russia-arms-control-deal-says-kremlin-10492166.html)
  Cold War Echoes (https://www.thenation.com/article/world/us-russia-nuclear-disarmament/)
  Nuclear disarmament process requires consensus on strategic stability (https://tass.com/world/1336156)
subquestions.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves Yes if both Russia and the US publicly announce exploratory talks on a new nuclear arms control agreement between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-15, 11:59 PM ET.
Resolution will be based on official statements from the White House and/or the Kremlin.
If the US or Russia announces exploratory talks, but does not meet the specified date range, the question will resolve to No.
If there is no announcement of exploratory talks, the question will resolve to No.
Source: Official statements from the White House and/or the Kremlin.
URL: https://www.whitehouse.gov/
https://kremlin.ru/
subquestions.rationale:
This question is relevant to the ultimate question because exploratory talks on a new nuclear arms control agreement could be an indicator of a potential deal between Russia and the US.
If both parties announce exploratory talks, it could indicate a willingness to negotiate a new agreement, which could be a positive sign for the ultimate question.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: BOTH Russia and the US must publicly announce exploratory talks on a NEW nuclear arms control agreement between 2025-10-31T00:00:00Z and 2025-11-15T23:59:59Z. Observable evidence: Official statements from the White House AND/OR the Kremlin explicitly announcing exploratory talks. Key entities: White House, Kremlin, both US and Russia must participate. This is not about extending an existing treaty (New START) but a NEW agreement.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Russia US nuclear arms control agreement exploratory talks 2025' (Oct 31–Nov 15) to find direct evidence; 2) 'White House Kremlin nuclear weapons treaty announcement November 2025' to find official statements; 3) 'US Russia announce new nuclear arms control talks agreement November 2025' to find joint announcements; 4) 'Rubio Lavrov nuclear agreement exploratory talks announcement' to find specific diplomatic announcements; 5) 'Russia offers US nuclear talks in bid to ease tensions' to find any offers or announcements.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (A) Trump's Nov 5 statement that US/Russia/China 'may be working on a denuclearization plan' — rejected because Kremlin explicitly denied expert-level talks were underway (Peskov, Oct 30); (B) Russia's offer of nuclear talks (Nov 11) to discuss US concerns about secret testing — rejected because this was a unilateral offer by Russia about discussing test-related allegations, not a joint announcement of exploratory talks on a new arms control agreement, and no US acceptance was found; (C) Russia urging US to extend New START (Nov 11–13) — rejected because this concerns extension of existing treaty, not a new agreement, and the US had not responded; (D) Lavrov's statement that US is 'considering' Putin's New START extension proposal — rejected because this is about an existing treaty extension, not a new agreement, and 'considering' ≠ announcing exploratory talks.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No candidate event exactly satisfies the resolution criteria. The criteria requires: (1) BOTH countries publicly announce, (2) exploratory talks, (3) on a NEW nuclear arms control agreement, (4) within the window. [TASS Nov 13](https://tass.com/politics/2043379) explicitly states 'the United States has not yet responded to Moscow's proposals.' [TASS Nov 5](https://tass.com/world/2039799) states Peskov confirmed 'Moscow and Washington are not currently engaged in expert-level talks on nuclear disarmament.' Russia's offer of talks (Nov 11) per [The News International](https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/1357258-russia-offers-nuclear-talks-with-us-to-defuse-rising-tensions) was about discussing test allegations, not a new arms control framework. No White House announcement of any kind was found.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No exact timestamp of a qualifying event (joint announcement of exploratory talks on a new nuclear arms control agreement) could be extracted because no such event occurred within the window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence was found within the window. The search confirms that as of November 13, 2025, the US had not responded to Russia's proposals, and no joint announcement was made.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: Multiple sources (TASS Nov 13, Newsweek Nov 9, Washington Times Nov 11, RT Nov 12) consistently confirm that: (1) the US had not substantively responded to Russian nuclear arms control proposals; (2) the Kremlin denied expert-level talks were underway; (3) tensions around nuclear testing dominated the period rather than cooperative talks. Trump's vague 'maybe working on denuclearization' was not an official announcement of exploratory talks, and Russia did not confirm it. The resolution criteria specifically require a new agreement, not an extension of New START.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. No qualifying event occurred within the window (Oct 31–Nov 15, 2025). The evidence shows: (1) nuclear tensions escalated rather than produced cooperative announcements; (2) Russia made unilateral proposals for New START extension, which the US was 'considering' but had not accepted or responded to; (3) Kremlin explicitly denied expert-level nuclear disarmament talks with the US; (4) no official White House announcement of exploratory talks on a new nuclear arms control agreement was found. The window closed on November 15, 2025 without the required joint announcement being made.

question: Will Russia enter Borova by December 31?
description:

Territory will be considered captured if any part of Borova is shaded under a below specified layer on the ISW map (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/36a7f6a6f5a9448496de641cf64bd375) by the resolution date. Otherwise, the market will resolve to “No”.

For any change on the ISW map to qualify for this market’s resolution, the relevant shading indicating Russian control must persist through the next full ISW daily update cycle. If ISW skips a day, shading must persist until the next finalized ISW update is published, regardless of the date. Any continuous shading which reflects either "Assessed Russian Infiltration Areas in Ukraine", “Assessed Russian Control”, “Assessed Russian Advance In Ukraine”, or “Assessed Russian Gains in the Past 24 Hours” will qualify. 

Once a qualifying condition is met, any subsequent loss of control will not be considered towards the resolution of this market.

If Russia comes into control of the specified territory as a result of a negotiated settlement, this will qualify for a 'Yes' resolution, regardless of whether it is shaded red in the ISW map. However, an announcement of a negotiated settlement that gives Russia de jure control will not qualify. Actual control must be established.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the ISW Ukraine map. If the ISW map is rendered unavailable, information from DeepStateMap (https://deepstatemap.live/) may be used. If information from both the ISW and DeepStateMap are rendered permanently unavailable, a consensus of credible reporting may be used.

Note: Any temporary glitches or errors in the map will not be considered.

Multiple DeepState-confirmed captures exist within the window: [UAWire Dec 1](https://uawire.org/analysts-say-russian-forces-capture-promin-and-vysoke-advancing-near-pokrovsk-myrnohrad-and-hulyaipole) explicitly references DeepState map for Promin and Vysoke captures (2 villages). [Ukrainska Pravda Dec 9](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2025/12/09/8010993/) reports DeepState confirmed 5 more villages on Dec 8. Criteria fully matched - well over 2 villages confirmed on DeepState map within window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Earliest clear DeepState-confirmed captures within the window: December 1, 2025 - Promin and Vysoke (2 villages) per UAWire citing DeepState map context. December 2, 2025 - Kozatske explicitly 'marked in red on [DeepState] map' per Ukrainska Pravda. The resolution threshold of 2 villages is definitively met by December 1-2, 2025.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The Nov 28 articles reference Zelenyi Hai capture (which DeepState reported Nov 27 - just before the window), and DeepState also reported Russian advances near Myrnohrad on Nov 28. The Promin and Vysoke captures (Dec 1) are clearly within the window and represent the first unambiguous pair of villages captured within the window per DeepState-referenced data. No earlier qualifying occurrence within the window (before Dec 1) that meets the 2-village threshold has been found.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: Some Russian MoD claims were disputed by Ukraine (e.g., Klynove, Kupiansk, Pokrovsk, Siversk). However, Kozatske and the Dec 8 villages (Lysivka, Sukhyi Yar, Hnativka, Rih, Novopavlivka) were confirmed by DeepState itself - a Ukrainian analytical group with access to military sources - not by Russian MoD alone. The Dec 2 Ukrainska Pravda article explicitly cites DeepState map red markings. The Dec 9 Ukrainska Pravda article explicitly cites DeepState confirming 5 village captures. Multiple independent sources corroborate these DeepState findings. No contradictory evidence found regarding these specific DeepState-confirmed captures.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence firmly supports resolution = Yes. DeepState confirmed multiple village captures within the Nov 28 - Dec 15, 2025 window. The minimum threshold of 2 villages is met well before December 15. The earliest confirmed DeepState-map-marked pair of villages within the window is December 1-2, 2025 (Promin/Vysoke on Dec 1 per DeepState-referenced analysis, and Kozatske explicitly marked red on DeepState map on Dec 2). By December 8, DeepState confirmed 5 additional village captures. Resolution datetime = December 2, 2025 (when DeepState explicitly marked Kozatske in red, with earlier references to Promin/Vysoke from Dec 1 also using DeepState map data).

question: Will Ukraine agree to cede territory to Russia in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a deal in which Ukraine agrees to cede any territory under its control at the time of the agreement is reached between the Russian Federation and Ukraine by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The deal must be a publicly announced mutual agreement or otherwise confirmed by an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting.  

If such an agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to "Yes", regardless of if/when the agreement goes into effect.

Only territory ceded as part of a diplomatic process or agreement will qualify. 

If a territorial adjustment is made as part of a mutual border demarcation process or technical boundary agreement that does not materially alter de facto control or reflect a broader territorial concession, it will not qualify for a 'Yes' resolution unless it is reported as a territorial concession by a consensus of credible reporting.

Any agreement which cedes de facto military control of territory held by Ukraine will qualify regardless of whether Ukraine formally maintains its claim to sovereignty. For example, the 1999 Kumanovo Military Technical Agreement, in which Yugoslavia agreed to pull military forces out of Kosovo but did not recognize Kosovo’s autonomy or independence would qualify for a 'Yes' resolution.

The primary resolution source for this market will be an official announcement by Ukraine and/or the Russian Federation, however, an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting confirming an agreement has been reached will also qualify.

subquestions.question: Will the US Secretary of State, Antony Blinken, or equivalent, publicly acknowledge Russia's control over any Ukrainian territory in a diplomatic meeting or press conference between October 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025?

Key distinctions: (1) the actor must be the Secretary of State specifically (not Trump, Witkoff, or other officials); (2) the acknowledgment must be explicit — not inferred from peace proposals or ceasefire language; (3) it must be in a diplomatic meeting or press conference setting; (4) recorded by a reputable source.

Query 4: 'Secretary of State Rubio Ukraine territory cession statement recognition' — looking for explicit recognition language. Query 7: 'Rubio press conference statement Ukraine Russia-controlled demarcation line territorial recognition' — explicit criteria match. subquestions.background_information: The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) announced that 2025 is on track to be among the warmest years on record, likely ranking second or third (1). evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition for Yes: NOAA reports 2025 global mean surface air temperature ≥1.42°C above pre-industrial levels by January 1, 2026. evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) Copernicus/C3S Dec 9, 2025 report: Jan–Nov 2025 average = 1.48°C above pre-industrial (incomplete year). (2) WWA Dec 30–31 reports: 2025 among three hottest years, three-year average exceeds 1.5°C, but no specific 2025 annual temperature stated within window. (3) Hindustan Times Jan 3, 2026 (outside window): Projects ~1.4°C for full year 2025 based on WMO. (4) WMO Jan 14, 2026 (outside window): Confirms 1.44°C ± 0.13°C for 2025. No NOAA report for full-year 2025 was issued within the window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: Within the resolution window (Dec 30–Jan 1, 2026): No NOAA annual global temperature report for full-year 2025 was published. The fallback condition ('consensus of credible reporting') applies. Within the window, credible reporting includes: (a) Copernicus Jan–Nov data at 1.48°C [News18](https://www.news18.com/agency-feeds/2025-set-to-become-2nd-or-3rd-warmest-year-on-record-copernicus-9759903.html), but this is incomplete (11 months only); (b) WWA reports 2025 among three hottest on record but give no specific annual temperature within the window; (c) WMO projected full-year ~1.4°C per Hindustan Times Jan 3 (outside window). After the window, NOAA specifically reported 1.3°C [FOX29](https://www.fox29.com/news/2025-hottest-years-record-data), while WMO reported 1.44°C [UN News](https://news.un.org/en/story/2026/01/1166758). These post-window figures conflict: NOAA at 1.3°C (below threshold) vs. WMO at 1.44°C (above threshold).
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No exact timestamp within the Dec 30–Jan 1 window exists for a NOAA report of 2025 annual global temperature. The WMO announcement that it would release consolidated data on January 14, 2026, confirms no such data was available by January 1, 2026 [MirageNews](https://www.miragenews.com/wmo-to-reveal-2025-global-temperature-data-1599230/). Cannot extract a qualifying timestamp within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Post-window evidence is highly relevant to resolution via consensus fallback. NOAA (per FOX29, Jan 16, 2026) reported 2025 at 1.3°C above pre-industrial — BELOW the 1.42°C threshold. WMO (Jan 14, 2026) reported 1.44°C — ABOVE the threshold. This discrepancy is due to different methodologies and baselines used by different agencies. Importantly, the resolution criteria specifically names NOAA, and post-window NOAA data shows 1.3°C. Within the window itself, no NOAA data for full-year 2025 was available. The Jan–Nov Copernicus figure of 1.48°C does not represent full-year 2025 data. The consensus available by Jan 1 was incomplete (no full-year 2025 data from any agency). Given that the specific NOAA figure (the named agency in the criteria) reported 1.3°C after the window and the WMO reported 1.44°C, a definitive consensus is unclear and potentially contradictory.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution criteria requires NOAA specifically to report ≥1.42°C for 2025, OR (as a fallback) consensus of credible reporting to confirm this. Within the Dec 30–Jan 1 window, NOAA had not released its 2025 annual global temperature. The fallback consensus within the window is also not definitive — only partial-year data (11 months at 1.48°C) was available. Post-window data shows NOAA specifically reported 1.3°C (below threshold) while WMO reported 1.44°C (above threshold). The NOAA figure (1.3°C) is below 1.42°C and would resolve No. However, this NOAA figure was released outside the resolution window and the question specifies resolution by January 1, 2026. Given (1) no NOAA report within the window, (2) ambiguity in the consensus fallback, and (3) conflicting post-window figures from different agencies, this question cannot be resolved with certainty. The evidence is indirect and outside the window for the specific NOAA requirement.
