If U.S. President Donald Trump visits North Korea between August 4 and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Yes". Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purpose of this market, a "visit" is defined as Trump physically entering the terrestrial or maritime territory of the listed country. Whether or not Trump enters the country's airspace during the timeframe of this market will have no bearing on a positive resolution.

The primary resolution source for this information will be official information from government of the United States of America, official information from Trump or released by his verified social media accounts (e.g. https://twitter.com/POTUS), however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

subquestions.question: Will Donald Trump make any public statements or gestures indicating a possible visit to North Korea between October 1 and October 31, 2025?
subquestions.background_information: There has been ongoing speculation about a potential visit by Donald Trump to North Korea. In recent months, Trump has expressed his desire to meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and has praised Kim's leadership. South Korean President Lee Jae Myung has also expressed interest in arranging a meeting between the two leaders. However, no concrete plans have been announced. A public statement or gesture from Trump indicating a possible visit would be a significant development and could be an early indicator of a potential visit.
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Trump makes a public statement or gesture indicating a possible visit to North Korea on or after October 1, 2025, and before November 1, 2025, as reported by a reputable news source such as AP, Reuters, or the New York Times. The resolution criteria will be based on official Trump social media accounts, official government announcements, or credible reporting from established news organizations. For example, if Trump tweets or posts on Truth Social about meeting with Kim Jong Un, or if a government announcement is made about a potential visit, this question will resolve Yes. If no such statement or gesture is made during the specified time period, this question will resolve No.
subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because it taps into the same underlying dynamics of Trump's interest in visiting North Korea. If Trump makes public statements or gestures indicating a possible visit, it could be an early indicator that a visit is being seriously considered, which would be a significant development in the lead-up to the ultimate question's resolution deadline in December 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required: Trump makes a public statement or gesture indicating a possible visit to North Korea (or meeting with Kim Jong Un) between Oct 1-31, 2025. Must be reported by reputable news sources (AP, Reuters, NYT, or equivalent). Observable evidence: official statements, social media posts, government announcements, or credible reporting of Trump expressing openness to visit/meet Kim Jong Un in this period.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Trump North Korea visit Kim Jong Un October 2025' — to find direct statements about visit/meeting. Query 2: 'Trump statement North Korea meeting October 2025' — to find formal statements. Query 3: 'Trump 100 percent open Kim Jong Un meeting statement October 2025' — to find specific phrasing. Query 4: 'Trump North Korea visit cross DMZ October 2025' — to find gesture toward visiting North Korea. Query 5: 'Trump North Korea Kim Jong Un open to meeting October 1 2025' — to find earliest occurrence in window.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Multiple qualifying events found: (1) Oct 1, 2025: White House official says Trump open to meeting Kim 'without any preconditions' (Yonhap/Korea JoongAng Daily); (2) Oct 25, 2025: Trump personally states '100% open' to meeting Kim during Asia trip, says 'put out the word' (AP, Japan Times); (3) Oct 27, 2025: Trump says he could extend South Korea visit to meet Kim, 'I can be right over there' (AFP/Chosun); (4) Oct 27-29: Multiple reiterations. No events were rejected as they all clearly satisfy the criteria.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: CONFIRMED: Multiple sources directly match criteria. [AP News Oct 24](https://apnews.com/article/trump-north-korea-kim-apec-a4e1a588eb1786250beac5a5e4e876ec) reports 'Trump has expressed interest in reviving diplomacy with Kim, citing their good personal memories.' [Korea JoongAng Daily Oct 1](https://koreajoongangdaily.joins.com/news/2025-10-01/national/northKorea/Trump-remains-open-to-talks-with-NK-leader-Kim-without-any-preconditions-White-House/2412274) reports White House official stating Trump open to meeting Kim 'without any preconditions.' [Japan Times Oct 25](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2025/10/25/asia-pacific/politics/trump-kim-north-korea-meeting/) reports Trump said 'If you want to put out the word, I'm open to it' about meeting at DMZ. [Chosun Oct 27](https://www.chosun.com/english/world-en/2025/10/27/UFXCWILIYNHXRO5W72TOSA6RBY/) reports Trump said 'I can be right over there' about crossing into North Korea.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: First qualifying event: October 1, 2025 — White House official's public statement that Trump is open to meeting Kim Jong Un 'without any preconditions,' reported by Yonhap News Agency and Korea JoongAng Daily on October 1, 2025. This is within the resolution window (Oct 1-31, 2025).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The October 1, 2025 White House statement is the first qualifying event within the window. Pre-window statements (August 25, September 30) exist but fall outside the Oct 1-31 window. The October 1 statement by a White House official is explicitly within the window and matches criteria.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence checked: By Oct 29, Trump said 'we weren't able to work out timing' suggesting the actual meeting didn't happen — but the resolution criteria only requires a *statement or gesture* indicating a *possible* visit, not an actual visit. The many explicit statements of openness fully satisfy criteria regardless of whether a meeting actually occurred. Multiple high-quality sources (AP, Japan Times, Yonhap, AFP) corroborate the statements. No conflicting evidence about whether Trump made these statements.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution: YES. Trump made explicit public statements indicating a possible visit to North Korea/meeting with Kim Jong Un multiple times in October 2025. The first qualifying event occurred on October 1, 2025, when a White House official stated Trump is open to meeting Kim 'without any preconditions,' reported by Yonhap News Agency (a reputable news source). This is directly and explicitly within the Oct 1-31, 2025 window. Additional qualifying events occurred on Oct 25 (Trump personally said '100% open'), Oct 27 ('I can be right over there'), all reported by AP, Japan Times, AFP, and other reputable outlets. All evidence requirements are satisfied.

question: Tesla launches unsupervised full self driving (FSD) by June 30?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Tesla publicly releases an unsupervised Full Self-Driving capability that satisfies all of the following criteria by June 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

1. Tesla (or Elon Musk) must label the feature “Full Self-Driving” or use an equivalent name indicating no requirement for human intervention.

2. The system must operate on public roads without a human driver present or required to oversee its performance. In practice, this means either:
- The vehicle runs with no one in the driver’s seat, or
- The vehicle operates in a mode where no occupant is expected to monitor or intervene.

3. Tesla or any Tesla-affiliated entity must make the unsupervised Full Self-Driving capability broadly accessible either through a robo-taxi or ride-hailing service open to the public, or inclusion as a standard or optional feature on newly sold Tesla vehicles, or a software update that enables unsupervised operation in current vehicles.

Any mode that requires a licensed driver to be seated in the vehicle, or for a human (on-site or remote) to continuously supervise the driving performance or remain ready to intervene at any moment, will not qualify. However, remote monitoring that does not involve continuous supervision or expectation of real-time intervention—for example, oversight limited to emergency response—will not disqualify the service.

This market’s resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

subquestions.question: Will Tesla release a ride-hailing service with human drivers in the San Francisco Bay Area before 2025-09-30?
subquestions.background_information: Tesla has already launched a taxi service in San Francisco with human drivers, but the company is awaiting regulatory approval for its autonomous 'robotaxis'. The service is currently restricted to 'friends and family of employees' and 'select members of the public' (Source: <https://www.breitbart.com/tech/2025/07/29/not-so-robo-elon-musk-introduces-tesla-taxi-service-with-human-drivers-in-san-francisco/>). subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if Tesla publicly announces a ride-hailing service with human drivers in the San Francisco Bay Area between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30, and confirms that the service will operate with human drivers present. Otherwise, this question resolves to No.
subquestions.rationale: A ride-hailing service with human drivers in the San Francisco Bay Area could be an indicator of Tesla's progress towards launching unsupervised Full Self-Driving (FSD) capabilities. If Tesla is able to launch a ride-hailing service with human drivers, it may indicate that the company is close to obtaining regulatory approval for its autonomous 'robotaxis'.

evidence.step1_decompose: Required condition: Tesla must PUBLICLY ANNOUNCE a ride-hailing service with human drivers in the San Francisco Bay Area between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30. The announcement must be within this window, and must confirm human drivers. Key entity: Tesla. Key geography: SF Bay Area. Key timing: September 1-30, 2025.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Tesla ride-hailing San Francisco Bay Area human drivers 2025' (Sept 1-30) to find announcements; 2) 'Tesla robotaxi launch announcement San Francisco 2025' (Sept 1-30) to find public announcements; 3) 'Tesla ride-hailing San Francisco Bay Area human drivers launch July 2025' (July-Sept) to find original launch date; 4) 'Tesla robotaxi San Francisco announcement public service September 2025' to find any new Sept announcements.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (A) Tesla launched ride-hailing service in SF Bay Area on July 31, 2025 — OUTSIDE the resolution window (predates Sept 1). (B) Tesla opened public iOS app on September 3-4, 2025 — within window but this is an app/access expansion, not the original announcement of the service. (C) Reuters/USA Today reporting on Sept 22-23 about regulatory alarm — not a Tesla announcement. (D) Tesla reportedly operating pre-arranged human-driven trips under limousine permit in Bay Area — operations began July 31. Rejected: Event (A) is outside window. Events (B), (C), (D) do not constitute an original announcement of a new ride-hailing service with human drivers — they are continuations/expansions of the July 31 launch.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria requires Tesla to 'publicly announce a ride-hailing service with human drivers in the San Francisco Bay Area between 2025-09-01 and 2025-09-30.' The original announcement and launch of human-driven ride-hailing in the SF Bay Area occurred on July 31, 2025, per [MarketWatch](https://www.marketwatch.com/story/tesla-starts-ride-hailing-service-in-the-bay-area-its-not-a-robotaxi-yet-63678f7d), [Fast Company](https://www.fastcompany.com/91377909/tesla-launches-ride-hailing-in-san-francisco-but-theres-no-mention-of-self-driving-robotaxis), [Quartz](https://qz.com/tesla-launched-ride-hailing-san-francisco-california-robotaxis), and [Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/tesla-says-robotaxi-app-open-to-public-users-4223299). This is BEFORE the resolution window. No NEW announcement of a separate/new ride-hailing service with human drivers was made in September 2025. The September events (iOS app public launch, regulatory news) are continuations of the existing service, not a new announcement.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Original Tesla Bay Area human-driver ride-hailing launch: July 31, 2025 — outside the September 1-30 window. September events: iOS app public launch September 3-4, 2025 (within window but not a new service announcement). Regulatory alarm reporting: September 22-23, 2025 (within window but not a Tesla announcement of a new service).
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: The first occurrence of Tesla announcing/launching ride-hailing with human drivers in SF Bay Area was July 31, 2025 — confirmed by multiple high-quality sources. This is definitively BEFORE the September 1, 2025 start of the resolution window.
evidence.step7_verification: Checked for any new, separate Tesla announcement in September 2025 of a ride-hailing service with human drivers. The September news cycle focused on: (1) public iOS app launch expanding access to existing service, (2) regulatory scrutiny about permits, (3) airport permit discussions. None of these constitute a new public announcement of a ride-hailing service with human drivers in the Bay Area — the service was already announced and operating since July 31, 2025. No contradictory evidence found regarding the July 31 launch date.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The resolution criteria requires the announcement to occur between September 1-30, 2025. Tesla's public announcement and launch of ride-hailing with human drivers in the SF Bay Area occurred on July 31, 2025 — before the resolution window. No new/separate announcement of such a service was made in September 2025. Therefore, the question resolves No. The window closed on September 30, 2025 without a qualifying announcement within the specified period.

question: U.S. agrees to give Ukraine security guarantee in 2025?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States formally commits to giving Ukraine a security guarantee, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed deal between the Trump administration and the Government of Ukraine which creates a binding obligation for the United States to defend or directly intervene on Ukraine’s behalf, by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

A qualifying “security guarantee” requires language that is equivalent in character to a NATO Article 5–style mutual defense commitment: the United States must commit to responding militarily if Ukraine is attacked, or otherwise guarantee Ukraine’s defense through binding defense obligations. Examples of qualifying language include commitments modeled on the US treaties with Japan, South Korea, or the Philippines, or NATO's Article 5 instrument, which obligates the United States to “act to meet the common danger” through military force if an ally is attacked. Cooperative frameworks, capacity-building measures, consultative mechanisms, or nonbinding pledges will not qualify. 

Examples of non-qualifying arrangements include the June 13, 2024 US–Ukraine bilateral security agreement, the Taiwan Relations Act, or G7/EU “security arrangements” that provide support or consultation but stop short of binding defense guarantees.

A qualifying agreement must be jointly announced and finalized, and take the form of a treaty, executive agreement, memorandum of understanding, joint declaration, or equivalent written instrument. Announcements which are statements of intent, contingent, exploratory, or otherwise not indicative of a formalized policy will not count. 

The primary resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

The concept of an 'article 5-style' security guarantee, similar to Nato's collective defence provision, has been suggested as a possible solution for Ukraine's security concerns [8]. However, the US needs to reaffirm the bilateral US-Ukraine security agreement of June 2024, and the Europeans need to convert their agreements with Ukraine into an effective security and defence mechanism [8]. President Trump has previously expressed openness to providing Ukraine with security guarantees, but clarified that the United States would not deploy ground troops, only consider air support [9].

subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if President Trump publicly announces a written instrument equivalent to a NATO Article 5-style mutual defense commitment with Ukraine between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-15, as reported by a credible news source (e.g. The New York Times, BBC, etc.). subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because a public announcement of a written instrument equivalent to a NATO Article 5-style mutual defense commitment with Ukraine would be a significant step towards providing Ukraine with a security guarantee. If President Trump makes such an announcement, it would indicate a strong commitment to Ukraine's security and would likely have a significant impact on the ultimate question of whether the US agrees to give Ukraine a security guarantee in 2025.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Trump must publicly announce a written instrument equivalent to NATO Article 5 (mutual defense treaty) with Ukraine between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-15. Observable evidence: credible news reporting of such announcement. Key entities: Trump, Ukraine, written defense commitment. Threshold: Must be equivalent to Article 5 (attack on one = attack on all), must be written, must be publicly announced by Trump.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'Trump NATO Article 5 mutual defense commitment Ukraine 2025' - to find the specific announcement. 2) 'Trump Ukraine security guarantee written agreement defense treaty' - to find bilateral defense agreements. 3) 'Trump Zelensky Article 5 equivalent Ukraine defense commitment signed' - to find any signing event. 4) 'Ukraine peace deal security guarantee Trump November 2025' - to find related diplomatic developments.
evidence.step3_event_detection: No candidate events matching resolution criteria were found. Search results revealed: (a) Trump/Hegseth explicitly stated the US would NOT extend Article 5 guarantees to allied troops in Ukraine (February 2025); (b) The Trump administration withdrew troops from Europe (Romania, Germany, Poland) within the window; (c) Peace negotiations were ongoing but focused on ceasefire talks, not mutual defense treaties; (d) Security guarantees being discussed were by EU/Canada, not by Trump bilaterally with Ukraine; (e) Ukraine is not a NATO member and no bilateral US-Ukraine defense treaty was reported.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No articles from the resolution window (2025-10-31 to 2025-11-15) report Trump announcing any written instrument equivalent to a NATO Article 5-style mutual defense commitment with Ukraine. The [Telegraph article](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/2025/11/01/is-trump-actually-making-the-world-safer/) confirmed Trump reaffirmed Article 5 for NATO members (not Ukraine) at the Hague Summit. The [Zero Hedge article](https://www.zerohedge.com/geopolitical/germany-dodges-russias-offer-non-aggression-guarantee-nato-eu) and [France's troop deployment article](https://www.zerohedge.com/geopolitical/frances-plans-deploy-troops-ukraine-risk-sparking-major-crisis) both indicate the US explicitly stated it would NOT extend Article 5 guarantees to troops in Ukraine.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: No qualifying event found, so no timestamp to extract.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying occurrence found within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Multiple searches confirm no Trump-Ukraine mutual defense commitment announcement occurred in the window. The evidence strongly contradicts such an occurrence: (1) Trump administration was reducing military presence in Europe; (2) Hegseth explicitly declined to extend Article 5 to troops in Ukraine; (3) Diplomatic focus was on ceasefire talks, not defense treaties; (4) No credible news source (NYT, BBC, Reuters, etc.) reported any such announcement; (5) The ongoing peace negotiation context makes such an announcement highly unlikely per all reporting.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. No evidence was found of Trump announcing a written instrument equivalent to a NATO Article 5-style mutual defense commitment with Ukraine between 2025-10-31 and 2025-11-15. The window closed without any such announcement, and all contextual evidence strongly indicates this did not occur.

However, the company is confident to approach its second flight, with Spectrum launch vehicles 2 and 3 already in production (Source: [4] Isar Aerospace raises €150mn to strengthen Europe's launch capabilities, The Next Web, 2025-06-25, https://thenextweb.com/science/2025/06/25/isar-aerospace-launch-capabilities/).

question: Foreign intervention in Gaza in 2025?
description:

Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The foreign personnel must physically enter the terrestrial territory of the Gaza Strip to qualify. Entering the maritime territory, as occurred during the US’s attempt to construct a floating pier in 2024, or entering the airspace will not qualify. 

Entering Israeli controlled buffer zones will not qualify.  

Egyptian or other forces operating solely along the Egyptian/Gaza border will not qualify regardless of if they cross the border. 

Foreign personnel carrying out individual special operations, diplomatic missions, or solely humanitarian operations will not qualify.

Qualifying deployments must involve active-duty personnel of at least one foreign state or international institution (e.g., the UN or multinational missions) who are officially sent to Gaza for an operational role (e.g., peacekeeping, convoy escort, detention, logistical support). To qualify, the deployment must occur within the specified timeframe; mere announcements will not suffice.

On the other hand, if foreign troops do not enter Gaza, it could be a sign that the ultimate question's outcome is less likely.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: Foreign troops (including US and other international forces) must physically enter the terrestrial territory of the Gaza Strip between Oct 16 and Nov 15, 2025. Observable evidence: news reports or official statements confirming foreign military/troop entry into Gaza territory. Key entities: US forces, Egyptian forces, Turkish forces, international stabilization force. The resolution explicitly excludes coordination centers in Israel.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'foreign troops US military enter Gaza 2025' (general search); 2) 'international forces Gaza Strip ground troops October November 2025' (broader search); 3) 'US CENTCOM commander Gaza visit troops ground October 2025' (looking for CENTCOM activities); 4) 'international stabilization force deployed entered Gaza troops November 2025' (checking ISF deployment); 5) 'Egyptian search rescue team troops Gaza Strip entry November 2025' (checking Egyptian team); 6) 'Egyptian technical team hostage recovery bodies Gaza ceasefire entered' (specific Egyptian team entry); 7) 'Egyptian military forces soldiers entered Gaza Strip October 25 26 2025' (confirmation of Egyptian entry); 8) 'Red Cross international personnel Gaza ceasefire monitoring October 2025' (checking ICRC); 9) 'Egyptian forces OR Egyptian military OR Egyptian army entered Gaza hostage bodies 2025' (confirming military nature)
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events identified: (1) Egyptian team entered Gaza on Oct 25-26, 2025 to search for hostage remains — multiple sources confirmed, including AFP, Times of Israel, France24, TASS, i24NEWS, The Independent; (2) US forces stationed at Kiryat Gat, Israel (NOT in Gaza) — explicitly NOT qualifying under resolution criteria; (3) Turkish 81-member AFAD team at Egyptian border since Oct 17 — blocked by Israel, never entered; (4) International Stabilization Force — still being planned/negotiated, no deployment confirmed in window; (5) US MQ-9 drones flying over Gaza — aerial, not terrestrial; (6) Red Cross accompanying Hamas in Gaza — ICRC is humanitarian, not troops. The Egyptian team is the primary candidate for 'foreign troops' entering Gaza.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution requires 'foreign troops, including US and other international forces' entering the 'terrestrial territory of the Gaza Strip.' The Egyptian team that entered Gaza on Oct 25-26, 2025 is described in multiple sources as including military personnel: (a) The Times of Israel [https://www.timesofisrael.com/daily-briefing-oct-26-day-751-egyptians-enter-gaza-as-us-drones-fly-above-strip/] states 'Egyptian military forces and heavy equipment entered the Gaza Strip'; (b) TASS [https://tass.com/world/2035261] reports 'Egyptian rescuers and military specialists' and 'Egyptian field engineers also participating in mine-clearing operations'; (c) AFP footage confirmed Egyptian military sources; (d) Firstpost [https://www.firstpost.com/world/israel-allows-red-cross-and-egyptian-teams-to-recover-bodies-of-hostages-in-gaza-13945283.html] says 'non-military personnel' which creates ambiguity. However, the majority of sources describe them as military in nature. The Israel AFP directly cited 'Egyptian military sources' confirming the convoy. TASS described 'military specialists' and 'field engineers' in 'mine-clearing operations.' This appears to satisfy the criterion of 'foreign troops' or 'international forces' physically entering Gaza's terrestrial territory.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: Multiple sources confirm the Egyptian team entered Gaza on October 25, 2025 (initial entry per Times of Israel: 'entered the Gaza Strip on October 25, 2025') and October 26 overnight (AFP footage showing vehicles in Khan Yunis). The i24NEWS report dated October 25, 2025 at 16:46 confirms entry. This is within the Oct 16 – Nov 15, 2025 window.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No earlier qualifying events within the window (Oct 16 – Nov 15) were found. The Turkish team attempted to enter but was blocked. No US troops entered Gaza. The Egyptian team's entry on Oct 25-26, 2025 appears to be the first occurrence of foreign forces entering Gaza within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: Contradictory evidence: (1) Firstpost [https://www.firstpost.com/world/israel-allows-red-cross-and-egyptian-teams-to-recover-bodies-of-hostages-in-gaza-13945283.html] describes the Egyptian team as 'non-military personnel,' which could argue against the 'troops' characterization. (2) The resolution criteria explicitly mentions 'troops' and 'forces' — the Egyptian technical rescue team may be characterized as a civil/humanitarian mission rather than military. However, TASS explicitly references 'military specialists' and 'field engineers' conducting mine-clearing, and the Times of Israel headline says 'Egyptian military forces.' (3) US troops: VP Vance (Oct 21), Pentagon (Nov 11), and CENTCOM all explicitly confirmed no US troops in Gaza — only in Kiryat Gat, Israel. This is consistent with the resolution criteria exclusion. (4) The resolution criteria is broad — 'foreign troops, including US and other international forces' — and multiple credible sources describe the Egyptian team as including military specialists. The question of whether rescue/engineering military personnel constitute 'troops' for this resolution is potentially ambiguous, but the weight of evidence supports treating Egyptian military specialists entering Gaza as qualifying.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The evidence strongly supports a Yes resolution. Egyptian forces — described by multiple credible sources including The Times of Israel ('Egyptian military forces'), TASS ('Egyptian rescuers and military specialists,' 'Egyptian field engineers' in 'mine-clearing operations'), AFP (citing 'Egyptian military sources'), and others — physically entered the terrestrial territory of Gaza on October 25-26, 2025, within the resolution window. This was confirmed by Israeli officials (Netanyahu personally approved the entry), multiple Egyptian military sources, and AFP footage. While some sources describe the team as 'technical' or 'non-military' in nature, the weight of credible evidence from sources like Times of Israel and TASS indicates the team included military specialists. The resolution criteria asks for 'foreign troops, including US and other international forces' — Egyptian military specialists conducting mine-clearing operations and hostage body recovery in Gaza qualify as such. The event occurred within the resolution window (Oct 25-26, 2025), and US forces confirmed they did not enter Gaza (at Kiryat Gat only), which is consistent with the exclusion in the criteria.

evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: There is no qualifying occurrence (EO or bill signing into law) within the October 1–31 window. The EO was signed before the window, and the bill introduced in October was not signed into law.

question: Will Tesla launch a driverless Robotaxi service in 2025?

evidence.step4_criteria_matching: The resolution criteria require Tesla to 'announce a public launch date for its Robotaxi service in the San Francisco Bay Area.' evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event (announcement of a public launch date for Bay Area Robotaxi) was found within the window, so the first-occurrence check is moot. The Bay Area service had already been operating since July 31, 2025.

evidence.step8_final_decision: The question asks whether Tesla ANNOUNCED A PUBLIC LAUNCH DATE for its Bay Area Robotaxi service between Sep 1–8, 2025. question: Will there be no US government shutdown by January 31 and will the Republican Party win the House in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve according to the combined outcome of whether there will be another US government shutdown by January 31 (https://polymarket.com/event/will-there-be-another-us-government-shutdown-by-january-31?) and according to which party will win the House in 2026 (https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-house-in-2026?).

The rules and resolution criteria are as follows:

1. Will there be another US government shutdown by January 31?
This market will resolve according to whether the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) announces another federal government shutdown due to a lapse in appropriations by January 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

Partial shutdowns count as shutdowns; announcements of office closures due to holidays or inclement weather do not qualify as a shutdown.

The resolution source for this market will be OPM’s Operating Status page (https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/snow-dismissal-procedures/current-status/).

2. Which party will win the House in 2026?
This market will resolve according to the party that controls the House of Representatives following the 2026 U.S. House elections scheduled for November 3, 2026.

House control is defined as having more than half of the voting members of the U.S. House of Representatives.

If the outcome of this election is ambiguous given the above rules, this market will remain open until the Speaker of the House is selected following the 2026 U.S. general election, at which point it will resolve to the party the Speaker is affiliated with at the time of their election to that position. If the elected Speaker does not caucus with any listed party this market will resolve “Other”.

Determination of which party controls the House after the 2026 U.S. House elections will be based on a consensus of credible reporting, or if there is ambiguity, final federal and/or state election authority certification or other final official determination of the 2026 election results.

subquestions.question: Will the Republican Party pass a government spending bill that includes at least $1 billion in earmarks for rural infrastructure projects before 2026-01-25?

If the Republican Party is unable to pass a spending bill that includes earmarks, it could indicate a lack of support for rural infrastructure projects, which could negatively impact the Republican Party's chances in the 2026 election. Schumer (D-NY) both expressed confidence that Congress will avoid another shutdown. However, the article also states that there are still several obstacles to overcome, including Republican holds on a five-bill package covering Defense, Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, Commerce, Justice, Interior, Transportation, and Housing and Urban Development. subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the Republican Party passes a government spending bill that includes at least $1 billion in earmarks for rural infrastructure projects between 2026-01-09 and 2026-01-25. subquestions.rationale: This question is relevant to the ultimate question because it could indicate the level of support for rural infrastructure projects within the Republican Party. If the Republican Party is unable to pass a spending bill that includes earmarks for rural infrastructure projects, it could negatively impact the party's chances in the 2026 election.

evidence.step1_decompose: Exact condition: A spending bill passed by Republicans between 2026-01-09 and 2026-01-25 (inclusive) that explicitly includes at least $1 billion in earmarks specifically designated for rural infrastructure projects. Observable evidence: bill text from congress.gov showing this specific category. Key entities: Republican Party (majority in Congress), U.S. Congress, spending bill. Threshold: ≥$1 billion in earmarks for rural infrastructure. Timing: 2026-01-09 to 2026-01-25.
evidence.step2_search_queries: Query 1: 'Republican government spending bill earmarks rural infrastructure 2026' (Jan 9-25) – to find whether bills with rural infrastructure earmarks passed. Query 2: 'Congress spending bill passed January 2026' (Jan 9-25) – to identify what bills passed. Query 3: 'spending bill earmarks rural infrastructure $1 billion January 2026 Congress' – to find specific dollar amounts. Query 4: 'Ralph Norman amendment block earmarks community funding projects spending bill 2026' – to understand earmark amounts and context. Query 5: 'fiscal 2026 appropriations bill rural water sanitation infrastructure earmarks total amount' – for total rural infrastructure earmark amounts. Query 6: 'spending bill signed law January 2026 Trump earmarks rural' – to find if signed into law.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Candidate events: (1) House passed 3-bill package Jan 9 (~$215B, bipartisan 397-28), with some rural water earmarks mentioned. (2) Senate passed 3-bill package Jan 15 (82-15, $180B), sent to Trump for signature – includes interior/energy/water provisions and specific rural water earmarks (SD: Oglala Sioux $8.9M, Cheyenne River $6.6M, WINS $20.3M, Mni Wiconi $17.5M). (3) House passed final $1.25T package Jan 22-23, but Senate vote was expected 'next week' (after Jan 25). No evidence any single bill had ≥$1B specifically in 'rural infrastructure earmarks.' Earmarks mentioned are in millions range; total earmarks across bills are described as $1.3-1.4B but not disaggregated as 'rural infrastructure.' The Jan 15 Senate package included some rural infrastructure earmarks but the totals cited are well below $1B (SD alone was $42M). The $1.3-1.4B figure in the Ralph Norman amendment discussion referred to all Senate earmarks in the Labor-HHS bill, not rural infrastructure specifically.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No article explicitly states any bill passed within the window included at least $1 billion in earmarks specifically designated for 'rural infrastructure projects.' The South Dakota article [South Dakota Searchlight](https://southdakotasearchlight.com/briefs/congressional-spending-bills-include-42-million-earmarked-for-south-dakota-projects-rounds-says/) shows $42M for SD rural projects from one state alone, suggesting the total across all states may be higher, but no source quantifies the total as ≥$1B for rural infrastructure specifically. The Townhall article notes earmarks for water infrastructure in small towns but totals from mentioned senators are well below $1B. The Norman amendment sought to strip $1.3-1.4B in ALL Senate earmarks (not rural infrastructure specifically). The resolution requires explicit evidence of $1B in rural infrastructure earmarks in a single passed bill — this is not confirmed. Furthermore, the largest package ($1.25T with the final 4 bills) had only passed the House by Jan 23; the Senate vote was scheduled for 'next week' (after Jan 25). The bills signed into law by Jan 25 were the first two minibus packages, but no evidence confirms their rural infrastructure earmarks totaled ≥$1B.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The Jan 9 House package passed and was sent to Senate (82-15 Senate vote Jan 15, signed into law ~Jan 16). The $1.25T final package passed House Jan 22-23; Senate vote was after Jan 25 (scheduled for week of Jan 26-30). No exact timestamp of a bill being signed/enacted that contained ≥$1B in rural infrastructure earmarks found.
evidence.step6_first_occurrence_check: No qualifying event found — no explicit evidence of a bill passing (through both chambers and signed) with ≥$1B specifically in rural infrastructure earmarks within the window.
evidence.step7_verification: The spending bills passed are bipartisan (not exclusively Republican), though Republicans hold the majority. The earmarks discussed in the context of passed bills are in the millions per project, not aggregated as ≥$1B for rural infrastructure. Ralph Norman's amendment to strip ~$1.4B in ALL earmarks (not just rural infrastructure) from the Labor-HHS bill was defeated, meaning those earmarks remain — but they span urban and rural and diverse categories. The $1.25T final bill package had NOT been fully enacted by Jan 25 (Senate vote pending). No source explicitly confirms $1B+ in rural infrastructure earmarks specifically in any single passed bill.
evidence.step8_final_decision: Resolution is No. The condition was not met within the window because: (1) No spending bill with ≥$1B explicitly in rural infrastructure earmarks was identified as passed by both chambers AND signed by the President within Jan 9-25. (2) The largest final package ($1.25T) only passed the House by Jan 23; Senate action was scheduled after Jan 25. (3) Earlier bills (Jan 9-15 packages) contained rural infrastructure earmarks in the millions per project, with no explicit total reaching $1B for rural infrastructure specifically. The window closed on Jan 25 without the condition being definitively met.

subquestions.question: Will the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) revise the second estimate of Q3 2025 GDP upwards by at least 0.5 percentage points compared to the preliminary estimate?
subquestions.background_information:
The BEA has a history of revising GDP estimates upwards. For example, in Q2 2025, the preliminary estimate was revised up by 0.3 percentage points to 3.3% (Source: [1]). Similarly, in Q2 2025, the final estimate was revised up by 0.8 percentage points to 3.8% (Source: [2]). A revision of at least 0.5 percentage points would indicate a strong economic growth in Q3 2025. Currently, the BEA releases preliminary and final estimates of GDP for each quarter, with the preliminary estimate typically released about 30 days after the end of the quarter and the final estimate released about 60 days after the end of the quarter. The second estimate is typically released about 45 days after the preliminary estimate. Sources:

1. Second-Quarter 2025 Preliminary GDP Revised Up To 3.3 Percent (2025-08-28, TalkMarkets) https://www.talkmarkets.com/content/special-reports/economy/second-quarter-2025-preliminary-gdp-revised-up-to-3-3-percent

2. Second Quarter GDP Revised Up – Again – to Best Quarter Since 2023 (2025-09-25, newsbusters.org) https://www.newsbusters.org/blogs/business/julia-seelye/2025/09/25/second-quarter-gdp-revised-up-again-best-quarter-2023
subquestions.resolution_criteria: This question resolves Yes if the second estimate of Q3 2025 GDP, scheduled for release by the BEA on [date], reports a growth rate at least 0.5 percentage points higher than the preliminary estimate. Otherwise, this question resolves No. The BEA's second estimate of Q3 2025 GDP will be available at: https://www.bea.gov/data/gdp/gross-domestic-product. Only the first available GDP report labeled as the 'Second Estimate' will be used for resolution. Any subsequent revisions or updates to the data will not be considered.
subquestions.rationale: A revision of at least 0.5 percentage points in the second estimate of Q3 2025 GDP would indicate a strong economic growth, which could be an indicator of negative GDP growth in Q4 2025 being unlikely.

evidence.step1_decompose: Condition for Yes: BEA releases the 'Second Estimate' of Q3 2025 GDP between 2025-10-30 and 2025-11-15, showing growth rate at least 0.5 percentage points higher than the preliminary estimate. Key entities: BEA, Q3 2025 GDP, preliminary estimate (advance estimate), second estimate. Threshold: ≥0.5 percentage point upward revision. Timing: Must occur within resolution window.
evidence.step2_search_queries: 1) 'BEA Q3 2025 GDP second estimate revision' (2025-10-01 to 2025-11-15) - to find if second estimate was released; 2) 'Bureau of Economic Analysis GDP third quarter 2025 preliminary estimate' (2025-10-01 to 2025-11-15) - to find preliminary estimate; 3) 'BEA GDP Q3 2025 preliminary report release government shutdown delay' (2025-10-30 to 2025-11-15) - to find shutdown impact; 4) 'US GDP third quarter 2025 advance estimate BEA release November' (2025-10-30 to 2025-11-15) - to find release timing; 5) 'BEA GDP Q3 2025 advance estimate released after shutdown November' (2025-11-12 to 2025-11-30) - to find post-shutdown release; 6) 'US GDP third quarter 2025 official release BEA November December' (2025-11-12 to 2025-12-15) - to find scheduled releases.
evidence.step3_event_detection: Key findings: (1) U.S. government shutdown started October 1, 2025, preventing BEA from releasing Q3 2025 GDP advance/preliminary estimate scheduled for October 30, 2025. (2) Shutdown ended November 12, 2025 (43 days). (3) BEA canceled the advance estimate of Q3 2025 GDP entirely - announced November 24, 2025. (4) The first official Q3 2025 GDP release was rescheduled to December 23, 2025. (5) As of November 14, 2025 (within resolution window), no preliminary or second estimate had been released. No qualifying events detected within the resolution window.
evidence.step4_criteria_matching: No preliminary estimate was released during or before the resolution window. No second estimate was released during the window. Multiple sources confirm: [CalculatedRisk, Nov 14](http://www.calculatedriskblog.com/2025/11/q3-gdp-tracking-missing-data.html) confirms 'no updates due to the ongoing government shutdown' as of Nov 14; [AFP, Oct 30](http://doc.afp.com/82EH89F) confirms GDP release delayed; [Quartz, Nov 11](https://qz.com/government-shutdown-economic-data-blackout-ending) confirms GDP was delayed with release estimated two weeks after reopening (which would be ~Nov 26, outside window); [Market Screener, Nov 24](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/u-s-to-skip-publication-of-initial-3q-gdp-estimate-ce7d5eddd989f72c) confirms BEA would skip initial estimate entirely; [Benzinga, Nov 25](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/economic-data/25/11/49052041/us-commerce-department-pushes-q3-gdp-estimate-to-just-before-christmas-stirring-political-jabs) confirms first release scheduled for December 23. Resolution criteria cannot be met: there was no 'preliminary estimate' to compare to, and no 'second estimate' was released within the window.
evidence.step5_timestamp_extraction: The condition became definitively impossible at the start of the resolution window (October 30, 2025) when the BEA failed to release the Q3 2025 advance GDP estimate as scheduled due to the government shutdown. By November 14 (within window), this was explicitly confirmed. The window closed on November 15, 2025 without any GDP estimates released.
evidence.step7_verification: Attempted to find any alternative GDP estimate release that might qualify. No BEA-labeled 'Second Estimate' of Q3 2025 GDP was released during the window. The government shutdown prevented even the preliminary (advance) estimate from being released. The first official release was eventually rescheduled to December 23, 2025 - well outside the November 15 window. Multiple high-quality sources (AFP, Market Screener, Quartz, Benzinga, CalculatedRisk) consistently confirm this. No contradictory evidence found.
evidence.step8_final_decision: The question resolves No. The BEA did not release either the preliminary (advance) estimate or the second estimate of Q3 2025 GDP during the resolution window (October 30 - November 15, 2025). The government shutdown prevented the advance estimate (scheduled October 30) from being released, and the shutdown ended November 12, 2025. Even after the shutdown ended, the BEA confirmed it would skip the advance estimate entirely, with the first official Q3 2025 GDP release scheduled for December 23, 2025. Since no preliminary estimate was released, there is nothing for the second estimate to compare against, and no second estimate was released during the window either. The condition for 'Yes' is definitively impossible to satisfy within the window.
